## Control / Coordination / Centralization

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_control_plane["Control Plane"]
    n_orchestration["Orchestration"]
    n_centralized_configuration["Centralized Configuration"]
    n_centralized_authentication["Centralized Authentication"]
    n_centralized_logging["Centralized Logging"]
    n_decentralization["Decentralization"]
    n_leader_election["Leader Election"]
    n_consensus["Consensus"]
    n_choreography["Choreography"]
    n_control_plane --> n_orchestration
    n_orchestration --> n_control_plane
    n_leader_election --> n_consensus
    n_leader_election --> n_control_plane
    n_choreography --> n_decentralization
```

### Control Plane

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Control / Coordination / Centralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-control-coordination-centralization)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: platform, infrastructure, distributed system
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
Descriptive data about the desired state of a distributed runtime, held in one place and applied to every node through a management interface.

Requires
[Management API](LEXICON.md#lexicon-management-api), [Policy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-policy)

Reinforces
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Orchestration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-orchestration)

Enables
[Centralized Control of Distributed Runtime](LEXICON.md#lexicon-centralized-control-of-distributed-runtime)

In tension with
[Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability)

Conflicts with
[Fully Decentralized Control](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fully-decentralized-control)

Referenced by
[Orchestration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-orchestration), [Leader Election](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-leader-election)

Contracts
[Control Plane](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-control-plane)

Tensions
[Control Plane / Availability](SCHEMA.md#tension-availability-control-plane)

Violated by
[Scattered Configuration](LEXICON.md#lexicon-scattered-configuration)

Detected by
manual node/service control

Measured by
control coverage, control-plane availability

Refactored by
[Management API](LEXICON.md#lexicon-management-api), [Policy as Code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-policy-as-code)

Enforced by
platform architecture

Before

```typescript
for (const node of fooNodes) {
  node.configure({ retries: 3, timeoutMs: 500 });
}
```

After

```typescript
controlPlane.apply("foo-service", {
  retries: 3,
  timeoutMs: 500,
  rollout: "progressive",
});
```

How it is checked

Checked by
platform architecture

Population
Every node, service and workflow step that shares configuration, identity, logs, leadership or agreement

Freshness
A verdict stands until membership, topology or the coordinating policy changes

Refusal
The workflow test or the platform policy rejects a participant that bypasses the coordinator or the agreed value

Observation
The control plane's recorded state compared with each participant's reported state

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The control plane's recorded state, which each participant's reported state is compared against

[Management API](LEXICON.md#lexicon-management-api), [Policy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-policy), [Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Orchestration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-orchestration), [Centralized Control of Distributed Runtime](LEXICON.md#lexicon-centralized-control-of-distributed-runtime)

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

```typescript
await fooService.create(foo);
await barService.create(bar);
await bazService.create(baz);
```

After

```typescript
await orchestrator.run("CreateFooFlow", {
  steps: [
    step("foo", () => fooService.create(foo)),
    step("bar", () => barService.create(bar)),
    step("baz", () => bazService.create(baz)),
  ],
});
```

### Centralized Configuration

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that keeps every service's configuration in one versioned store the services read from.

Requires
[Config Store](LEXICON.md#lexicon-config-store), [Access Control](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-access-control)

Reinforces

Measured by

[Schema Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-schema-validation)

Before

```typescript

const barConfig = loadLocalBarConfig();
const bazConfig = loadLocalBazConfig();
```

After

```typescript
barApp.apply(config.bar);
bazApp.apply(config.baz);
```

### Leader Election

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Control / Coordination / Centralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-control-coordination-centralization)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: distributed systems
- Scope: distributed system, coordination, availability
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets a group of nodes agree on one coordinator and replace it when it fails.

Requires
[Consensus](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consensus)

Reinforces
[Control Plane](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-control-plane), [Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance)

Enables
[Single-Writer Coordination](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-writer-coordination), [Automatic Failover of Leadership](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automatic-failover-of-leadership)

In tension with
[Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability)

Conflicts with
[Split-Brain Coordination](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-brain-coordination)

Tensions
[Leader Election / Availability](SCHEMA.md#tension-availability-leader-election)

Violated by
[Split-Brain Coordination](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-brain-coordination)

Detected by

Measured by
split-brain incident rate

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
distributed-systems review

Before

```typescript
if (process.env.IS_LEADER === "true") runFooScheduler();
```

After

```typescript
const lease = await fooCoordinator.acquireLeadership("foo-scheduler", {
  ttlMs: 10_000,
});
lease.onAcquired(() => runFooScheduler());
lease.onLost(() => stopFooScheduler());
```

### Consensus

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Control / Coordination / Centralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-control-coordination-centralization)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: distributed systems
- Scope: distributed system, agreement, consistency
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets a quorum of nodes commit one value, so every correct node ends up with the same value.

Requires
[Quorum](LEXICON.md#lexicon-quorum)

Reinforces
[Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance)

Enables
[Agreed Single Value Across Nodes](LEXICON.md#lexicon-agreed-single-value-across-nodes)

In tension with
[Latency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-latency), [Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability)

Conflicts with
[Independent Node Decisions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-independent-node-decisions)

Referenced by
[Total-Order Broadcast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-total-order-broadcast), [Leader Election](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-leader-election)

Tensions
[Consensus / Latency](SCHEMA.md#tension-consensus-latency), [Consensus / Availability](SCHEMA.md#tension-availability-consensus)

Distinct from
[Leader Election](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-leader-election): Consensus commits one value across a quorum, while leader election uses it to agree on one coordinator and replace it when it fails.

Distinct from
[Total-Order Broadcast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-total-order-broadcast): Consensus agrees on one value, while total-order broadcast agrees on the order of every message.

Violated by
[Independent Node Decisions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-independent-node-decisions)

Detected by
divergent committed state across replicas

Measured by
agreement-violation rate

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
distributed-systems review

Before

```typescript
fooNodeA.setValue(value);
```

After

```typescript
const committed = await fooCluster.propose(value, {
  quorum: majority(fooNodes),
});
if (!committed.accepted) throw new NoQuorumError();
```

## Correctness / Determinism / Verification

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

```mermaid
    n_predictability["Predictability"]

    n_verification --> n_correctness
```

### Determinism

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Correctness / Determinism / Verification](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-correctness-determinism-verification)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: function, process, build, test
- Layer: [Computation Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-computation-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that the same inputs and state always produce the same result, with time and randomness passed in as inputs.

Requires
[Controlled State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controlled-state), [Controlled State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controlled-state)

Reinforces
[Predictability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-predictability), [Reproducibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reproducibility)

Enables
[Reliable Testing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reliable-testing)

In tension with
[Runtime Adaptivity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-runtime-adaptivity)

Conflicts with
[Hidden Time/Randomness/Global State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-time-randomness-global-state)

Referenced by
[Predictability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-predictability), [Referential Transparency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-referential-transparency), [Pure Functions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-pure-functions), [Reproducibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reproducibility), [Artificial Intelligence Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-artificial-intelligence-architecture), [Agentic Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-agentic-architecture), [Write Scope and Read Population](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-write-scope-and-read-population), [One-Sided Liveness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-one-sided-liveness), [Declare-Before-Read Order](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declare-before-read-order), [Derived Party Count](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-derived-party-count), [Externally Resolved Slot](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-externally-resolved-slot)

Contracts
[Computation Core](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-computation-core)

Tensions
[Determinism / Runtime Adaptivity](SCHEMA.md#tension-determinism-runtime-adaptivity)

Distinct from
[Referential Transparency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-referential-transparency): Determinism is the same inputs giving the same result, while referential transparency is being able to replace an expression by its value.

Violated by
[Hidden Time/Randomness/Global State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-time-randomness-global-state)

Detected by
flaky tests, hidden random/time calls

Measured by
flake rate, reproducibility score

Refactored by
[Inject Clock and Randomness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-inject-clock-and-randomness), [Encapsulate State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-encapsulate-state)

Enforced by
deterministic test rules

Before

```typescript
function makeFoo(name: string) {
  return { id: crypto.randomUUID(), name, createdAt: new Date() };
}
```

After

```typescript
function makeFoo(name: string, id: FooId, createdAt: Date): Foo {
  return { id, name, createdAt };
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
deterministic test rules

Population
Every function, build and test run whose result the verification claims to hold

Freshness
A verdict stands for the code, inputs and dependency versions it ran against, and goes stale when any of them changes

Refusal
The failing test, proof or analyzer finding fails the gate

Observation
Test, proof and analyzer results, plus reruns that show whether a result repeats

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The specification the test or proof encodes, which a result is compared against

Depends on
[Controlled State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controlled-state), [Controlled State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controlled-state), [Predictability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-predictability), [Reproducibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reproducibility), [Reliable Testing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reliable-testing)

Shape it refuses
[Hidden Time/Randomness/Global State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-time-randomness-global-state)

[Maintainability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-maintainability): Predictability is foreseeing behavior, while maintainability is the ease of changing it.

Distinct from
[Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security): Predictability is foreseeable behavior, while security is protection from misuse.

[Startup Cost](LEXICON.md#lexicon-startup-cost): Predictability is foreseeable behavior, while startup cost is the time discovery adds at initialization.

[Repeatability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-repeatability): Predictability is foreseeing an outcome from the contract, while repeatability is rerunning and observing the same outcome.

[Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility): Predictability is fixed, foreseeable behavior, while runtime extensibility is adding capability to a running system.

[Thread Safety](LEXICON.md#lexicon-thread-safety): Predictability is foreseeing behavior from a contract, while thread safety is data surviving concurrent access uncorrupted.

### Referential Transparency

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)

Details

Definition

Before

```typescript
function fooTotal(values: number[]) {
  globalCounter += 1;
  return values.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) + globalCounter;
}
```

After

```typescript
function fooTotal(values: readonly number[]) {
  return values.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);

}
```

After

```typescript
type Foo = Readonly<{ name: string; tags: readonly string[] }>;

  return { ...foo, tags: [...foo.tags, tag] };
}
```

Before

```typescript
function averageFoo(total: number, count: number) {
  return total / count;
}
```

After

```typescript
function averageFoo(total: number, count: number) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(total)) throw new Error("invalid total");
  if (!Number.isInteger(count) || count <= 0) throw new Error("invalid count");
  return total / count;
}
```

Definition
The activity of proving, against a formal specification, that an algorithm or protocol keeps its invariants for every input.

Requires
[Formal Specification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-formal-specification)

Reinforces
[Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness)

Enables
[Mathematical Assurance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mathematical-assurance)

In tension with
[Cost/Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cost-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Informal Validation Only](LEXICON.md#lexicon-informal-validation-only)

Tensions
[Formal Verification / Cost/Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-cost-complexity-formal-verification)

Violated by
[Informal Validation Only](LEXICON.md#lexicon-informal-validation-only)

Detected by
missing formal model for critical invariant

Measured by
proven property coverage

Refactored by
[Formal Model](LEXICON.md#lexicon-formal-model)

Enforced by
proof tooling

Before

```typescript
function transferFoo(a: FooBalance, b: FooBalance, amount: number) {
  a.value -= amount;
  b.value += amount;
}
```

After

```typescript
function transferFoo(state: FooState, amount: PositiveAmount): FooState {
  requires(state.from >= amount.value);
  const next = { from: state.from - amount.value, to: state.to + amount.value };
  ensures(next.from + next.to === state.from + state.to);
  return next;
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
proof tooling

Population
Every function, build and test run whose result the verification claims to hold

Freshness
A verdict stands for the code, inputs and dependency versions it ran against, and goes stale when any of them changes

Refusal
The failing test, proof or analyzer finding fails the gate

Observation
Test, proof and analyzer results, plus reruns that show whether a result repeats

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The specification the test or proof encodes, which a result is compared against

Depends on
[Formal Specification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-formal-specification), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [Mathematical Assurance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mathematical-assurance)

Shape it refuses
[Informal Validation Only](LEXICON.md#lexicon-informal-validation-only)

```typescript
await fooStore.save(foo);
return { ok: true };
```

After

```typescript
await fooStore.save(foo);

if (!persisted || persisted.version !== foo.version)
  throw new Error("verification failed");
return { ok: true } as const;
```

## Portability / Infrastructure / Deployment

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_portability["Portability"]
    n_platform_independence["Platform Independence"]
    n_environment_parity["Environment Parity"]
    n_containerization["Containerization"]
    n_infrastructure_as_code["Infrastructure as Code"]
    n_standards_compliance["Standards Compliance"]
    n_protocol_independence["Protocol Independence"]
    n_configuration_externalization["Configuration Externalization"]
    n_immutable_infrastructure["Immutable Infrastructure"]
    n_platform_independence --> n_portability
    n_environment_parity --> n_configuration_externalization
    n_environment_parity --> n_infrastructure_as_code
    n_containerization --> n_portability
    n_containerization --> n_environment_parity
    n_protocol_independence --> n_portability
    n_configuration_externalization --> n_portability
    n_configuration_externalization --> n_environment_parity
    n_immutable_infrastructure --> n_infrastructure_as_code
    n_immutable_infrastructure --> n_environment_parity
```

### Platform Independence

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)

[Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability)

Enables
[Cross-Platform Deployment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cross-platform-deployment)

In tension with
[Native Optimization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-native-optimization)

Conflicts with
[OS/Vendor Lock-In](LEXICON.md#lexicon-os-vendor-lock-in)

Tensions
[Platform Independence / Native Optimization](SCHEMA.md#tension-native-optimization-platform-independence)

Violated by
[OS/Vendor Lock-In](LEXICON.md#lexicon-os-vendor-lock-in)

Detected by
OS-specific paths/APIs in portable layers

Measured by
cross-platform test pass rate

Refactored by
[Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port), [Canonicalization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-canonicalization)

Enforced by
cross-platform CI

Before

```typescript
function saveFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return winRegistry.write("Foo", foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooPersistence {
  save(foo: Foo): Promise<void>;
}
function saveFoo(foo: Foo, persistence: FooPersistence) {
  return persistence.save(foo);
}
```

### Environment Parity

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Portability / Infrastructure / Deployment](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-portability-infrastructure-deployment)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: dev, test, staging, production
- Layer: [Resource Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-resource-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that development, test, staging and production run the same build, differing only in configuration.

Requires
[Configuration Externalization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-configuration-externalization), [Infrastructure as Code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-infrastructure-as-code)

Reinforces
[Reproducibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reproducibility)

Enables
[Reliable Deployment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reliable-deployment)

In tension with
[Cost](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cost)

Conflicts with
[Snowflake Environments](LEXICON.md#lexicon-snowflake-environments)

Referenced by
[Containerization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-containerization), [Configuration Externalization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-configuration-externalization), [Immutable Infrastructure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-immutable-infrastructure)

Tensions
[Environment Parity / Cost](SCHEMA.md#tension-cost-environment-parity)

Distinct from
[Configuration Externalization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-configuration-externalization): Environment parity runs the same build everywhere, while configuration externalization is how the differences are kept outside that build.

Violated by
[Snowflake Environments](LEXICON.md#lexicon-snowflake-environments)

Detected by
works-in-dev-only defects

Measured by
[environment drift](LEXICON.md#lexicon-environment-drift)

Refactored by
[Containerization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-containerization), [Externalize Configuration](LEXICON.md#lexicon-externalize-configuration), [Infrastructure as Code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-infrastructure-as-code)

Enforced by
environment drift checks

Before

```typescript
if (env === "dev") useMemoryFooStore();
if (env === "prod") useSqlFooStore();
```

After

```typescript
const container = buildFooImage("foo-app:1.0.0");
runEnvironment("dev", container, devConfig);
runEnvironment("prod", container, prodConfig);
```

environment drift checks

```typescript
});
```

### Standards Compliance

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Portability / Infrastructure / Deployment](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-portability-infrastructure-deployment)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: protocol, security, data, infrastructure
- Layer: [Resource Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-resource-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that an implementation conforms to the published standard for its protocol, format or domain.

Requires
[Applicable Standard](LEXICON.md#lexicon-applicable-standard)

Reinforces
[Interoperability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interoperability), [Compliance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compliance)

[Proprietary Deviation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-proprietary-deviation)

Tensions
[Standards Compliance / Innovation/Flexibility](SCHEMA.md#tension-innovation-flexibility-standards-compliance)

Distinct from
[Compliance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compliance): Standards compliance is technical conformance to a published protocol or format, while compliance is implementing and evidencing the controls a regulation requires.

Distinct from
[Applicable Standard](LEXICON.md#lexicon-applicable-standard): Standards compliance is conforming, while the applicable standard is the one standard identified to conform to.

Violated by
[Proprietary Deviation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-proprietary-deviation)

Detected by
conformance test failure

Measured by
standard compliance score

Refactored by
[Contract Testing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-contract-testing)

Enforced by
standards checks

```typescript
const payload = encodePrivateFooBinary(foo);
```

After

```typescript
const payload: JsonFooV1 = toJsonFoo(foo);
http.send(JSON.stringify(payload), {
  contentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8",
});
```

standards checks

### Protocol Independence

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Portability / Infrastructure / Deployment](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-portability-infrastructure-deployment)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: integration, service boundary
- Layer: [Resource Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-resource-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that domain logic is written against ports, and each transport protocol reaches it through its own adapter.

Requires
[Adapter/Port Abstraction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adapter-port-abstraction)

Reinforces
[Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability)

Enables
[Protocol Swap](LEXICON.md#lexicon-protocol-swap)

In tension with
[Protocol-Specific Features](LEXICON.md#lexicon-protocol-specific-features)

Conflicts with
[Protocol-Coupled Domain Logic](LEXICON.md#lexicon-protocol-coupled-domain-logic)

Tensions
[Protocol Independence / Protocol-Specific Features](SCHEMA.md#tension-protocol-independence-protocol-specific-features)

Violated by
[Protocol-Coupled Domain Logic](LEXICON.md#lexicon-protocol-coupled-domain-logic)

Detected by
protocol imports in core layer

Measured by
protocol leakage count

Refactored by
[Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port), [Extract Adapter](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-adapter)

Enforced by
import rules

Before

```typescript
class FooService {
  handleHttp(request: HttpRequest) {
    return fooStore.save(request.body);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class CreateFoo {
  constructor(private readonly store: FooStore) {}
  execute(input: CreateFooInput) {
    return this.store.save(Foo.create(input));
  }
}
httpAdapter.bind(createFoo);
grpcAdapter.bind(createFoo);
```

How it is checked

Checked by
import rules

Every platform call, environment, configuration value and infrastructure resource the deployment uses

Freshness
A verdict stands until the code, the image, the configuration or the live infrastructure changes

Refusal

Platform imports read from source, and the declared infrastructure compared with the live state

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared infrastructure, which the live state is compared against

[Adapter/Port Abstraction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adapter-port-abstraction), [Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Protocol Swap](LEXICON.md#lexicon-protocol-swap)

Violated by
[Hardcoded Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-hardcoded-configuration)

Detected by

Measured by
externalized config coverage

Refactored by

```typescript
const config = {
  fooUrl: "https://foo.prod.example",
  retries: 3,

```

After

```typescript
type FooConfig = Readonly<{ fooUrl: URL; retries: number }>;
const config = FooConfigSchema.parse({
  fooUrl: process.env.FOO_URL,
  retries: process.env.FOO_RETRIES,
});
```

### Immutable Infrastructure

## Core Modular Design

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

```mermaid
    n_separation_of_concerns["Separation of Concerns"]

    n_low_coupling["Low Coupling"]

    n_high_cohesion --> n_single_responsibility
```

### Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Core Modular Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-core-modular-design)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: class, module, service
- Aliases: SRP, Single Responsibility Principle
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a class or module has one reason to change, because it serves one responsibility.

Requires
[High Cohesion](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-high-cohesion), [Explicit Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-boundaries)

Reinforces
[Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns), [Modularity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-modularity), [Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability)

Enables
[Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Reusability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reusability)

In tension with
[Excessive Fragmentation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-excessive-fragmentation)

Conflicts with

Before

```typescript
class FooService {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    fooDb.insert(foo);
  }
  send(foo: Foo) {

  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooRepository {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return fooDb.insert(foo);
  }
}
class FooNotifier {
  send(foo: Foo) {
    return fooMail.send(foo);
  }
}
class FooReporter {
  report(foo: Foo) {
    return `${foo.id}:${foo.name}`;
  }
}
```

### Separation of Concerns

Refused by rules

Before

```typescript
function handleFoo(request: Request) {
  const foo = JSON.parse(request.body);
  fooDb.insert(foo);
  return `<div>${foo.name}</div>`;
}
```

```typescript
function parseFoo(request: Request): Foo {
  return decodeFoo(request.body);
}
function saveFoo(foo: Foo) {

}

  return `<div>${foo.name}</div>`;
}
```

Before

```typescript
function validateFoo(foo: Foo) {
  if (!foo.name || foo.name.length > 40) throw new Error("invalid name");
}
function validateBar(bar: Bar) {
  if (!bar.name || bar.name.length > 40) throw new Error("invalid name");
}
```

After

```typescript
function validateName(name: string) {
  if (!name || name.length > 40) throw new Error("invalid name");
}
function validateFoo(foo: Foo) {
  validateName(foo.name);
}
function validateBar(bar: Bar) {
  validateName(bar.name);
}
```

```typescript
    return fooDb.insert(foo);
  }
  resizeImage(image: Image) {

  }
  parseBar(raw: string) {
    return JSON.parse(raw) as Bar;
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooRepository {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return fooDb.insert(foo);
  }

    return fooDb.delete(id);
  }
}

  resize(image: Image) {
    return image.resize(100, 100);
  }
}
class BarParser {
  parse(raw: string) {
    return JSON.parse(raw) as Bar;
  }
}
```

### Encapsulation

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)

Definition

[Explicit Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-boundaries), [Aggregate](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-aggregate), [Value Object](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-value-object), [Entity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-entity), [Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-invariant), [High Cohesion](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-high-cohesion), [Information Hiding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-information-hiding), [Introspection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-introspection), [Command Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-pattern), [Iterator Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-iterator-pattern), [Memento Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-memento-pattern), [Factory Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-factory-pattern), [Facade Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-facade-pattern), [Proxy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-proxy-pattern), [State Isolation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-state-isolation)

Distinct from
[Information Hiding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-information-hiding): Encapsulation protects state and its invariants, while information hiding keeps implementation decisions private behind an interface.

Before

```typescript
class FooCounter {
  count = 0;
}
const counter = new FooCounter();
counter.count = -100;
```

After

```typescript
class FooCounter {
  #count = 0;
  increment() {
    this.#count += 1;
  }
  value() {
    return this.#count;
  }
}
```

None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Before

```typescript
class FooStore {
  public readonly rows = new Map<string, Foo>();
}
fooStore.rows.set(foo.id, foo);
```

After

```typescript
interface FooStore {
  save(foo: Foo): void;
  find(id: string): Foo | undefined;
}
class MapFooStore implements FooStore {
  #rows = new Map<string, Foo>();
  save(foo: Foo) {
    this.#rows.set(foo.id, foo);
  }
  find(id: string) {
    return this.#rows.get(id);
  }
}
```

### Abstraction

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Core Modular Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-core-modular-design)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: class, module, service, system
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a concept is expressed by what it does for the code that uses it, and the detail of how it does it stays out of that expression.

Requires
[Stable Semantics](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stable-semantics), [Interface Definition](LEXICON.md#lexicon-interface-definition)

Reinforces
[Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability)

Enables
[Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability)

In tension with
[Simplicity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity)

Conflicts with
[Concrete Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concrete-coupling), [Middle Man](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-middle-man)

Referenced by
[Dynamic Binding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-binding), [Interface-Based Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interface-based-design), [Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability), [Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns), [Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-duplicate-code), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation), [Reusability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reusability), [Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism), [Inversion of Control (IoC)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-inversion-of-control), [Dependency Injection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-injection)

Tensions
[Abstraction / Simplicity](SCHEMA.md#tension-abstraction-simplicity)

Distinct from
[Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion): Abstraction expresses a concept by what it does, while dependency inversion fixes that the high-level policy owns that expression.

Distinct from
[Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-duplicate-code): Abstraction hides how a thing works behind what it does, while DRY keeps one source for each piece of logic.

Distinct from
[Interface-Based Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interface-based-design): Abstraction is the general rule, while interface-based design applies it to module dependencies supplied from outside.

Distinct from
[Inversion of Control (IoC)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-inversion-of-control): Abstraction hides detail, while inversion of control moves object creation and control flow to a framework or composition root.

Distinct from
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed): Abstraction hides detail, while the open/closed principle adds behavior at an extension point without editing existing code.

Distinct from
[Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns): Abstraction separates what from how, while separation of concerns separates parsing, logic, persistence and presentation.

Violated by
[Leaky Abstraction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-leaky-abstraction), [Concrete Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concrete-coupling)

Detected by
concrete type usage across boundaries

Measured by
abstraction ratio, interface stability

Refactored by
[Extract Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-interface), [Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port), [Invert Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-invert-dependency)

Enforced by
architecture tests, dependency inversion rules

Before

```typescript
function saveFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return sqlClient.query("insert into foos(id,name) values($1,$2)", [
    foo.id,
    foo.name,
  ]);
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooRepository {
  save(foo: Foo): Promise<void>;
}
class SqlFooRepository implements FooRepository {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return sqlClient.query("insert into foos(id,name) values($1,$2)", [
      foo.id,
      foo.name,
    ]);
  }
}
class HttpFooRepository implements FooRepository {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return http.post("/foos", foo);
  }
}
function saveFoo(foo: Foo, repository: FooRepository) {
  return repository.save(foo);
}
```

### Modularity

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Core Modular Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-core-modular-design)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: package, component, service, system
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a system is divided into cohesive modules with explicit boundaries and few dependencies between them.

Requires
[High Cohesion](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-high-cohesion), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Explicit Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-boundaries)

Reinforces

Enables

In tension with
[Cross-Cutting Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cross-cutting-concerns)

Conflicts with
[Big Ball of Mud](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-big-ball-of-mud)

Referenced by
[Bounded Context](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bounded-context), [Explicit Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-boundaries), [Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-responsibility), [Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns), [High Cohesion](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-high-cohesion), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Composability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composability), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture), [Component-Based Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-component-based-architecture), [Package by Feature](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-package-by-feature)

Tensions

Distinct from
[Autonomy](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-autonomy): Modularity divides a system into cohesive parts, while autonomy gives each owner its own data and decisions.

Distinct from
[Composability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composability): Modularity divides a system, while composability lets its parts combine.

Distinct from
[Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation): Modularity is division into modules, while encapsulation protects one object's state.

Distinct from
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed): Modularity divides the system, while the open/closed principle governs adding behavior at an extension point.

Distinct from
[Package by Feature](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-package-by-feature): Modularity is the rule to divide, while package by feature chooses the axis of division, the feature.

Distinct from
[Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns): Modularity divides into cohesive modules, while separation of concerns names which concerns must not share a part.

Distinct from
[Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-responsibility): Modularity is the division of a system, while single responsibility limits one class or module to one reason to change.

Violated by
[Circular Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-circular-dependency), [Shared Mutable State](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-shared-mutable-state), [Boundary Leakage](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-boundary-leakage)

Refactored by
[Split Module](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-module), [Define Module Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-define-module-boundaries), [Invert Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-invert-dependency)

Enforced by
module rules, package ownership, [fitness functions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fitness-functions)

Before

```typescript
class FooApplication {
  parse(raw: string) {
    return JSON.parse(raw) as Foo;
  }
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return fooDb.insert(foo);
  }
  publish(foo: Foo) {
    return fooBus.emit(foo);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
export const fooParser = { parse: (raw: string) => decodeFoo(raw) };
export const fooRepository = { save: (foo: Foo) => fooDb.insert(foo) };
export const fooPublisher = { publish: (foo: Foo) => fooBus.emit(foo) };
```

### Composability

Before

```typescript
function processFoo(raw: string) {
  const foo = JSON.parse(raw) as Foo;
  const normalized = { ...foo, name: foo.name.trim() };
  return fooDb.insert(normalized);
}
```

After

```typescript
const parseFoo = (raw: string): Foo => decodeFoo(raw);
const normalizeFoo = (foo: Foo): Foo => ({ ...foo, name: foo.name.trim() });
const saveFoo = (foo: Foo) => fooDb.insert(foo);
const processFoo = flow(parseFoo, normalizeFoo, saveFoo);
```

### Composition Over Inheritance

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Core Modular Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-core-modular-design)

- Aliases: Composite Reuse Principle
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that behavior is reused by holding and delegating to another object instead of extending its class.

Requires
[Delegation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-delegation), [Interface-Based Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interface-based-design)

Reinforces
[Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability)

Enables
[Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern), [Decorator Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decorator-pattern)

In tension with
[Simplicity for Trivial Reuse](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity-for-trivial-reuse)

Conflicts with

Referenced by
[Bridge Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bridge-pattern)

Tensions
[Composition Over Inheritance / Simplicity for Trivial Reuse](SCHEMA.md#tension-composition-over-inheritance-simplicity-for-trivial-reuse)

Violated by
[Deep Inheritance Hierarchy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-deep-inheritance-hierarchy), [Broken Inheritance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broken-inheritance)

Detected by

Measured by
inheritance depth, composition ratio

Refactored by
[Replace Inheritance with Delegation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-replace-inheritance-with-delegation), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern)

Enforced by
inheritance depth limits, review rules

Before

```typescript
class RetryingSqlFooStore extends SqlFooStore {
  async save(foo: Foo) {
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt += 1) {
      try {
        return await super.save(foo);
      } catch (error) {
        if (attempt === 2) throw error;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class RetryingFooStore implements FooStore {
  constructor(
    private readonly inner: FooStore,
    private readonly attempts: number,
  ) {}
  async save(foo: Foo) {
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < this.attempts; attempt += 1) {
      try {
        return await this.inner.save(foo);
      } catch (error) {
        if (attempt === this.attempts - 1) throw error;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)

Definition

[Context-Specific Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-context-specific-coupling)

Violated by

Detected by

Measured by

Refactored by
[Introduce Parameter Object](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-parameter-object), [Extract Module](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-module), [Pass Context Explicitly](LEXICON.md#lexicon-pass-context-explicitly)

Enforced by
API review, dependency rules

Before

```typescript
function saveAdminFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return adminFooDb.insert(foo);
}
function savePublicFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return publicFooDb.insert(foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
function saveFoo(store: FooStore, foo: Foo) {
  return store.save(foo);
}
const saveAdminFoo = (foo: Foo) => saveFoo(adminFooStore, foo);
const savePublicFoo = (foo: Foo) => saveFoo(publicFooStore, foo);
```

### Replaceability

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Core Modular Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-core-modular-design)

Details

Definition

In tension with
[Deep Optimization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-deep-optimization)

Conflicts with
[Concrete Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concrete-coupling)

Referenced by
[Explicit Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-boundaries), [Stable Interfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stable-interfaces), [Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability), [Protocol Independence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-protocol-independence), [Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-responsibility), [Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns), [High Cohesion](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-high-cohesion), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Information Hiding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-information-hiding), [Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Modularity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-modularity), [Composition Over Inheritance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composition-over-inheritance), [Interchangeability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interchangeability), [Adapter Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-adapter-pattern), [Dependency Injection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-injection), [Ports and Adapters Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ports-and-adapters-architecture), [Component-Based Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-component-based-architecture)

Tensions
[Replaceability / Deep Optimization](SCHEMA.md#tension-deep-optimization-replaceability)

Distinct from
[High Cohesion](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-high-cohesion): Replaceability is swapping an implementation, while high cohesion is members sharing one purpose.

Distinct from
[Interchangeability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interchangeability): Replaceability is substituting one implementation when the code changes, while interchangeability is selecting among several live implementations at runtime.

Distinct from
[Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability): Replaceability swaps one component, while portability moves the whole software to another platform.

Distinct from
[Reusability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reusability): Replaceability puts a new implementation behind the same callers, while reusability serves a new caller with the same implementation.

Distinct from
[Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability): Replaceability swaps an implementation in production, while testability supplies dependencies in a test.

Distinct from
[Stable Interfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stable-interfaces): Replaceability swaps what sits behind an interface, while stable interfaces keep the interface itself unchanged across releases.

Distinct from
[Maintainability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-maintainability): Replaceability makes one kind of change cheap, while maintainability is the ease of every kind of correction and extension.

[Vendor Lock-In Leakage](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-vendor-lock-in-leakage)

infrastructure imports in core layers

Measured by
adapter coverage, boundary purity

[Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port), [Extract Adapter](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-adapter), [Invert Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-invert-dependency)

Before

```typescript
class FooService {
  private readonly store = new SqlFooStore();
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return this.store.save(foo);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooService {
  constructor(private readonly store: FooStore) {}
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return this.store.save(foo);
  }
}
test("saves without a database", async () => {
  const store = new MemoryFooStore();
  await new FooService(store).save(foo);
  expect(store.find(foo.id)).toEqual(foo);
});
```

Before

```typescript
class FooModule {
  create(foo: Foo) {
    barModule.refresh(foo.id);
    bazModule.rebuild(foo.id);
    return fooDb.insert(foo);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooModule {
  constructor(
    private readonly store: FooStore,
    private readonly events: EventSink,
  ) {}
  async create(foo: Foo) {
    await this.store.save(foo);
    this.events.emit({ type: "FooCreated", fooId: foo.id });
  }
}
```

### Autonomy

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Core Modular Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-core-modular-design)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: service, team, bounded context
- Aliases: Service Autonomy
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a service or team owns its data and decisions, so it alone writes its data and others reach or change it only through its published API or events.

Requires
[Independence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-independence), [Own Data](LEXICON.md#lexicon-own-data), [Explicit Contracts](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-contracts)

Enables
[Microservices](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-microservices), [Bounded Context Ownership](LEXICON.md#lexicon-bounded-context-ownership), [Independent Deployment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-independent-deployment)

In tension with
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Standardization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-standardization), [Global Consistency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-global-consistency)

Conflicts with
[Centralized Runtime Control](LEXICON.md#lexicon-centralized-runtime-control), [Shared Database](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-database), [Cyclic Deployment Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-cyclic-deployment-dependency)

Referenced by
[Bounded Context](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bounded-context), [Service Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-service-contract), [Decentralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decentralization), [Choreography](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-choreography), [Independence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-independence), [Microservices](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-microservices), [Service-Oriented Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-service-oriented-architecture)

Tensions
[Autonomy / Governance](SCHEMA.md#tension-autonomy-governance), [Autonomy / Standardization](SCHEMA.md#tension-autonomy-standardization), [Autonomy / Global Consistency](SCHEMA.md#tension-autonomy-global-consistency)

Distinct from
[Explicit Contracts](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-contracts): Autonomy is ownership of data and decisions, while explicit contracts are the declared boundaries others use to reach them.

Distinct from
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance): Autonomy leaves decisions with their owner, while governance holds decisions to shared policy.

Distinct from
[Standardization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-standardization): Autonomy lets each owner choose, while standardization fixes one choice everywhere.

Distinct from
[Decentralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decentralization): Autonomy is one unit owning its data and decisions, while decentralization is the system-wide placement of control with those units.

Distinct from
[Independence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-independence): Autonomy is ownership, while independence is being tested and deployed without the neighboring modules.

Violated by

Detected by

Measured by
ownership clarity, deployment independence

Refactored by
[Own Data per Service](LEXICON.md#lexicon-own-data-per-service), [Split Bounded Context](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-bounded-context), [Domain Events](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-domain-events)

Enforced by
ownership boundaries, API policies

Before

```typescript
async function createFoo(foo: Foo) {
  const bar = await barService.get(foo.barId);
  await bazService.validate(foo, bar);
  return fooStore.save(foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function createFoo(foo: Foo) {
  await fooStore.save(foo);
  await outbox.append({ type: "FooCreated", fooId: foo.id, barId: foo.barId });
}
```

## SOLID / Object-Oriented Design

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_interface_segregation["Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)"]
    n_dependency_inversion["Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)"]
    n_open_closed["Open/Closed Principle (OCP)"]
    n_liskov_substitution["Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)"]
    n_polymorphism["Polymorphism"]
    n_liskov_substitution --> n_polymorphism
    n_polymorphism --> n_open_closed
```

### Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [SOLID / Object-Oriented Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-solid-object-oriented-design)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: interface, service, module
- Aliases: ISP, Interface Segregation Principle
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a client depends on an interface holding only the methods it uses.

Requires
[Role-Specific Interfaces](LEXICON.md#lexicon-role-specific-interfaces)

Reinforces
[Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-responsibility), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling)

Enables
[Consumer-Specific Contracts](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consumer-specific-contracts)

In tension with
[Interface Proliferation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-interface-proliferation)

Conflicts with
[Fat Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fat-interface), [Repository Dump](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-repository-dump)

Tensions
[Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) / Interface Proliferation](SCHEMA.md#tension-interface-proliferation-interface-segregation-principle-isp)

Violated by
[Fat Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fat-interface)

Detected by
unused interface method implementations

Measured by
interface method usage ratio

Refactored by
[Split Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-interface), [Extract Role Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-role-interface)

Enforced by
interface usage analysis, lint rules

Before

```typescript
interface FooWorker {
  load(id: FooId): Foo;
  save(foo: Foo): void;
  delete(id: FooId): void;
  export(): string;
}
class FooReader implements FooWorker {}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooReader {
  load(id: FooId): Foo;
}
interface FooWriter {
  save(foo: Foo): void;
}
interface FooRemover {
  delete(id: FooId): void;
}
class CachedFooReader implements FooReader {
  load(id: FooId) {
    return fooCache.get(id)!;
  }
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
interface usage analysis, lint rules

Population
Every interface, class hierarchy and dependency edge in the object model

Freshness
A verdict stands until an interface, an override or a dependency changes

Refusal
The dependency rule or the contract test fails a change that breaks substitution, segregation or dependency direction

Observation
Interface usage, override contracts and dependency direction, read from source and contract tests

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The interface contract, which every implementation and override conforms to

Depends on
[Role-Specific Interfaces](LEXICON.md#lexicon-role-specific-interfaces), [Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-responsibility), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Consumer-Specific Contracts](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consumer-specific-contracts)

[Fat Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fat-interface), [Repository Dump](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-repository-dump)

- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)

- Aliases: OCP, Open-Closed Principle
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a module gains new behavior by adding code at an extension point, leaving its existing code unchanged.

Requires
[Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points)

Reinforces
[Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern)

Enables
[Feature Extension without Modification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-feature-extension-without-modification)

In tension with
[Simplicity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity)

Conflicts with
[Switch-Based Extension](LEXICON.md#lexicon-switch-based-extension)

Referenced by
[Dynamic Dispatch](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-dispatch), [Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility), [Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern), [Command Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-pattern), [State Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-state-pattern), [Chain of Responsibility Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-chain-of-responsibility-pattern), [Visitor Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-visitor-pattern), [Factory Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-factory-pattern), [Factory Method Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-factory-method-pattern), [Decorator Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decorator-pattern), [Composite Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composite-pattern), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture), [Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points)

Contracts
[Extensibility Core](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-extensibility-core)

Tensions
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP) / Simplicity](SCHEMA.md#tension-open-closed-principle-ocp-simplicity)

Distinct from
[Composability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composability): The open/closed principle adds behavior without editing existing code, while composability combines parts through compatible interfaces.

Violated by
[Switch-Based Extension](LEXICON.md#lexicon-switch-based-extension)

Detected by
growing conditionals, repeated edits to central classes

Measured by
modification frequency of core modules

Refactored by
[Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern), [Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture)

Enforced by
extension policies, change analysis

Refused by rules
open-closed

Before

```typescript
function priceFoo(kind: string, value: number) {
  if (kind === "foo") return value;
  if (kind === "bar") return value * 2;
  throw new Error("unknown kind");
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooPricing {
  price(value: number): number;
}
const registry = new Map<string, FooPricing>();
export function registerPricing(kind: string, pricing: FooPricing) {
  registry.set(kind, pricing);
}
export function priceFoo(kind: string, value: number) {
  const pricing = registry.get(kind);
  if (!pricing) throw new Error(`unknown kind ${kind}`);
  return pricing.price(value);
}
registerPricing("bar", { price: (value) => value * 2 });
```

How it is checked

Checked by
extension policies, change analysis

Population
Every interface, class hierarchy and dependency edge in the object model

Freshness
A verdict stands until an interface, an override or a dependency changes

Refusal
The dependency rule or the contract test fails a change that breaks substitution, segregation or dependency direction

Observation
Interface usage, override contracts and dependency direction, read from source and contract tests

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The interface contract, which every implementation and override conforms to

Depends on
[Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern), [Feature Extension without Modification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-feature-extension-without-modification)

Shape it refuses
[Switch-Based Extension](LEXICON.md#lexicon-switch-based-extension)

### Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [SOLID / Object-Oriented Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-solid-object-oriented-design)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: class, interface, type hierarchy
- Aliases: LSP, Liskov Substitution Principle, Behavioral Subtyping
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a subtype can replace its base type anywhere, because it keeps the base type's preconditions, postconditions and invariants.

Requires
[Contract Preservation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-contract-preservation), [Preconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-preconditions), [Postconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-postconditions), [Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-invariant)

Reinforces
[Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism), [Type Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-type-safety)

Enables
[Safe Substitution](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-substitution), [Substitutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-substitutability)

In tension with
[Narrow Specialized Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-narrow-specialized-behavior)

Conflicts with
[Broken Inheritance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broken-inheritance), [Broken Inheritance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broken-inheritance)

Referenced by
[Design by Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-design-by-contract)

Tensions
[Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) / Narrow Specialized Behavior](SCHEMA.md#tension-liskov-substitution-principle-lsp-narrow-specialized-behavior)

Violated by
[Broken Inheritance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broken-inheritance)

Detected by
overridden method contract divergence

Measured by
contract test pass rate across subtypes

Refactored by
[Replace Inheritance with Delegation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-replace-inheritance-with-delegation), [Extract Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-interface), [Split Hierarchy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-hierarchy)

Enforced by
contract tests, type tests

Before

```typescript
class FooStore {
  save(foo: Foo): Promise<Receipt> {
    return persist(foo);
  }
}
class ReadOnlyFooStore extends FooStore {
  save(): Promise<Receipt> {
    throw new Error("not supported");
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooStore {
  save(foo: Foo): Promise<Receipt> {
    return persist(foo);
  }
}
class AuditedFooStore extends FooStore {
  async save(foo: Foo): Promise<Receipt> {
    const receipt = await super.save(foo);
    audit.record(receipt);
    return receipt;
  }
}
```

Checked by
contract tests, type tests

Population
Every interface, class hierarchy and dependency edge in the object model

Freshness
A verdict stands until an interface, an override or a dependency changes

Refusal
The dependency rule or the contract test fails a change that breaks substitution, segregation or dependency direction

Observation
Interface usage, override contracts and dependency direction, read from source and contract tests

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The interface contract, which every implementation and override conforms to

Depends on
[Contract Preservation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-contract-preservation), [Preconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-preconditions), [Postconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-postconditions), [Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-invariant), [Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism), [Type Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-type-safety), [Safe Substitution](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-substitution), [Substitutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-substitutability)

[Broken Inheritance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broken-inheritance), [Broken Inheritance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broken-inheritance)

### Polymorphism

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [SOLID / Object-Oriented Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-solid-object-oriented-design)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: class, interface, runtime
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets one interface have several implementations, with the implementation chosen by the object that receives the call.

Requires
[Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Substitutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-substitutability)

Reinforces
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern)

Enables
[Dynamic Dispatch](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-dispatch), [Interchangeability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interchangeability)

In tension with
[Traceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-traceability)

Conflicts with
[Type Switching](LEXICON.md#lexicon-type-switching)

Referenced by
[Dynamic Binding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-binding), [Dynamic Dispatch](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-dispatch), [Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Interchangeability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interchangeability), [Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-liskov-substitution), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern), [State Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-state-pattern), [Null Object Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-null-object-pattern)

Tensions
[Polymorphism / Traceability](SCHEMA.md#tension-polymorphism-traceability)

Distinct from
[Dynamic Dispatch](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-dispatch): Polymorphism is one interface with several implementations, while dynamic dispatch is the runtime selection of which one runs, from the receiver or a keyed table.

Distinct from
[Type Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-type-safety): Polymorphism varies the implementation behind a type, while type safety rejects operations on the wrong type.

Violated by
[Type Switching](LEXICON.md#lexicon-type-switching)

Detected by
conditional type checks, duplicated branching

Measured by
polymorphic dispatch ratio

Refactored by
[Replace Conditional with Polymorphism](LEXICON.md#lexicon-replace-conditional-with-polymorphism)

Enforced by
[code review](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-code-review), static analysis rules

Before

```typescript
function renderFoo(kind: string, foo: Foo) {
  if (kind === "text") return foo.name;
  if (kind === "json") return JSON.stringify(foo);
  throw new Error("unknown renderer");
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooRenderer {
  render(foo: Foo): string;
}
class TextFooRenderer implements FooRenderer {
  render(foo: Foo) {
    return foo.name;
  }
}
class JsonFooRenderer implements FooRenderer {
  render(foo: Foo) {
    return JSON.stringify(foo);
  }
}
function renderFoo(renderer: FooRenderer, foo: Foo) {
  return renderer.render(foo);
}
```

Refusal
The dependency rule or the contract test fails a change that breaks substitution, segregation or dependency direction

Observation
Interface usage, override contracts and dependency direction, read from source and contract tests

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The interface contract, which every implementation and override conforms to

[Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Substitutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-substitutability), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Strategy Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-strategy-pattern), [Dynamic Dispatch](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-dispatch), [Interchangeability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interchangeability)

### Event-Driven Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: service, integration, system
- Aliases: EDA
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of connecting services through published events, with each consumer reacting independently of the producer.

Requires
[Events](LEXICON.md#lexicon-events), [Message Contract](LEXICON.md#lexicon-message-contract), [Idempotency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotency)

Reinforces
[Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Asynchronous Communication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-asynchronous-communication)

Enables
[Event Sourcing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-sourcing), [Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-query-responsibility-segregation), [Saga Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-saga-pattern)

In tension with
[Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-debuggability), [Strong Consistency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-strong-consistency)

Conflicts with
[Hidden Temporal Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-temporal-coupling)

Referenced by
[Choreography](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-choreography), [Event Bus](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-bus), [Domain Events](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-domain-events), [Asynchronous Communication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-asynchronous-communication), [Observer Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observer-pattern), [Idempotency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotency)

Tensions
[Event-Driven Architecture / Debuggability](SCHEMA.md#tension-debuggability-event-driven-architecture), [Event-Driven Architecture / Strong Consistency](SCHEMA.md#tension-event-driven-architecture-strong-consistency)

Violated by
[Non-Idempotent Operation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-non-idempotent-operation), [Ad-Hoc Payloads](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ad-hoc-payloads)

Detected by
missing correlation IDs, direct synchronous chains

Measured by
event contract coverage, [retry safety](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retry-safety)

Refactored by
[Domain Events](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-domain-events), [Outbox Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-outbox-pattern), [Consumer-Driven Contract Tests](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consumer-driven-contract-tests)

Enforced by
[schema registry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-schema-registry), idempotency tests

Before

```typescript
async function createFoo(foo: Foo) {
  await fooStore.save(foo);
  await barService.refresh(foo.id);
  await bazService.notify(foo.id);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function createFoo(foo: Foo) {
  await fooStore.save(foo);
  await events.publish({ type: "FooCreated", fooId: foo.id });
}
events.on("FooCreated", updateBarProjection);
events.on("FooCreated", notifyBaz);
```

How it is checked

Checked by
schema registry, idempotency tests

Population
Every event, message, topic and consumer that crosses an asynchronous boundary

Freshness
A verdict stands until an event schema, a consumer or the delivery guarantee changes

Refusal
The schema registry, idempotency test or workflow test fails the change that breaks delivery or contract

Observation
Published schemas, consumer registrations, and redelivery, lag and dead-letter counts from the broker

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The published schema and the delivery guarantee, which every producer and consumer conforms to

Depends on
[Events](LEXICON.md#lexicon-events), [Message Contract](LEXICON.md#lexicon-message-contract), [Idempotency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotency), [Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling), [Asynchronous Communication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-asynchronous-communication), [Event Sourcing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-sourcing), [Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-query-responsibility-segregation), [Saga Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-saga-pattern)

Shape it refuses
[Hidden Temporal Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-temporal-coupling)

### Publish/Subscribe Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: integration, eventing
- Aliases: Pub/Sub
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern in which publishers send messages to a topic and every subscriber to that topic receives them.

Requires
[Publisher](LEXICON.md#lexicon-publisher), [Subscriber](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subscriber), [Broker/Event Bus](LEXICON.md#lexicon-broker-event-bus)

Reinforces
[Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling)

Enables
[Fan-Out Notification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fan-out-notification)

In tension with
[Delivery Ordering](LEXICON.md#lexicon-delivery-ordering)

Conflicts with
[Direct Point-to-Point Calls](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-point-to-point-calls)

Referenced by
[Message Broker](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-message-broker), [Event Bus](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-bus)

Tensions
[Publish/Subscribe Pattern / Delivery Ordering](SCHEMA.md#tension-delivery-ordering-publish-subscribe-pattern)

Violated by
[Point-to-Point Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-point-to-point-coupling)

Detected by
direct calls to subscriber list

Measured by
publisher-subscriber coupling

Refactored by
[Event Bus](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-bus)

Enforced by
messaging contracts

Before

```typescript
function saveFoo(foo: Foo) {
  fooStore.save(foo);
  auditFoo(foo);
  indexFoo(foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
publisher.publish("foo.saved", { fooId: foo.id });
subscriber.on("foo.saved", auditFoo);
subscriber.on("foo.saved", indexFoo);
```

messaging contracts

None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side

### Message Queue

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: integration, async processing
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that holds messages durably until a consumer takes and acknowledges each one.

Requires
[Message Contract](LEXICON.md#lexicon-message-contract), [Consumer](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consumer)

Reinforces
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backpressure)

Enables
[Asynchronous Processing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-asynchronous-processing)

[In-Memory Direct Invocation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-in-memory-direct-invocation)

Tensions
[Message Queue / Latency](SCHEMA.md#tension-latency-message-queue)

Distinct from
[Consumer](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consumer): A message queue holds messages until they are acknowledged, while the consumer is the component that takes and processes them.

Violated by
[Missing Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-missing-backpressure)

Detected by
synchronous blocking chains for async work

Measured by
queue depth, retry/dead-letter rates

Refactored by
[Competing Consumers](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-competing-consumers)

Enforced by
infrastructure policy, load tests

Before

```typescript
for (const foo of foos) await processFoo(foo);
```

After

```typescript
for (const foo of foos) await fooQueue.enqueue({ type: "ProcessFoo", foo });
fooWorker.consume(fooQueue, (message) => processFoo(message.foo));
```

Refusal

Observation

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

The published schema and the delivery guarantee, which every producer and consumer conforms to

### Message Broker

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)

```typescript

);
broker.subscribe(
  "foo.created",
  { group: "baz-consumer", ack: "manual" },
  handleBaz,
);
```
