### Event Sourcing

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: domain, persistence
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that stores state as the sequence of events that produced it and rebuilds current state by replaying them.

Requires
[Append-Only Log](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-append-only-log), [Domain Events](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-domain-events)

Reinforces
[Auditability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auditability), [Temporal Modeling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-temporal-modeling)

Enables
[Replay](LEXICON.md#lexicon-replay), [Replay](LEXICON.md#lexicon-replay)

In tension with
[Query Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-query-complexity)

Conflicts with
[CRUD-Only State Persistence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-crud-only-state-persistence)

Referenced by
[Event-Driven Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-driven-architecture), [Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-query-responsibility-segregation), [Append-Only Log](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-append-only-log)

Tensions
[Event Sourcing / Query Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-event-sourcing-query-complexity)

Distinct from
[Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-query-responsibility-segregation): Event sourcing stores state as its events, while CQRS separates the command model from the query model whatever the storage.

Distinct from
[Append-Only Log](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-append-only-log): Event sourcing rebuilds state by replay, while an append-only log is the storage it replays from.

Distinct from
[Domain Events](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-domain-events): Event sourcing makes events the source of state, while domain events can be published with state stored some other way.

Distinct from
[Saga Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-saga-pattern): Event sourcing is how state is stored, while a saga is how a distributed transaction is coordinated.

Violated by
[CRUD-Only State Persistence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-crud-only-state-persistence)

Detected by
state changes lacking events

Measured by
event/state consistency

Refactored by
[Query Projection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-query-projection)

Enforced by
event append rules

Before

```typescript
type FooRow = { id: FooId; name: string; status: string };
await fooTable.update(foo);
```

After

```typescript
type FooEvent = FooCreated | FooRenamed | FooClosed;
await fooEventStore.append(foo.id, foo.uncommittedEvents());
const foo = fooEventStore.read(fooId).reduce(applyFooEvent, emptyFoo());
```

```typescript
  save(foo: Foo) {}
  search(query: string): Foo[] {
    return complexJoin(query);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooCommandStore {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return fooDb.write(foo);
  }
}

  search(query: string) {
    return fooReadModel.search(query);
  }
}
commandBus.execute(new SaveFoo(foo));
queryBus.execute(new SearchFoos(query));
```

### Saga Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: service workflow, distributed system
- Aliases: Saga
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that runs a cross-service transaction as a sequence of local steps, each paired with a compensating step.

Requires
[Compensating Transaction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compensating-transaction), [Idempotency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotency)

Reinforces
[Eventual Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-eventual-consistency)

Enables
[Long-Running Transactions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-long-running-transactions)

In tension with
[Workflow Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-workflow-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Global ACID Transaction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-global-acid-transaction)

Referenced by
[Orchestration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-orchestration), [Event-Driven Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-driven-architecture), [Compensating Transaction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compensating-transaction)

Tensions
[Saga Pattern / Workflow Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-saga-pattern-workflow-complexity)

Violated by
[Global ACID Transaction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-global-acid-transaction), [Hidden Distributed Transaction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-distributed-transaction)

Detected by
distributed transaction attempts

Measured by
compensation coverage

Refactored by
[Compensating Transaction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compensating-transaction)

Enforced by
workflow tests

Before

```typescript
const tx = coordinator.begin();
await fooService.prepare(tx, foo);
await barService.prepare(tx, bar);
await bazService.prepare(tx, baz);
await coordinator.commit(tx);
```

After

```typescript
await saga([
  {
    action: () => fooService.create(foo),
    compensate: (id) => fooService.cancel(id),
  },
  {
    action: () => barService.create(bar),
    compensate: (id) => barService.cancel(id),
  },
  {
    action: () => bazService.create(baz),
    compensate: (id) => bazService.cancel(id),
  },
]).run();
```

How it is checked

Checked by
workflow tests

Population
Every event, message, topic and consumer that crosses an asynchronous boundary

Freshness
A verdict stands until an event schema, a consumer or the delivery guarantee changes

Refusal
The schema registry, idempotency test or workflow test fails the change that breaks delivery or contract

Observation
Published schemas, consumer registrations, and redelivery, lag and dead-letter counts from the broker

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The published schema and the delivery guarantee, which every producer and consumer conforms to

Depends on
[Compensating Transaction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compensating-transaction), [Idempotency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotency), [Eventual Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-eventual-consistency), [Long-Running Transactions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-long-running-transactions)

Shape it refuses
[Global ACID Transaction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-global-acid-transaction)

### Outbox Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)

Details

Definition

Reinforces

Refactored by

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
await fooStore.save(foo);
await eventBus.publish({ type: "FooSaved", fooId: foo.id });
```

After

```typescript
await database.transaction(async (tx) => {
  await tx.foos.save(foo);
  await tx.outbox.insert({ id: eventId(), type: "FooSaved", fooId: foo.id });
});
await outboxRelay.publishPending();
```

### Compensating Transaction

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

Before

```typescript
await fooService.create(foo);
await barService.create(bar);
```

After

```typescript
const fooId = await fooService.create(foo);
try {
  await barService.create(bar);
} catch (error) {
  await fooService.compensateCreate(fooId);
  throw error;
}
```

### Dead-Letter Queue

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: production systems
- Scope: service, messaging, resilience
- Aliases: DLQ
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that moves a message which keeps failing into a separate queue, where it can be inspected and reprocessed.

Requires
[Message Queue](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-message-queue)

Reinforces
[Fault Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fault-isolation), [Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability)

Enables

In tension with

Conflicts with
[Infinite Redelivery Loop](LEXICON.md#lexicon-infinite-redelivery-loop)

Tensions
[Dead-Letter Queue / Operational Overhead](SCHEMA.md#tension-dead-letter-queue-operational-overhead)

Violated by
[Infinite Redelivery Loop](LEXICON.md#lexicon-infinite-redelivery-loop)

Detected by

Measured by
redelivery count per failed message

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
messaging design review

Before

```typescript
worker.consume(fooQueue, async (message) => {
  await processFoo(message);
});
```

After

```typescript
worker.consume(fooQueue, async (message) => {
  try {
    await processFoo(message);
  } catch (error) {
    if (message.attempts >= 5) return fooDeadLetterQueue.send(message, error);
    throw error;
  }
});
```

### Idempotent Consumer

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Event / Messaging / Asynchronous Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-event-messaging-asynchronous-architecture)

Definition

none

Before

```typescript
worker.consume(fooQueue, (message) => chargeFoo(message.fooId, message.amount));
```

After

```typescript
worker.consume(fooQueue, async (message) => {
  if (await processedMessages.has(message.id)) return;
  await chargeFoo(message.fooId, message.amount);
  await processedMessages.add(message.id);
});
```

## Error Handling / Resilience

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_defensive_programming["Defensive Programming"]
    n_fail_fast["Fail Fast"]
    n_fail_safe["Fail Safe"]
    n_fail_secure["Fail Secure"]
    n_graceful_degradation["Graceful Degradation"]
    n_fault_tolerance["Fault Tolerance"]
    n_resilience["Resilience"]
    n_robustness_principle["Robustness Principle"]
    n_error_handling["Error Handling"]
    n_error_boundaries["Error Boundaries"]
    n_fallback_pattern["Fallback Pattern"]
    n_retry_pattern["Retry Pattern"]
    n_timeout_pattern["Timeout Pattern"]
    n_circuit_breaker_pattern["Circuit Breaker Pattern"]
    n_bulkhead_pattern["Bulkhead Pattern"]
    n_backpressure["Backpressure"]
    n_defensive_programming --> n_error_handling
    n_defensive_programming --> n_fail_fast
    n_fail_fast -.-> n_graceful_degradation
    n_fail_safe --> n_resilience
    n_graceful_degradation --> n_fault_tolerance
    n_fault_tolerance --> n_error_handling
    n_fault_tolerance --> n_resilience
    n_resilience --> n_fault_tolerance
    n_error_handling --> n_resilience
    n_error_boundaries --> n_resilience
    n_fallback_pattern --> n_graceful_degradation
    n_retry_pattern --> n_fault_tolerance
    n_circuit_breaker_pattern --> n_fault_tolerance
    n_circuit_breaker_pattern --> n_backpressure
    n_backpressure --> n_resilience
```

### Defensive Programming

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: function, module, boundary
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that code checks its inputs and assumptions before acting on them, and reports a violation as an explicit error.

Requires
[Input Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-input-validation), [Error Handling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-error-handling)

Reinforces
[Robustness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-robustness), [Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast)

Enables
[Safe Failure](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-failure)

In tension with
[Verbosity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-verbosity)

Conflicts with
[Trusting Invalid Inputs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trusting-invalid-inputs)

Tensions
[Defensive Programming / Verbosity](SCHEMA.md#tension-defensive-programming-verbosity)

Distinct from
[Error Handling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-error-handling): Defensive programming checks inputs and assumptions before acting, while error handling decides what happens to an error once raised.

Violated by
[Trusting Invalid Inputs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trusting-invalid-inputs)

Detected by
null/empty/range unsafe access

Measured by
guard coverage, runtime exception rate

Refactored by
[Precondition Check](LEXICON.md#lexicon-precondition-check), [Input Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-input-validation)

Enforced by
linting, [tests](LEXICON.md#lexicon-tests)

Before

```typescript
function renameFoo(foo: Foo, name: string) {
  foo.name = name.trim();
}
```

After

```typescript
function renameFoo(foo: Foo | undefined, name: unknown) {
  if (!foo) throw new Error("Foo required");
  if (typeof name !== "string" || name.trim().length === 0)
    throw new Error("valid name required");
  return { ...foo, name: name.trim() };
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
linting, tests

Population
Every failure path: catch blocks, dependency calls, input boundaries and fallbacks

Freshness
A verdict stands until a dependency, a failure path or the resilience policy changes

Refusal
The lint rule, failure-injection test or policy check fails the change that leaves a failure path unhandled or unsafe

Observation
Catch blocks and dependency calls read from source, plus outcomes recorded by failure-injection runs

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The resilience policy, which every failure path conforms to

Depends on
[Input Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-input-validation), [Error Handling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-error-handling), [Robustness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-robustness), [Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast), [Safe Failure](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-failure)

Shape it refuses
[Trusting Invalid Inputs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trusting-invalid-inputs)

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)

Definition
A design rule that invalid input or state stops the operation at the point it is detected, with an explicit error.

[Preconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-preconditions), [Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-validation)

Reinforces

Before

```typescript
const fooUrl = process.env.FOO_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000";
startFooApp(fooUrl);
```

After

```typescript
const fooUrl = process.env.FOO_URL;
if (!fooUrl) throw new Error("FOO_URL is required");

```

```typescript
try {
  await openFooGate();
} catch {
  fooGate.unlock();
}
```

After

```typescript
} catch {

  throw new Error("Foo gate remains locked");
}
```

Before

```typescript
function authorizeFoo(token?: string) {
  if (!token) return { role: "admin" };
  return decodeToken(token);
}
```

After

```typescript
function authorizeFoo(token?: string): FooIdentity {
  if (!token) throw new UnauthorizedError();
  const identity = verifyToken(token);
  if (!identity) throw new UnauthorizedError();
  return identity;
}
```

Before

```typescript
async function renderFooPage() {
  const foo = await fooService.get();
  const bar = await barRecommendations.get();
  return render(foo, bar);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function renderFooPage() {
  const foo = await fooService.get();
  const bar = await barRecommendations.get().catch(() => [] as Bar[]);
  return render(foo, bar);
}
```

### Resilience

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: production systems
- Scope: service, system, infrastructure
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
The degree to which a system contains failures, stays stable under stress and recovers.

Requires
[Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance), [Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability)

Reinforces
[Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture), [Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-recovery)

Enables
[Stability Under Stress](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stability-under-stress)

In tension with
[Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Brittle Architecture](LEXICON.md#lexicon-brittle-architecture)

Referenced by
[Service Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-service-discovery), [Decentralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decentralization), [Autonomy](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-autonomy), [Message Queue](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-message-queue), [Asynchronous Communication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-asynchronous-communication), [Compensating Transaction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compensating-transaction), [Fail Safe](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-safe), [Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance), [Error Handling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-error-handling), [Error Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-error-boundaries), [Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backpressure), [Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability), [Statelessness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-statelessness), [Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture), [Rollback](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-rollback)

Tensions
[Resilience / Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-complexity-resilience)

Distinct from
[Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance): Resilience contains failures and recovers from them, while fault tolerance keeps operating correctly while components are failing.

Distinct from
[Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling): Resilience is surviving failure, while low coupling is surviving change.

Distinct from
[Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability): Resilience is containing and recovering from failure, while observability is seeing what the system does.

Distinct from
[Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-complexity): Resilience is surviving failure, while complexity is the intricacy that its mechanisms add.

Distinct from
[Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-debuggability): Resilience is recovering without help, while debuggability is how easily the developer can locate a fault.

Distinct from
[Stability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stability): Resilience includes recovery after failure, while stability is steady operation under load without collapse.

Violated by
[Failure Propagation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-propagation)

Detected by
[failure propagation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-propagation), lack of isolation

Measured by
MTTR, error budget, [availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability)

Refactored by
[Circuit Breaker Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-circuit-breaker-pattern), [Bulkhead Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bulkhead-pattern), [Retry Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-retry-pattern), [Timeout Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-timeout-pattern)

Enforced by
[chaos testing](REASONING.md#reasoning-technique-chaos-testing), SLO gates

Before

```typescript
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return remoteFoo.get(id);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return circuitBreaker.execute(() =>
    retry.withBackoff(() => remoteFoo.get(id), { attempts: 3 }),
  );
}
```

### Robustness Principle

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a component is strict in what it sends and tolerant of harmless variation in what it receives.

[Compatibility](LEXICON.md#lexicon-compatibility)

Measured by

Enforced by
compatibility test suite

Before

```typescript
function readFoo(message: any) {
  return { id: message.id, name: message.name };
}
function writeFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return { ...foo, debug: globalThis };
}
```

After

```typescript
function readFoo(message: unknown) {
  const value = FooEnvelopeSchema.parse(message);
  return { id: value.id, name: value.name };
}
function writeFoo(foo: Foo): FooEnvelopeV1 {
  return { version: 1, id: foo.id, name: foo.name };
}
```

error-handling

Before

```typescript
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  try {
    return await fooStore.find(id);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
type LoadFooResult =
  | { ok: true; value: Foo }
  | { ok: false; error: "NOT_FOUND" | "STORE_UNAVAILABLE" };
async function loadFoo(id: FooId): Promise<LoadFooResult> {
  return fooStore.findResult(id);
}
```

[Failure Propagation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-propagation)

Tensions
[Error Boundaries / Hidden Errors](SCHEMA.md#tension-error-boundaries-hidden-errors)

Violated by
[Failure Propagation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-propagation)

Detected by
uncaught exceptions crossing boundary

Measured by
blast radius

Refactored by
[Bulkhead Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bulkhead-pattern)

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
function renderApp() {
  return renderFooPanel(loadFoo());
}
```

After

```typescript
function FooBoundary({ render }: { render(): View }) {
  try {
    return render();
  } catch (error) {
    return renderFooError(toFooError(error));
  }
}
const app = FooBoundary({ render: () => renderFooPanel(loadFoo()) });
```

### Fallback Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: service, dependency call
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that routes a failed call to an alternate provider or response declared in advance.

Requires
[Alternate Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-alternate-behavior)

Reinforces
[Graceful Degradation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-graceful-degradation)

[Partial Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-partial-availability)

[Single Behavior Path](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-behavior-path)

Violated by
[Single Behavior Path](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-behavior-path)

Detected by
hard dependency in optional path

Measured by
fallback coverage

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
failure injection tests

Before

```typescript
const foo = await primaryFooStore.find(id);
```

After

```typescript
const foo = await primaryFooStore
  .find(id)
  .catch(() => replicaFooStore.find(id));
if (!foo) throw new FooUnavailableError(id);
```

### Retry Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: network, IO, message handling
- Aliases: Retry
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that repeats an idempotent call after a transient failure, a bounded number of times with backoff.

Requires
[Idempotency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotency), [Timeout](LEXICON.md#lexicon-timeout), [Backoff](LEXICON.md#lexicon-backoff)

Reinforces
[Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance)

Enables
[Transient Failure Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-transient-failure-recovery)

In tension with
[Load Amplification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-load-amplification)

Conflicts with
[Non-Idempotent Operation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-non-idempotent-operation)

Referenced by
[Eventual Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-eventual-consistency)

Tensions
[Retry Pattern / Load Amplification](SCHEMA.md#tension-load-amplification-retry-pattern)

Violated by
[Unbounded Retry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unbounded-retry), [Retry Storm](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-retry-storm)

Detected by
retry loops without timeout/backoff

Measured by
retry success rate, retry storm rate

Refactored by
[Backoff](LEXICON.md#lexicon-backoff), [Idempotency Key](LEXICON.md#lexicon-idempotency-key)

Enforced by
resilience libraries, policy checks

Before

```typescript
await remoteFoo.save(foo);
```

After

```typescript
await retry.withBackoff(() => remoteFoo.save(foo), {
  attempts: 3,
  retryIf: isTransientError,
  jitter: true,
});
```

resilience libraries, policy checks

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)

Definition
A design pattern that gives every external call a time budget and fails the call when the budget runs out.

Reinforces
[Fault Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fault-isolation)

missing timeout config

Measured by
timeout coverage, latency tail

Refactored by
[Deadline Propagation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-deadline-propagation)

```typescript
const foo = await remoteFoo.find(id);
```

After

```typescript
const foo = await withTimeout(
```

### Circuit Breaker Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: dependency call, service
- Aliases: Circuit Breaker
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that stops calling a dependency after repeated failures and probes it again after a wait.

Requires
[Failure Threshold](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-threshold), [Fallback](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fallback)

Reinforces
[Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance), [Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backpressure)

Enables
[Cascading Failure Prevention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cascading-failure-prevention)

In tension with
[Availability of Degraded Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability-of-degraded-dependency)

Conflicts with
[Unbounded Retry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unbounded-retry), [Retry Storm](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-retry-storm)

Tensions
[Circuit Breaker Pattern / Availability of Degraded Dependency](SCHEMA.md#tension-availability-of-degraded-dependency-circuit-breaker-pattern)

Violated by
[Failure Propagation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-propagation)

Detected by
high failure dependency calls without breaker

Measured by
breaker trip rate, downstream error rate

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
[resilience policy](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-resilience-policy)

Before

```typescript
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return remoteFoo.find(id);
}
```

After

```typescript
const fooBreaker = new CircuitBreaker({
  failureThreshold: 5,
  resetAfterMs: 30_000,
});
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return fooBreaker.execute(() => remoteFoo.find(id));
}
```

Catch blocks and dependency calls read from source, plus outcomes recorded by failure-injection runs

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The resilience policy, which every failure path conforms to

Depends on
[Failure Threshold](LEXICON.md#lexicon-failure-threshold), [Fallback](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fallback), [Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance), [Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backpressure), [Cascading Failure Prevention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cascading-failure-prevention)

### Bulkhead Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: resource pool, service, runtime
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that gives each workload its own pool of threads or connections, so one workload cannot exhaust the others.

Requires
[Resource Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-resource-isolation)

Reinforces
[Fault Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fault-isolation)

Enables
[Blast-Radius Reduction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-blast-radius-reduction)

Violated by
[Shared Resource Pool](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-resource-pool)

Detected by
shared pools across critical/noncritical workloads

Measured by
resource saturation isolation

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
resource policy

Before

```typescript
const pool = new WorkerPool(100);
pool.submit(fooTask);
pool.submit(barTask);
```

After

```typescript
const fooPool = new WorkerPool(20);
const barPool = new WorkerPool(20);
fooPool.submit(fooTask);
barPool.submit(barTask);
```

Checked by
resource policy

Population
Every failure path: catch blocks, dependency calls, input boundaries and fallbacks

Freshness
A verdict stands until a dependency, a failure path or the resilience policy changes

Refusal
The lint rule, failure-injection test or policy check fails the change that leaves a failure path unhandled or unsafe

### Backpressure

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: high-load systems
- Scope: stream, queue, service
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets a consumer signal its capacity, so a producer slows down when the consumer falls behind.

Requires
[Capacity Signaling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-capacity-signaling)

Reinforces
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Stability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stability)

Enables
[Overload Protection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-overload-protection)

In tension with
[Throughput](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-throughput)

Conflicts with
[Missing Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-missing-backpressure)

Referenced by
[Message Queue](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-message-queue), [Circuit Breaker Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-circuit-breaker-pattern), [Rate Limiting](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-rate-limiting), [Streaming Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-streaming-architecture)

Tensions
[Backpressure / Throughput](SCHEMA.md#tension-backpressure-throughput)

Distinct from
[Event Stream](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-stream): Backpressure is a consumer slowing its producer, while an event stream is the replayable log consumers read from their own offset.

Distinct from
[Message Queue](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-message-queue): Backpressure signals capacity back to the producer, while a message queue holds messages until a consumer takes them.

Distinct from
[Rate Limiting](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-rate-limiting): Backpressure slows a producer by the consumer's live capacity, while rate limiting caps a caller at a fixed rate and rejects the excess.

Violated by
[Missing Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-missing-backpressure)

Detected by
queue growth without throttling

Measured by
queue depth, rejection/throttle rate

Refactored by
[Rate Limiting](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-rate-limiting), [Bounded Queue](LEXICON.md#lexicon-bounded-queue), [Autoscaling Policy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-autoscaling-policy)

Enforced by
load tests, runtime policies

Before

```typescript
stream.on("data", (foo) => processFoo(foo));
```

After

```typescript
for await (const foo of stream) {
  await capacity.acquire();
  void processFoo(foo).finally(() => capacity.release());
}
```

load tests, runtime policies

Observation

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side

Depends on
[Capacity Signaling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-capacity-signaling), [Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Stability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stability), [Overload Protection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-overload-protection)

## Architecture Review / Evolution / Governance Artifacts

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_assessment["Assessment"]
    n_architecture_review["Architecture Review"]
    n_design_review["Design Review"]
    n_code_review["Code Review"]
    n_impact_analysis["Impact Analysis"]
    n_gap_analysis["Gap Analysis"]
    n_fitness_functions["Fitness Functions"]
    n_quality_attributes["Quality Attributes"]
    n_architecture_decision_records["Architecture Decision Records (ADR)"]
    n_evolutionary_architecture["Evolutionary Architecture"]
    n_minimum_viable_architecture["Minimum Viable Architecture"]
    n_greenfield_development["Greenfield Development"]
    n_first_principles_design["First-Principles Design"]
    n_reference_architecture["Reference Architecture"]
    n_pattern_consistency["Pattern Consistency"]
    n_architectural_consistency["Architectural Consistency"]
    n_standardization["Standardization"]
    n_assessment --> n_quality_attributes
    n_architecture_review --> n_architecture_decision_records
    n_architecture_review --> n_architectural_consistency
    n_fitness_functions --> n_evolutionary_architecture
    n_quality_attributes --> n_architecture_review
    n_evolutionary_architecture --> n_fitness_functions
    n_greenfield_development --> n_first_principles_design
    n_reference_architecture --> n_standardization
    n_architectural_consistency --> n_pattern_consistency
```

### Assessment

- Kind: [activity](SCHEMA.md#kind-activity)

Details

Definition
The activity of evaluating a codebase or architecture against stated criteria, using collected evidence.

Requires
[Criteria](LEXICON.md#lexicon-criteria), [Evidence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-evidence)

Reinforces
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Quality Attributes](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-quality-attributes)

Tensions
[Assessment / Time Cost](SCHEMA.md#tension-assessment-time-cost)

Violated by
[Assumption-Based Judgment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-assumption-based-judgment)

Detected by

Measured by
assessment coverage

Refactored by
none

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
approveFooArchitecture();
```

After

```typescript
const assessment = assess(fooArchitecture, {
  dimensions: ["modularity", "reliability", "security", "operability"],
  evidence: collectArchitectureEvidence(fooSystem),
});
requirePassingAssessment(assessment);
```

How it is checked

Checked by
review process

Population
Every architecture change, decision and deviation the review or gate is asked to pass

Freshness
A verdict stands for the change it reviewed and goes stale when the architecture, the criteria or the decision record changes

Refusal
The gate or the reviewer withholds approval, so the change does not merge

Observation
The recorded review, decision record or fitness run attached to the change

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The decision record and the review criteria, which a change is compared against

Depends on
[Criteria](LEXICON.md#lexicon-criteria), [Evidence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-evidence), [Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Quality Attributes](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-quality-attributes), [Prioritized Refactoring](LEXICON.md#lexicon-prioritized-refactoring)

```typescript

```

After

```typescript

});
```


How it is checked

Checked by
review checklist

Population
Every architecture change, decision and deviation the review or gate is asked to pass

Freshness
A verdict stands for the change it reviewed and goes stale when the architecture, the criteria or the decision record changes

Refusal
The gate or the reviewer withholds approval, so the change does not merge

Observation
The recorded review, decision record or fitness run attached to the change

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The decision record and the review criteria, which a change is compared against

[Design Criteria](LEXICON.md#lexicon-design-criteria), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [Maintainability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-maintainability), [Early Defect Prevention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-early-defect-prevention)

```typescript

```

After

```typescript
const forces = identifyForces(fooProblem);
const invariants = deriveInvariants(forces);
const design = synthesizeArchitecture({ forces, invariants });
```

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the modules, patterns and allowed dependencies that a family of systems instantiates.

Requires

Reinforces

[Reusable Architecture Guidance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reusable-architecture-guidance): A reference architecture defines the modules and dependencies a family of systems instantiates, while reusable guidance is the wider body of advice it packages.

Violated by

Detected by

Measured by

```typescript
teamB.buildFooAnotherWay();
```

```typescript
const fooReference = defineReferenceArchitecture({
  modules: ["api", "application", "domain", "adapters"],
  allowedDependencies: fooDependencyRules,
});
teamA.instantiate(fooReference);
teamB.instantiate(fooReference);
```

### Pattern Consistency

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Architecture Review / Evolution / Governance Artifacts](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-architecture-review-evolution-governance-artifacts)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)

Details

Definition

Requires
[Naming/Structure Conventions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-naming-structure-conventions)

Reinforces
[Predictability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-predictability), [Maintainability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-maintainability)

Distinct from
[Architectural Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-architectural-consistency): Pattern consistency is one problem solved one way everywhere, while architectural consistency is code following the declared boundaries and layers.

Distinct from
[Local Optimization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-local-optimization): Pattern consistency is the degree shared patterns are used, while local optimization is the one-off gain that using them gives up.

Violated by

Detected by

Enforced by
linting, [review](LEXICON.md#lexicon-review), scaffolding

Before

```typescript
fooModule.useRepository();
barModule.queryDatabaseDirectly();
bazModule.useActiveRecord();
```

After

```typescript
const persistencePattern = "repository" as const;
fooModule.use(persistencePattern);
barModule.use(persistencePattern);
bazModule.use(persistencePattern);
```

## Metadata / Self-Description / Declarative Systems

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_self_describing_architecture["Self-Describing Architecture"]
    n_self_describing_api["Self-Describing API"]
    n_self_describing_structures["Self-Describing Structures"]
    n_metadata_driven_design["Metadata-Driven Design"]
    n_declarative_configuration["Declarative Configuration"]
    n_convention_over_configuration["Convention over Configuration"]
    n_capability_declaration["Capability Declaration"]
    n_manifest_based_design["Manifest-Based Design"]
    n_self_describing_architecture --> n_capability_declaration
    n_metadata_driven_design --> n_declarative_configuration
    n_manifest_based_design --> n_self_describing_architecture
    n_manifest_based_design --> n_capability_declaration
```

### Self-Describing Architecture

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Metadata / Self-Description / Declarative Systems](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-metadata-self-description-declarative-systems)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: system, runtime, integration
- Layer: [Declarative Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-declarative-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that each module declares its name, version, capabilities and requirements in metadata that tools and the runtime can read.

Requires
[Metadata](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metadata), [Capability Declaration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-capability-declaration)

Reinforces
[Discoverability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discoverability), [Runtime Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-discovery)

Enables
[Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture), [Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automation)

In tension with
[Metadata Drift](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metadata-drift)

Conflicts with
[Hidden Runtime Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-runtime-behavior)

Referenced by
[Manifest-Based Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manifest-based-design)

Tensions
[Self-Describing Architecture / Metadata Drift](SCHEMA.md#tension-metadata-drift-self-describing-architecture)

Violated by
[Hidden Runtime Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-runtime-behavior)

Detected by
undocumented runtime capability

Measured by
metadata coverage

Refactored by
[Manifest-Based Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manifest-based-design), [Declare Capability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-capability), [Schema Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-schema-validation)

Enforced by
manifest validation, metadata tests

Before

```typescript
const modules = [new FooModule(), new BarModule()];
```

After

```typescript
type ModuleDescriptor = {
  name: string;
  version: string;
  provides: readonly string[];
  requires: readonly string[];
};
const fooModule = defineModule({
  name: "foo",
  version: "1.0.0",
  provides: ["FooStore"],
  requires: ["EventBus"],
});
```

How it is checked

Checked by
manifest validation, metadata tests

Population
Every manifest, schema, configuration file and declared capability, and the code each one describes

Freshness
A verdict stands until the metadata or the code it describes changes

Refusal
Manifest or schema validation fails when a declaration and the code disagree

Observation
Each declaration compared with the capability, endpoint or structure found in the code

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
None, because the declaration and the code both declare the capability, so a green comparison shows that they agree and not that either is right

Depends on
[Metadata](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metadata), [Capability Declaration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-capability-declaration), [Discoverability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discoverability), [Runtime Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-discovery), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture), [Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automation)

Shape it refuses
[Hidden Runtime Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-runtime-behavior)

```typescript
app.post("/foo", createFoo);
```

After

Details

Definition
An approach in which behavior such as forms, routes or plugins is generated from validated metadata instead of written case by case.

Requires
[Metadata Schema](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metadata-schema), [Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-validation)

Reinforces
[Declarative Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declarative-configuration), [Runtime Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-discovery)

Enables
[Code Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-code-generation), [Plugins](LEXICON.md#lexicon-plugins)

In tension with
[Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-debuggability)

Conflicts with
[Hardcoded Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-behavior)

Referenced by
[Model-Driven Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-driven-architecture)

Tensions
[Metadata-Driven Design / Debuggability](SCHEMA.md#tension-debuggability-metadata-driven-design)

Violated by
[Unvalidated Metadata](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unvalidated-metadata), [Hidden Runtime Behavior](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-runtime-behavior)

Detected by
metadata/config drift

Measured by
metadata coverage, config error rate

Refactored by
[Declare Capability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-capability), [Schema Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-schema-validation), [Configuration Schema](LEXICON.md#lexicon-configuration-schema)

Enforced by
metadata schema tests

Before

```typescript
if (field === "name") renderText();
if (field === "count") renderNumber();
```

After

```typescript
const fooFields = {
  name: { kind: "text", required: true },
  count: { kind: "integer", min: 0 },
} as const;
renderForm(fooFields);
```

How it is checked

Checked by
metadata schema tests

Population
Every manifest, schema, configuration file and declared capability, and the code each one describes

Freshness
A verdict stands until the metadata or the code it describes changes

Refusal
Manifest or schema validation fails when a declaration and the code disagree

Observation
Each declaration compared with the capability, endpoint or structure found in the code

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
None, because the declaration and the code both declare the capability, so a green comparison shows that they agree and not that either is right

[Metadata Schema](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metadata-schema), [Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-validation), [Declarative Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declarative-configuration), [Runtime Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-discovery), [Code Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-code-generation), [Plugins](LEXICON.md#lexicon-plugins)

Before

```typescript
const app = new FooApp();
app.enableCache();
app.setRetries(3);
app.register(new BarPlugin());
```

After

```typescript

  cache: { enabled: true },

});
```

### Convention over Configuration

```typescript
try {
  await plugin.exportFoo(foo);
} catch (error) {
  if (isMissingMethod(error)) return;
}
```

After

```typescript
type FooPlugin = {
  capabilities: readonly ("read" | "write" | "export")[];
  exportFoo?: (foo: Foo) => Promise<void>;
};
if (plugin.capabilities.includes("export")) await plugin.exportFoo!(foo);
```

## Metaprogramming / Language-Oriented Architecture

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_homoiconicity["Homoiconicity"]
    n_code_as_data["Code as Data"]
    n_metaprogramming["Metaprogramming"]
    n_reflection["Reflection"]
    n_introspection["Introspection"]
    n_compile_time_evaluation["Compile-Time Evaluation"]
    n_runtime_code_generation["Runtime Code Generation"]
    n_domain_specific_language["Domain-Specific Language (DSL)"]
    n_language_oriented_programming["Language-Oriented Programming"]
    n_model_driven_architecture["Model-Driven Architecture"]
    n_homoiconicity --> n_metaprogramming
    n_code_as_data --> n_homoiconicity
    n_reflection --> n_introspection
```

### Homoiconicity

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Metaprogramming / Language-Oriented Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-metaprogramming-language-oriented-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: language, metaprogramming
- Layer: [Declarative Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-declarative-core)

Details

Definition
The degree to which a language represents its programs in its own data structures, so programs can be inspected and transformed as data.

Requires
[Code-as-Data Representation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-code-as-data-representation)

Reinforces
[Metaprogramming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-metaprogramming)

Enables
[Macro Systems](LEXICON.md#lexicon-macro-systems), [DSLs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-dsls)

In tension with
[Readability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-readability)

Conflicts with
[Opaque Syntax Trees](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-syntax-trees)

Referenced by
[Code as Data](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-code-as-data)

Tensions
[Homoiconicity / Readability](SCHEMA.md#tension-homoiconicity-readability)

Distinct from
[Readability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-readability): Homoiconicity is programs held as data, while readability is how easily the developer reads the source that results.

Violated by
[String-Based Code Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-string-based-code-generation)

Detected by
language capability check

Measured by
macro/code-as-data usage

Refactored by
[Syntax Tree Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-syntax-tree-generation)

Enforced by
language/tooling constraints

Refused by rules
homoiconicity

Before

```typescript
function evaluateFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return foo.value * 2;
}
const fooRule = { operation: "multiply", operand: 2 };
```

After

```typescript
type Expr =
  | { op: "value"; key: keyof Foo }
  | { op: "const"; value: number }
  | { op: "multiply"; left: Expr; right: Expr };
const fooRule: Expr = {
  op: "multiply",
  left: { op: "value", key: "value" },
  right: { op: "const", value: 2 },
};
const result = evaluate(fooRule, foo);
```

How it is checked

Checked by
language/tooling constraints

Population
Every generator, reflective access, evaluation site and language definition in the codebase

Freshness
A verdict stands until a generator, a grammar or the model it generates from changes

Refusal
The banned-API rule, the generator test or the grammar validation fails the change

Observation
Eval and reflection call sites read from source, and generated output compared with its model

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The model and the grammar, which generated output is derived from and compared against

Depends on
[Code-as-Data Representation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-code-as-data-representation), [Metaprogramming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-metaprogramming), [Macro Systems](LEXICON.md#lexicon-macro-systems), [DSLs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-dsls)

Shape it refuses
[Opaque Syntax Trees](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-syntax-trees)

### Code as Data

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Metaprogramming / Language-Oriented Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-metaprogramming-language-oriented-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: language, compiler, runtime
- Layer: [Declarative Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-declarative-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that logic to be generated or transformed is held as a typed data structure, such as a syntax tree, that tools can inspect and rewrite.

Requires
[AST or Data Representation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ast-or-data-representation)

Reinforces
[Homoiconicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-homoiconicity), [Code Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-code-generation)

Enables
[Program Transformation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-program-transformation)

In tension with
[Safety/Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safety-debuggability)

Conflicts with
[String-Based Code Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-string-based-code-generation)

Tensions
[Code as Data / Safety/Debuggability](SCHEMA.md#tension-code-as-data-safety-debuggability)

Violated by
[Unchecked Dynamic Code](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unchecked-dynamic-code)

Detected by
dynamic eval/string code construction

Measured by
unsafe eval count

Refactored by
[Syntax Tree Generation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-syntax-tree-generation), [Domain-Specific Language (DSL)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-domain-specific-language)

Enforced by
banned API rules

Before

```typescript
function fooRule(foo: Foo) {
  return foo.count > 3 && foo.active;
}
```

After

```typescript
const fooRule = {
  op: "and",
  args: [
    { op: "gt", field: "count", value: 3 },
    { op: "eq", field: "active", value: true },
  ],
} as const;
executeRule(fooRule, foo);
```

None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Before

```typescript
class FooDto {
  id!: string;
  name!: string;
}
class BarDto {
  id!: string;
  name!: string;
}
```

After

```typescript
const entity = defineEntity({ id: string(), name: string() });
const FooDto = generateType("FooDto", entity);
const BarDto = generateType("BarDto", entity);
```

### Reflection

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

[Dynamic Binding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-binding)

In tension with
[Performance/Safety](LEXICON.md#lexicon-performance-safety), [Static Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-static-analysis)

Conflicts with
none

Tensions
[Reflection / Performance/Safety](SCHEMA.md#tension-performance-safety-reflection), [Reflection / Static Analysis](SCHEMA.md#tension-reflection-static-analysis)

Distinct from
[Dynamic Binding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-binding): Reflection reads type metadata at runtime, while dynamic binding selects an implementation at runtime, with or without reflection.

Distinct from
[Introspection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-introspection): Introspection only reads a type and its members, while reflection also acts on what it reads.

Distinct from
[Static Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-static-analysis): Reflection inspects structure while the program runs, while static analysis inspects source without running it.

Violated by
[Reflective Contract Bypass](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reflective-contract-bypass)

Detected by
reflective access to internals

Measured by
unsafe reflection count

Refactored by
[Declare Capability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-capability)

Enforced by
lint/security rules

Before

```typescript
const fields = ["id", "name", "count"];
for (const field of fields) renderField(foo[field]);
```

After

```typescript
for (const [field, metadata] of reflect(FooSchema).entries()) {
  renderField(field, metadata, foo[field]);
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
lint/security rules

Population
Every generator, reflective access, evaluation site and language definition in the codebase

Freshness
A verdict stands until a generator, a grammar or the model it generates from changes

Refusal
The banned-API rule, the generator test or the grammar validation fails the change

Observation
Eval and reflection call sites read from source, and generated output compared with its model

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The model and the grammar, which generated output is derived from and compared against

Depends on
[Runtime Type Metadata](LEXICON.md#lexicon-runtime-type-metadata), [Introspection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-introspection), [Runtime Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-discovery), [Dynamic Binding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dynamic-binding)

Shape it refuses
Not answered

- Kind: [approach](SCHEMA.md#kind-approach)

```typescript
function processFoo(config: Record<string, unknown>) {

}
```

```typescript
const FooPolicyLanguage = defineLanguage({
  expressions: ["field", "equals", "all", "any"],
  typeChecker: fooPolicyTypeChecker,
  evaluator: fooPolicyEvaluator,
});
FooPolicyLanguage.run(fooPolicy, foo);
```

## Model Architecture

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

### Artificial Intelligence Architecture

- Kind: [model](SCHEMA.md#kind-model)
- Category: [Model Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-model-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: model-backed systems
- Scope: model-backed system, application, platform
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A conceptual representation of a system that calls a model behind validated inputs, grounded context, schema-checked outputs and governance.

Requires
[Model Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-governance), [Data/Model Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-data-model-boundaries)

Reinforces
[Model Evaluation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-evaluation), [Model Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-safety)

Enables
[Model-Integrated Systems](LEXICON.md#lexicon-model-integrated-systems)

In tension with
[Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism), [Explainability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explainability)

Conflicts with
[Opaque Ungoverned Model Use](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-ungoverned-model-use)

Referenced by
[Model Inference](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-inference)

Tensions
[Artificial Intelligence Architecture / Determinism](SCHEMA.md#tension-artificial-intelligence-architecture-determinism), [Artificial Intelligence Architecture / Explainability](SCHEMA.md#tension-artificial-intelligence-architecture-explainability)

Violated by
[Opaque Ungoverned Model Use](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-ungoverned-model-use)

Detected by
model calls without tests, [logging](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-logging), [fallback](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fallback), [policy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-policy)

Measured by
model quality/safety/evaluation coverage

Refactored by
[Evaluation Suite](LEXICON.md#lexicon-evaluation-suite), [Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port), [Guardrails](LEXICON.md#lexicon-guardrails)

Enforced by
model governance gates

Before

```typescript
async function answerFoo(prompt: string) {
  return model.generate(prompt);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function answerFoo(request: FooRequest) {
  const input = FooRequestSchema.parse(request);
  const context = await fooRetriever.retrieve(input.query);
  const output = await fooModel.generate(buildFooPrompt(input, context));
  return FooResponseSchema.parse(output);
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
model governance gates

Population
Every model call, model version, prompt, retrieval index and agent tool in a model-backed system

Freshness
A verdict stands for one model version, prompt version and dataset, and goes stale when any of them changes

Refusal
The evaluation gate or the governance gate blocks a model, prompt or index that fails its thresholds or lacks approval

Observation
Evaluation reports, registry entries and live output metrics recorded against the model version

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The evaluation thresholds and the approval record, which a model, prompt or index is compared against

Depends on
[Model Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-governance), [Data/Model Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-data-model-boundaries), [Model Evaluation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-evaluation), [Model Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-safety), [Model-Integrated Systems](LEXICON.md#lexicon-model-integrated-systems)

Shape it refuses
[Opaque Ungoverned Model Use](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-ungoverned-model-use)

MLOps gates

Before

```typescript
const model = trainFoo(loadAllData());
serve(model);
```

After

```typescript
const dataset = datasetRegistry.load("foo", "v3");
const features = fooFeaturePipeline.transform(dataset);
const model = trainFoo(features, versionedTrainingConfig);
modelRegistry.register(model, evaluateFooModel(model, validationSet));
```

How it is checked

Checked by
MLOps gates

Population
Every model call, model version, prompt, retrieval index and agent tool in a model-backed system

Freshness
A verdict stands for one model version, prompt version and dataset, and goes stale when any of them changes

Refusal
The evaluation gate or the governance gate blocks a model, prompt or index that fails its thresholds or lacks approval

Observation

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side

```typescript

```

After

```typescript
const query = normalizeFooQuery(question);
const documents = await fooRetriever.search(query, { topK: 8 });
const groundedPrompt = buildGroundedFooPrompt(question, documents);
const answer = await model.generate(groundedPrompt);
return attachCitations(answer, documents);
```

Before

```typescript
const fooLinks = new Map<string, string[]>();
fooLinks.set(foo.id, [bar.id, baz.id]);
```

After

```typescript
const graph = new KnowledgeGraph();
graph.addNode(foo.id, "Foo", foo);
graph.addNode(bar.id, "Bar", bar);
graph.addEdge(foo.id, "DEPENDS_ON", bar.id);
graph.addEdge(bar.id, "PRODUCES", baz.id);
```

### Explainability

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Model Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-model-architecture)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: regulated domains
- Scope: model, model-backed system, decision flow
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
The degree to which a model's decision comes with the evidence or attribution a reviewer needs to understand it.

Requires
[Traceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-traceability), [Rationale/Evidence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rationale-evidence)

Reinforces
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Trust](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trust)

Enables
[Audit and Debugging](LEXICON.md#lexicon-audit-and-debugging)

In tension with
[Model Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-model-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Opaque Black-Box Decisions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-black-box-decisions)

Referenced by
[Artificial Intelligence Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-artificial-intelligence-architecture), [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-retrieval-augmented-generation), [Knowledge Graphs](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-knowledge-graphs), [Agentic Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-agentic-architecture)

Tensions
[Explainability / Model Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-explainability-model-complexity)

Distinct from
[Model Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-safety): Explainability is a decision arriving with its evidence, while model safety is harmful inputs, outputs and actions being prevented.

Distinct from
[Traceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-traceability): Explainability is why one model decision was made, while traceability is following a request or change end to end.

Distinct from
[Knowledge Freshness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-knowledge-freshness): Explainability is showing the evidence behind a decision, while knowledge freshness is that evidence being current.

Distinct from
[Model Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-model-complexity): Explainability is understanding a decision, while model complexity is the intricacy that makes it harder.

Distinct from
[Trust](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trust): Explainability is the evidence a reviewer can inspect, while trust is how far users rely on the outputs.

Distinct from
[Semantic Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-semantic-consistency): Explainability concerns a model's decisions, while semantic consistency concerns names keeping one meaning.

Violated by
[Opaque Black-Box Decisions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-opaque-black-box-decisions)

Detected by
missing rationale/feature attribution/citations

Measured by
explanation coverage/quality

Refactored by
[Evidence Citation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-evidence-citation)

Enforced by
model governance gates

Before

```typescript
return model.predict(foo.features);
```

After

```typescript
const prediction = await model.predict(foo.features);
const explanation = await explainer.explain({
  modelVersion: model.version,
  input: foo.features,
  prediction,
});
return { prediction, explanation };
```

Before

```typescript
return model.generate(userPrompt);
```

After

```typescript
const input = await safety.validateInput(userPrompt);
const draft = await model.generate(input);
const checked = await safety.validateOutput(draft, {
  policy: "foo-assistant-v2",
});
if (!checked.allowed) return safeRefusal(checked.reasons);
return checked.output;
```

Checked by
safety gates, runtime monitors

Every model call, model version, prompt, retrieval index and agent tool in a model-backed system

Freshness
A verdict stands for one model version, prompt version and dataset, and goes stale when any of them changes

The evaluation gate or the governance gate blocks a model, prompt or index that fails its thresholds or lacks approval

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

### Prompt Engineering

- Kind: [technique](SCHEMA.md#kind-technique)
- Category: [Model Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-model-architecture)

- Scope: model-backed system, language-model system, application
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A technique for writing model instructions as versioned templates with fixed parameters and an evaluation for each change.

Requires
[Model Inference](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-inference)

Reinforces
[Model Evaluation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-evaluation), [Reproducibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-reproducibility)

Violated by
[Prompt Sprawl](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-prompt-sprawl)

Detected by

Measured by
duplicated prompt count

Refactored by
[Prompt Registry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-prompt-registry)

Enforced by
model design review

Before

```typescript
const answer = await model.generate("summarize: " + text);
```

After

```typescript
const prompt = fooPromptTemplate.render({
  task: "summarize",
  input: text,
  format: "bullet-points",
  maxWords: 100,
});
const answer = await model.generate(prompt, { temperature: 0, stop: ["\n\n"] });
```

### Model Drift Monitoring

- Kind: [activity](SCHEMA.md#kind-activity)

none

After

```typescript
monitor.track(fooModel, {
```

## Observability / Auditability / Traceability

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_observability["Observability"]
    n_logging["Logging"]
    n_monitoring["Monitoring"]
    n_alerting["Alerting"]
    n_auditability["Auditability"]
    n_audit_logging["Audit Logging"]
    n_traceability["Traceability"]
    n_correlation_id["Correlation ID"]
    n_causation_id["Causation ID"]
    n_distributed_tracing["Distributed Tracing"]
    n_slo_sli["SLO/SLI"]
    n_dashboards["Dashboards"]
    n_logging --> n_traceability
    n_alerting --> n_monitoring
    n_auditability --> n_audit_logging
    n_auditability --> n_traceability
    n_audit_logging --> n_auditability
    n_audit_logging --> n_traceability
    n_traceability --> n_correlation_id
    n_traceability --> n_auditability
    n_correlation_id --> n_distributed_tracing
    n_distributed_tracing --> n_observability
    n_slo_sli --> n_monitoring
    n_slo_sli --> n_observability
    n_slo_sli --> n_alerting
    n_dashboards --> n_monitoring
    n_dashboards --> n_observability
    n_dashboards --> n_traceability
```

### Observability

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Observability / Auditability / Traceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-observability-auditability-traceability)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: production systems
- Scope: service, system, runtime
- Layer: [Observability](SCHEMA.md#layer-observability)

Details

Definition
The degree to which a system's internal behavior in production can be inferred from the logs, metrics and traces it emits.

Requires
[Logs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-logs), [Metrics](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metrics), [Traces](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traces)

Reinforces
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-debuggability)

Enables
[Incident Diagnosis](LEXICON.md#lexicon-incident-diagnosis)

In tension with
[Cost/Noise](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cost-noise)

Conflicts with
[Unobservable Failure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-unobservable-failure)

Referenced by
[Centralized Logging](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-centralized-logging), [Information Hiding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-information-hiding), [Dead-Letter Queue](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dead-letter-queue), [Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast), [Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Error Handling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-error-handling), [Model Drift Monitoring](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-model-drift-monitoring), [Distributed Tracing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-distributed-tracing), [SLO/SLI](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-slo-sli), [Dashboards](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dashboards), [Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture), [Canary Deployment](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-canary-deployment), [Chaos Engineering](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-chaos-engineering)

Contracts
[Observability](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-observability)

Tensions
[Observability / Cost/Noise](SCHEMA.md#tension-cost-noise-observability)

Distinct from
[Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance): Observability is seeing internal behavior, while fault tolerance is operating correctly through component failure.

Distinct from
[Auditability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auditability): Observability infers internal behavior from signals, while auditability ties sensitive actions to their actors afterwards.

Distinct from
[Traceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-traceability): Observability is the whole view from logs, metrics and traces, while traceability is following one request or change end to end.

Distinct from
[Cost/Noise](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cost-noise): Observability is the insight telemetry gives, while cost and noise are what collecting more of it adds.

Distinct from
[Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-debuggability): Observability is inferring behavior in production, while debuggability is how easily the developer locates a fault.

Distinct from
[Fault Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fault-isolation): Observability is seeing a failure, while fault isolation is keeping it from spreading.

Violated by
[Blind Operation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-blind-operation)

Detected by
missing telemetry around critical paths

Measured by
telemetry coverage, MTTR

Refactored by
[Structured Log](LEXICON.md#lexicon-structured-log), [Metrics](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metrics), [Distributed Tracing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-distributed-tracing)

Enforced by
observability standards

Before

```typescript
async function processFoo(foo: Foo) {
  await fooStore.save(foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function processFoo(foo: Foo, telemetry: Telemetry) {
  return telemetry.trace("foo.process", { fooId: foo.id }, async (span) => {
    await fooStore.save(foo);
    span.event("foo.saved");
    telemetry.count("foo.processed", 1);
  });
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
observability standards

Population
Every critical path, sensitive operation, request and message the telemetry is meant to cover

Freshness
A verdict stands until a code path, a telemetry field or an alert threshold changes

Refusal
The logging, tracing or audit policy check fails a change that leaves a covered path without its signal

Observation
Emitted logs, metrics, spans and audit records, compared with the paths that should emit them

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared telemetry coverage, which the emitted signals are compared against

Depends on
[Logs](LEXICON.md#lexicon-logs), [Metrics](LEXICON.md#lexicon-metrics), [Traces](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traces), [Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Debuggability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-debuggability), [Incident Diagnosis](LEXICON.md#lexicon-incident-diagnosis)

Shape it refuses
[Unobservable Failure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-unobservable-failure), [Unobservable Failure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-unobservable-failure)

production readiness checklist

```typescript
setInterval(() => report(fooQueue.length), 60_000);
```

After

```typescript
metrics.gauge("foo.queue.depth", () => fooQueue.length);
metrics.histogram("foo.processing.duration_ms", fooProcessingDuration);
```

Before

```typescript
function renameFoo(foo: Foo, name: string) {
  foo.name = name;
}
```

After

```typescript
function renameFoo(foo: Foo, name: string, actor: Actor) {
  const previous = foo.name;
  foo.rename(name);
  audit.append({
    action: "FooRenamed",
    fooId: foo.id,
    actorId: actor.id,
    previous,
    next: name,
  });
}
```

```typescript
});
```

```typescript
);
```

```typescript
});
```

## Behavioral Patterns

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_strategy_pattern["Strategy Pattern"]
    n_template_method_pattern["Template Method Pattern"]
    n_observer_pattern["Observer Pattern"]
    n_mediator_pattern["Mediator Pattern"]
    n_command_pattern["Command Pattern"]
    n_state_pattern["State Pattern"]
    n_chain_of_responsibility_pattern["Chain of Responsibility Pattern"]
    n_iterator_pattern["Iterator Pattern"]
    n_visitor_pattern["Visitor Pattern"]
    n_memento_pattern["Memento Pattern"]
    n_null_object_pattern["Null Object Pattern"]
    n_finite_state_machine["Finite State Machine"]
    n_statecharts["Statecharts"]
    n_finite_state_machine --> n_state_pattern
    n_statecharts --> n_finite_state_machine
    n_statecharts --> n_finite_state_machine
```

### Strategy Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Behavioral Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-behavioral-patterns)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: algorithm, policy, behavior
- Aliases: Policy Pattern
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that puts each interchangeable algorithm behind one interface, so the caller selects behavior by passing an object.

Requires
[Interchangeable Algorithms](LEXICON.md#lexicon-interchangeable-algorithms)

Reinforces
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism)

Enables
[Runtime Behavior Selection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-runtime-behavior-selection)

In tension with
[Class Count](LEXICON.md#lexicon-class-count)

Conflicts with
[Large Conditional Logic](LEXICON.md#lexicon-large-conditional-logic)

Referenced by
[Composition Over Inheritance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composition-over-inheritance), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Polymorphism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-polymorphism)

Tensions
[Strategy Pattern / Class Count](SCHEMA.md#tension-class-count-strategy-pattern)

Distinct from
[Decorator Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decorator-pattern): A strategy replaces behavior behind one interface, while a decorator adds behavior by wrapping an object in the same interface.

Violated by
[Large Conditional Logic](LEXICON.md#lexicon-large-conditional-logic)

Detected by
conditional strategy selection with duplicated behavior

```typescript
class FooEvents {
  #listeners = new Set<(event: FooEvent) => void>();
  subscribe(listener: (event: FooEvent) => void) {
    this.#listeners.add(listener);

  }
}

  save(foo: Foo) {
    fooStore.save(foo);
    this.events.publish({ type: "FooSaved", foo });
  }
}

fooEvents.subscribe((event) => sendFooEmail(event.foo));
```

```typescript
interface FooState {
  submit(): FooState;
  approve(): FooState;
}

  submit: () => published,
  approve: () => published,

  constructor(private state: FooState = draft) {}

    this.state = this.state.submit();
  }
  approve() {
    this.state = this.state.approve();
  }
}
```

Details

Definition

[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-responsibility)

Before

```typescript
function handleFoo(request: FooRequest) {
  if (request.size > MAX_SIZE) return reject(request);
  if (!request.authorized) return deny(request);
  return process(request);
}
```

After

```typescript
type FooHandler = (request: FooRequest, next: () => FooResult) => FooResult;
const enforceSize: FooHandler = (request, next) =>
  request.size > MAX_SIZE ? reject(request) : next();
const enforceAuth: FooHandler = (request, next) =>
  request.authorized ? next() : deny(request);
const chain = composeHandlers([
  enforceSize,
  enforceAuth,
  () => process(request),
]);
chain(request);
```

```typescript
interface FooVisitor<T> {

  group(node: GroupNode): T;

  group(node: GroupNode) {

  }
}
```

[design review](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-design-review)

Before

```typescript
const backupName = foo.name;
const backupTags = [...foo.tags];
foo.rename(newName);
if (canceled) {
  foo.name = backupName;
  foo.tags = backupTags;
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooMemento {
  constructor(readonly snapshot: Readonly<Foo>) {}
}
const memento = foo.save();
foo.rename(newName);
if (canceled) foo.restore(memento);
```

Details

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
