Before

```typescript
let isOpen = false,
  isLoading = false,
  isError = false;
function onClick() {
  isLoading = true;
  if (isOpen) isOpen = false;
}
```

After

```typescript
type FooState = "closed" | "loading" | "open" | "error";
const transitions: Record<FooState, Partial<Record<FooEvent, FooState>>> = {
  closed: { open: "loading" },
  loading: { ready: "open", fail: "error" },
  open: { close: "closed" },
  error: { retry: "loading" },
};
function next(state: FooState, event: FooEvent): FooState {
  return transitions[state][event] ?? state;
}
```

```typescript
const fooChart = {

  parallel: { volume: { states: { muted: {}, loud: {} } } },
};
```

## Creational Patterns

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_factory_pattern["Factory Pattern"]
    n_factory_method_pattern["Factory Method Pattern"]
    n_abstract_factory_pattern["Abstract Factory Pattern"]
    n_builder_pattern["Builder Pattern"]
    n_prototype_pattern["Prototype Pattern"]
    n_singleton_pattern["Singleton Pattern"]
```

### Factory Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Creational Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-creational-patterns)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: [object_creation](SCHEMA.md#force-object-creation), module
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that moves the construction of an object and its defaults into one function or object.

Requires
[Creation Variation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-creation-variation)

Reinforces
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation)

Enables
[Polymorphic Construction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-polymorphic-construction)

In tension with
[Simplicity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity)

Conflicts with
[Scattered Construction Logic](LEXICON.md#lexicon-scattered-construction-logic)

Referenced by
[Registry Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-registry-pattern)

Tensions
[Factory Pattern / Simplicity](SCHEMA.md#tension-factory-pattern-simplicity)

Violated by
[Scattered Construction Logic](LEXICON.md#lexicon-scattered-construction-logic)

Detected by
repeated constructors/switches

Measured by
construction duplication count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
creation policy review

Before

```typescript
const foo = new Foo("foo", 0, [], new Date(), "draft");
```

After

```typescript
function makeFoo(name: string): Foo {
  return new Foo(fooId(), name, 0, [], clock.now(), "draft");
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
creation policy review

Population
Every construction site of the types the pattern governs

Freshness
A verdict stands until a constructor, a variant or the composition root changes

Refusal
The review or the construction test rejects a construction that bypasses the creational owner

Observation
Constructor call sites and their argument counts, read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The creational owner, which every construction site goes through

Depends on
[Creation Variation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-creation-variation), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation), [Polymorphic Construction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-polymorphic-construction)

After

```typescript
  protected parser() {
    return new JsonFooParser();
  }
}
```

Details

A design pattern that creates new objects by cloning a prepared template and applying overrides.

[Cloneable Template Object](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cloneable-template-object)

[Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility)

Refactored by
none

Before

```typescript
function copyFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return new Foo(
    foo.id,
    foo.name,
    [...foo.tags],
    foo.settings.theme,
    foo.settings.mode,
  );
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooPrototype {
  constructor(private readonly base: Foo) {}
  clone(overrides: Partial<Foo> = {}): Foo {
    return structuredClone({ ...this.base, ...overrides });
  }
}
const template = new FooPrototype(await buildExpensiveFoo());
const draft = template.clone({ name: "quick" });
```

## Structural Patterns

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_adapter_pattern["Adapter Pattern"]
    n_facade_pattern["Facade Pattern"]
    n_proxy_pattern["Proxy Pattern"]
    n_bridge_pattern["Bridge Pattern"]
    n_decorator_pattern["Decorator Pattern"]
    n_composite_pattern["Composite Pattern"]
    n_flyweight_pattern["Flyweight Pattern"]
```

### Adapter Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: integration, boundary
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that wraps a component with an incompatible interface so it implements the interface its callers expect.

Requires
[Incompatible Interfaces](LEXICON.md#lexicon-incompatible-interfaces)

Reinforces
[Anti-Corruption Layer](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-anti-corruption-layer), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability)

Enables
[Interoperability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interoperability)

In tension with
[Mapping Overhead](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mapping-overhead)

Conflicts with
[Direct External Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-external-coupling)

Referenced by
[Interface-Based Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interface-based-design)

Tensions
[Adapter Pattern / Mapping Overhead](SCHEMA.md#tension-adapter-pattern-mapping-overhead)

Distinct from
[Anti-Corruption Layer](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-anti-corruption-layer): An adapter fits one incompatible interface to the one expected, while an anti-corruption layer translates a whole external model into the local domain's terms.

Violated by
[Direct External Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-external-coupling)

Detected by
external SDK types in domain/application

Measured by
external leakage count

Refactored by
[Extract Adapter](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-adapter), [Anti-Corruption Layer](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-anti-corruption-layer)

Enforced by
boundary import rules

Before

```typescript
function saveFoo(foo: Foo) {
  return legacyClient.put(foo.id, foo.name, foo.count);
}
```

After

```typescript
class LegacyFooAdapter implements FooStore {
  constructor(private readonly client: LegacyClient) {}
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return this.client.put(foo.id, foo.name, foo.count);
  }
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
boundary import rules

Population
Every boundary, wrapper and composite structure that sits between a caller and the objects it uses

Freshness
A verdict stands until the wrapped interface or its callers change

Refusal
The boundary import rule or the conformance test fails a caller that reaches past the structure

Observation
Imports and call sites that cross the structure, read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The structure's interface, which every caller goes through

Depends on
[Incompatible Interfaces](LEXICON.md#lexicon-incompatible-interfaces), [Anti-Corruption Layer](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-anti-corruption-layer), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Interoperability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interoperability)

Shape it refuses
[Direct External Coupling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-external-coupling)

### Facade Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: module, subsystem, API
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that gives a subsystem one simple entry point, so callers do not depend on its parts.

Requires
[Subsystem Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subsystem-complexity)

Reinforces
[Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation), [Information Hiding](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-information-hiding)

Enables
[Simplified Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplified-access)

In tension with
[Over-Centralization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-over-centralization)

Conflicts with
[Leaky Subsystem API](LEXICON.md#lexicon-leaky-subsystem-api)

Tensions
[Facade Pattern / Over-Centralization](SCHEMA.md#tension-facade-pattern-over-centralization)

Violated by
[Leaky Subsystem API](LEXICON.md#lexicon-leaky-subsystem-api)

Detected by
broad dependency surface to subsystem

Measured by
consumer dependency count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
API boundary rules

Before

```typescript
const foo = fooValidator.validate(fooParser.parse(raw));
await fooStore.save(foo);
await fooEvents.publish(foo);
```

After

```typescript
class FooFacade {
  async create(raw: string) {
    const foo = fooValidator.validate(fooParser.parse(raw));
    await fooStore.save(foo);
    await fooEvents.publish(foo);
  }
}
```

### Proxy Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: access control, remote access, lazy loading
- Aliases: Surrogate
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that places a stand-in with the same interface in front of an object, to control, defer or cache access to it.

Requires
[Controlled Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controlled-access)

Reinforces
[Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation), [Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security)

Enables
[Lazy Load](LEXICON.md#lexicon-lazy-load), [Authorization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-authorization), [Remote Stub](LEXICON.md#lexicon-remote-stub)

In tension with
[Transparency / Debugging](LEXICON.md#lexicon-transparency-debugging)

Conflicts with
[Direct Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-access)

Tensions
[Proxy Pattern / Transparency / Debugging](SCHEMA.md#tension-proxy-pattern-transparency-debugging)

Violated by
[Direct Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-access)

Detected by
bypassed access wrapper

Measured by
proxy bypass count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
access rules

Before

```typescript
function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return remoteFooStore.find(id);
}
```

After

```typescript
class CachingFooStoreProxy implements FooStore {
  constructor(private readonly target: FooStore) {}
  async find(id: FooId) {
    const cached = fooCache.get(id);
    if (cached) return cached;
    const foo = await this.target.find(id);
    fooCache.set(id, foo);
    return foo;
  }
}
```

Observation
Imports and call sites that cross the structure, read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The structure's interface, which every caller goes through

Depends on
[Controlled Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controlled-access), [Encapsulation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-encapsulation), [Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security), [Lazy Load](LEXICON.md#lexicon-lazy-load), [Authorization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-authorization), [Remote Stub](LEXICON.md#lexicon-remote-stub)

### Bridge Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: abstraction, implementation variation
- Aliases: Handle-Body
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that separates two independent axes of variation into two hierarchies joined by composition.

Requires
[Independent Variation Axes](LEXICON.md#lexicon-independent-variation-axes)

Reinforces
[Composition Over Inheritance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composition-over-inheritance)

Enables
[Implementation Swap](LEXICON.md#lexicon-implementation-swap)

In tension with
[Indirection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-indirection)

Conflicts with
[Cartesian Inheritance Explosion](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cartesian-inheritance-explosion)

Tensions
[Bridge Pattern / Indirection](SCHEMA.md#tension-bridge-pattern-indirection)

Violated by
[Cartesian Inheritance Explosion](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cartesian-inheritance-explosion)

Detected by
parallel hierarchies / deep variant classes

Measured by
variant class count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
[design review](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-design-review)

Before

```typescript
class SqlJsonFooExporter {}
class SqlCsvFooExporter {}
class MemoryJsonFooExporter {}
class MemoryCsvFooExporter {}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooSource {
  read(): Promise<readonly Foo[]>;
}
interface FooFormat {
  encode(foos: readonly Foo[]): string;
}
class FooExporter {
  constructor(
    private readonly source: FooSource,
    private readonly format: FooFormat,
  ) {}
  async export() {
    return this.format.encode(await this.source.read());
  }
}
```

### Decorator Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: behavior composition
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that adds behavior to an object by wrapping it in another object with the same interface.

Requires
[Common Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-common-interface)

Reinforces
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Composability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composability)

Enables
[Runtime Behavior Extension](LEXICON.md#lexicon-runtime-behavior-extension)

In tension with
[Stack Debugging](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stack-debugging)

Conflicts with
[Subclass Explosion](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subclass-explosion)

Referenced by
[Composition Over Inheritance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composition-over-inheritance)

Tensions
[Decorator Pattern / Stack Debugging](SCHEMA.md#tension-decorator-pattern-stack-debugging)

Violated by
[Subclass Explosion](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subclass-explosion)

Detected by
repeated wrapper-like subclasses

Measured by
variant explosion count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
interface conformance tests

Before

```typescript
class LoggedSqlFooStore extends SqlFooStore {
  override save(foo: Foo) {
    logger.info("foo.saved", { fooId: foo.id });
    return super.save(foo);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class LoggedFooStore implements FooStore {
  constructor(
    private readonly inner: FooStore,
    private readonly log: Log,
  ) {}
  save(foo: Foo) {
    this.log.write(foo.id);
    return this.inner.save(foo);
  }
}
```

Evidence

Authoritative side
The structure's interface, which every caller goes through

[Common Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-common-interface), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Composability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composability), [Runtime Behavior Extension](LEXICON.md#lexicon-runtime-behavior-extension)

### Composite Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: structure, tree, hierarchy
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that gives leaves and groups one interface, so a tree is traversed without checking which kind each node is.

Requires
[Uniform Component Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-uniform-component-interface)

Reinforces
[Uniform Interface](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-uniform-interface), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed)

Enables
[Recursive Composition](LEXICON.md#lexicon-recursive-composition), [Leaf/Composite Transparency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-leaf-composite-transparency)

In tension with
[Type Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-type-safety)

Conflicts with
[Leaf-vs-Container Special-Casing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-leaf-vs-container-special-casing)

Tensions
[Composite Pattern / Type Safety](SCHEMA.md#tension-composite-pattern-type-safety)

Violated by
[Leaf-vs-Container Special-Casing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-leaf-vs-container-special-casing)

Detected by
isContainer/isLeaf conditionals during traversal

Measured by
node-kind conditional count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
[design review](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-design-review)

Before

```typescript
function totalFoo(item: Foo | FooGroup): number {
  if ("children" in item)
    return item.children.reduce((sum, child) => sum + totalFoo(child), 0);
  return item.value;
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooComponent {
  total(): number;
}
class FooLeaf implements FooComponent {
  constructor(private readonly value: number) {}
  total() {
    return this.value;
  }
}
class FooGroup implements FooComponent {
  constructor(private readonly children: readonly FooComponent[]) {}
  total() {
    return this.children.reduce((sum, child) => sum + child.total(), 0);
  }
}
```

Authoritative side

### Flyweight Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Structural Patterns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-structural-patterns)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: structure, memory, sharing
- Layer: [Design Patterns Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-design-patterns-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that shares one copy of immutable intrinsic state among many objects, each keeping only its own extrinsic state.

Requires
[Separable Intrinsic State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-separable-intrinsic-state)

Reinforces
[Memory Efficiency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-memory-efficiency)

Enables
[Shared Immutable State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-immutable-state), [High-Cardinality Object Reuse](LEXICON.md#lexicon-high-cardinality-object-reuse)

In tension with
[Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Per-Instance Duplicate State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-per-instance-duplicate-state)

Tensions
[Flyweight Pattern / Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-complexity-flyweight-pattern)

Violated by
[Per-Instance Duplicate State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-per-instance-duplicate-state)

Detected by
repeated equal intrinsic state across objects

Measured by
duplicate-state memory footprint

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
profiling review

Before

```typescript
const icons = foos.map(
  (foo) => new FooIcon(foo.position, loadSprite(foo.kind)),
);
```

After

```typescript
const spriteCache = new Map<string, Sprite>();
function fooSprite(kind: string) {
  const cached = spriteCache.get(kind);
  if (cached) return cached;
  const sprite = loadSprite(kind);
  spriteCache.set(kind, sprite);
  return sprite;
}
const icons = foos.map((foo) => ({
  position: foo.position,
  sprite: fooSprite(foo.kind),
}));
```

profiling review

Every boundary, wrapper and composite structure that sits between a caller and the objects it uses

Refusal

Observation
Imports and call sites that cross the structure, read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The structure's interface, which every caller goes through

[Separable Intrinsic State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-separable-intrinsic-state), [Memory Efficiency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-memory-efficiency), [Shared Immutable State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-immutable-state), [High-Cardinality Object Reuse](LEXICON.md#lexicon-high-cardinality-object-reuse)

### Scalability

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Scalability / Performance / Optimization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-scalability-performance-optimization)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: service, system, infrastructure
- Layer: [Performance Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-performance-core)

Details

Definition
The degree to which a system keeps its throughput and latency as load grows, by adding resources.

Requires
[Load Model](LEXICON.md#lexicon-load-model), [Bottleneck Awareness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-bottleneck-awareness)

Reinforces
[Performance Engineering](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-performance-engineering)

Enables
[Growth Handling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-growth-handling)

In tension with
[Simplicity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency)

Conflicts with
[Fixed-Capacity Design](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fixed-capacity-design)

Referenced by
[Service Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-service-discovery), [Message Broker](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-message-broker), [Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-command-query-responsibility-segregation), [Eventual Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-eventual-consistency), [Elasticity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-elasticity), [Load Balancing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-load-balancing), [Partitioning](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-partitioning), [Caching](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-caching), [Throughput](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-throughput), [Performance Engineering](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-performance-engineering), [Algorithmic Efficiency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-algorithmic-efficiency), [Memory Efficiency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-memory-efficiency), [Stateless Processing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stateless-processing), [Replication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replication), [Microservices](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-microservices)

Tensions
[Scalability / Simplicity](SCHEMA.md#tension-scalability-simplicity), [Scalability / Consistency](SCHEMA.md#tension-consistency-scalability)

Distinct from
[Elasticity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-elasticity): Scalability is keeping throughput as load grows by adding resources, while elasticity is those resources following demand automatically in both directions.

Distinct from
[Low Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-low-coupling): Scalability is growing with load, while low coupling is changing without ripple.

Distinct from
[Memory Efficiency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-memory-efficiency): Scalability is growth by adding resources, while memory efficiency is bounded use of the resources one process has.

Distinct from
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience): Scalability is holding performance under load, while resilience is containing and recovering from failure.

Distinct from
[Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability): Scalability is growing with load, while testability is running code in isolation.

Distinct from
[Cost Efficiency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cost-efficiency): Scalability is keeping throughput as load grows, while cost efficiency is the resource cost of the work.

Distinct from
[Resource Efficiency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-resource-efficiency): Scalability adds resources to meet load, while resource efficiency uses as few as possible for the same work.

Distinct from
[Simplicity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity): Scalability is growth with load, while simplicity is the absence of the structure that growth tends to add.

Distinct from
[Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability): Scalability is performance under growing load, while availability is the share of time the system serves at all.

Violated by
[Bottlenecks](LEXICON.md#lexicon-bottlenecks)

Detected by
saturation under load test

Measured by
throughput under increasing load

Refactored by
[Caching](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-caching), [Partitioning](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-partitioning), [Introduce Async Event](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-async-event), [Horizontal Scaling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-horizontal-scaling)

Enforced by
load tests, SLO gates

Before

```typescript
class FooServer {
  private readonly foos = new Map<FooId, Foo>();
  handle(request: FooRequest) {
    return processFoo(request, this.foos);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooServer {
  constructor(private readonly store: DistributedFooStore) {}
  handle(request: FooRequest) {
    return processFoo(request, this.store);
  }
}
```

load tests, SLO gates

Refusal
The load test, benchmark or SLO gate fails the change that breaks its budget

### Caching

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Scalability / Performance / Optimization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-scalability-performance-optimization)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: data access, computation, API
- Layer: [Performance Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-performance-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that stores the result of an expensive read or computation under a key derived from every input it depends on, and serves it again while that key matches.

Requires
[Invalidation Policy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-invalidation-policy)

Reinforces
[Latency Reduction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-latency-reduction), [Scalability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-scalability)

Enables
[Reduced Load](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reduced-load)

In tension with
[Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Always-Fresh Reads](LEXICON.md#lexicon-always-fresh-reads)

Conflicts with
[Cache Poisoning by Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-cache-poisoning-by-design)

Referenced by
[CDN / Edge Caching](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-cdn-edge-caching)

Tensions
[Caching / Consistency](SCHEMA.md#tension-caching-consistency), [Caching / Always-Fresh Reads](SCHEMA.md#tension-always-fresh-reads-caching)

Violated by
[Repeated Stable Computation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-repeated-stable-computation)

Detected by
hot repeated reads, high latency calls

Measured by
hit ratio, stale read rate

Refactored by
[Context-Keyed Cache](LEXICON.md#lexicon-context-keyed-cache), [Cache Invalidation on Write](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cache-invalidation-on-write)

Enforced by
performance tests

Before

```typescript
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return fooStore.find(id);
}
```

After

```typescript
async function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  const key = fingerprint(id, await fooStore.versionOf(id));
  const cached = await fooCache.get(key);
  if (cached) return cached;
  const foo = await fooStore.find(id);
  if (foo) await fooCache.set(key, foo);
  return foo;
}
```

```typescript
  ]);
  return render(foo, bar, baz);
}
```

```typescript
function duplicateFooIds(foos: Foo[]) {
  return foos.filter(
    (foo, index) => foos.findIndex((x) => x.id === foo.id) !== index,
  );
}
```

After

```typescript
function duplicateFooIds(foos: readonly Foo[]) {
  const seen = new Set<FooId>();
  return foos.filter((foo) => seen.has(foo.id) || !seen.add(foo.id));
}
```

Before

```typescript
function pairFoosWithBars(foos: Foo[], bars: Bar[]) {
  return foos.flatMap((foo) =>
    bars.filter((bar) => bar.fooId === foo.id).map((bar) => [foo, bar]),
  );
}
```

After

```typescript
function pairFoosWithBars(foos: readonly Foo[], bars: readonly Bar[]) {
  const barsByFoo = groupBy(bars, (bar) => bar.fooId);
  return foos.flatMap((foo) =>
    (barsByFoo.get(foo.id) ?? []).map((bar) => [foo, bar]),
  );
}
```

Refactored by
[Bottleneck Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bottleneck-analysis), [Cleanup / Simplification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-cleanup-simplification)

Enforced by
benchmark review

Before

```typescript
const fooCache = new Map<FooId, Foo>();
function loadFoo(id: FooId) {
  return fooCache.get(id) ?? expensiveLoad(id);
}
```

After

```typescript
const profile = profiler.measure("foo.load", representativeFooIds);
if (profile.hotspot === "foo-store-read") {
  enableBoundedFooCache({ maxEntries: 10_000, keyBy: fooVersionFingerprint });
}
```

### Rate Limiting

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that caps how many requests a caller can make in a time window and rejects the excess.

Reinforces
[Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backpressure), [Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security)

Refactored by

Before

```typescript
app.post("/foo", createFoo);
```

After

```typescript
app.post(
  "/foo",
  rateLimit({
    key: (request) => request.identity.id,
    limit: 100,
    windowMs: 60_000,
  }),
  createFoo,
);
```

### Read Replica

- Kind: [technique](SCHEMA.md#kind-technique)

Details

Definition

[Horizontal Scaling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-horizontal-scaling): A read replica scales database reads by copying data, while horizontal scaling adds stateless service instances behind a load balancer.

Violated by

```typescript

await primaryDb.write(fooCommand);
```


## Streaming / Pipeline / Dataflow Processing

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_streaming_architecture["Streaming Architecture"]
    n_single_pass_processing["Single-Pass Processing"]
    n_pipeline_architecture["Pipeline Architecture"]
    n_lazy_evaluation["Lazy Evaluation"]
    n_sequential_access["Sequential Access"]
    n_forward_only_processing["Forward-Only Processing"]
    n_dataflow_architecture["Dataflow Architecture"]
    n_stateless_processing["Stateless Processing"]
    n_windowing["Windowing"]
    n_fan_out_fan_in["Fan-out/Fan-in"]
    n_batch_vs_stream["Batch-vs-Stream"]
    n_streaming_architecture --> n_single_pass_processing
    n_forward_only_processing --> n_single_pass_processing
    n_dataflow_architecture --> n_pipeline_architecture
    n_windowing --> n_streaming_architecture
```

### Streaming Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)

- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of processing data record by record as it arrives, with backpressure, instead of collecting it first.

Requires

Reinforces

Enables

In tension with

Conflicts with
none

Referenced by

Tensions

Violated by
[Full Materialization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-full-materialization)

Detected by
unbounded collection over stream source

Measured by
lag, [throughput](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-throughput), memory usage

Refactored by
[Backpressure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backpressure)

Enforced by
load/memory tests

Before

```typescript
const foos = await source.readAll();
const results = foos.map(transformFoo);
await sink.writeAll(results);
```

After

```typescript
for await (const foo of source.stream()) {
  await sink.write(transformFoo(foo));
}
```

Before

```typescript
const names = foos.map((foo) => foo.name);
const active = foos.filter((foo) => foo.active);
const total = foos.reduce((sum, foo) => sum + foo.count, 0);
```

After

```typescript
const names: string[] = [];
const active: Foo[] = [];
let total = 0;
for (const foo of foos) {
  names.push(foo.name);
  if (foo.active) active.push(foo);
  total += foo.count;
}
```

## Plugin / Extensibility / IoC

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

### Plugin Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Plugin / Extensibility / IoC](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-plugin-extensibility-ioc)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: component, runtime, system
- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of building a small core that discovers and loads plugins through declared extension points.

Requires
[Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points), [Stable Interfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stable-interfaces), [Discovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discovery)

Reinforces
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Modularity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-modularity)

Enables
[Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility)

In tension with
[Static Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-static-analysis), [Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security)

Conflicts with
[Hardcoded Extensions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-extensions)

Referenced by
[Runtime Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-discovery), [Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility), [Modularity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-modularity), [Composability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composability), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Self-Describing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-describing-architecture), [Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points)

Tensions
[Plugin Architecture / Static Analysis](SCHEMA.md#tension-plugin-architecture-static-analysis), [Plugin Architecture / Security](SCHEMA.md#tension-plugin-architecture-security)

Violated by
[Hardcoded Extensions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-extensions)

Detected by
direct plugin imports, central switch for plugins

Measured by
plugin isolation score

Refactored by
[Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points), [Registry Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-registry-pattern)

Enforced by
plugin contract tests, dependency rules

Before

```typescript
class FooApp {
  run() {
    new FooExport().run();
    new BarExport().run();
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooPlugin {
  name: string;
  setup(app: FooApp): void;
}
class FooApp {
  constructor(private readonly plugins: readonly FooPlugin[]) {}
  run() {
    this.plugins.forEach((plugin) => plugin.setup(this));
  }
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
plugin contract tests, dependency rules

Population
Every extension point, plugin, registration and dependency construction site

Freshness
A verdict stands until a plugin, a registration or the composition root changes

Refusal
The dependency rule, plugin contract test or banned-API rule fails a change that hardcodes an extension or hides a dependency

Observation
Imports from the core to plugins, construction sites and registry contents, read from source and at startup

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The extension contract, which every plugin conforms to while the core names no plugin

Depends on
[Extension Points](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-extension-points), [Stable Interfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stable-interfaces), [Discovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discovery), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Modularity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-modularity), [Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility)

### Extension Points

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Plugin / Extensibility / IoC](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-plugin-extensibility-ioc)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: framework, plugin, module
- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that exposes named hooks or interfaces where new behavior can be added without editing the core.

Requires
[Stable Interfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stable-interfaces), [Contracts](LEXICON.md#lexicon-contracts)

Reinforces
[Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture)

Enables
[Third-Party Extension](LEXICON.md#lexicon-third-party-extension)

In tension with
[API Surface Growth](LEXICON.md#lexicon-api-surface-growth)

Conflicts with
[Closed Core](LEXICON.md#lexicon-closed-core)

Referenced by
[Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility), [Open/Closed Principle (OCP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-open-closed), [Plugin Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-plugin-architecture)

Tensions
[Extension Points / API Surface Growth](SCHEMA.md#tension-api-surface-growth-extension-points)

Violated by
[Closed Core](LEXICON.md#lexicon-closed-core)

Detected by

Measured by
extension coverage

Refactored by
[Extract Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-interface)

Enforced by
extension tests, API review

Before

```typescript
function saveFoo(foo: Foo) {
  validateFoo(foo);
  fooStore.save(foo);
  sendFooEmail(foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
type FooHooks = {
  beforeSave: Array<(foo: Foo) => void>;
  afterSave: Array<(foo: Foo) => void>;
};
function saveFoo(foo: Foo, hooks: FooHooks) {
  hooks.beforeSave.forEach((hook) => hook(foo));
  fooStore.save(foo);
  hooks.afterSave.forEach((hook) => hook(foo));
}
```

### Inversion of Control (IoC)

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Plugin / Extensibility / IoC](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-plugin-extensibility-ioc)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: framework, runtime, component
- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a framework or composition root owns object creation and control flow, and application code supplies the parts it calls.

Requires
[Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Composition Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-composition-root)

Reinforces
[Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Dependency Injection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-injection)

Enables
[Framework Control Flow](LEXICON.md#lexicon-framework-control-flow), [Plugins](LEXICON.md#lexicon-plugins)

In tension with
[Traceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-traceability)

Conflicts with
[Direct Control Ownership](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-control-ownership)

Tensions
[Inversion of Control (IoC) / Traceability](SCHEMA.md#tension-inversion-of-control-ioc-traceability)

Violated by
[Direct Control Ownership](LEXICON.md#lexicon-direct-control-ownership)

Detected by
scattered object lifecycle construction

Measured by
composition centralization

Refactored by
[Dependency Injection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-injection), [Composition Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-composition-root)

Enforced by
lifecycle rules

Before

```typescript
class FooJob {
  run() {
    const store = new SqlFooStore();
    return store.save(makeFoo());
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooJob {
  constructor(
    private readonly make: () => Foo,
    private readonly store: FooStore,
  ) {}
  run() {
    return this.store.save(this.make());
  }
}
container.run(FooJob);
```

### Dependency Injection

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Plugin / Extensibility / IoC](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-plugin-extensibility-ioc)

- Scope: class, module, component

- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that passes an object its dependencies from outside, usually through its constructor.

Requires
[Abstraction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-abstraction), [Composition Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-composition-root)

Reinforces
[Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability)

Enables
[Mocking](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mocking), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability)

[Hardcoded Instantiation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-instantiation), [Ambient Context](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ambient-context)

Referenced by

Tensions
[Dependency Injection / Constructor Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-constructor-complexity-dependency-injection)

Distinct from
[Adapter Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-adapter-pattern): Dependency injection supplies a dependency from outside, while an adapter makes an incompatible interface fit the one expected.

Distinct from
[Composition Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-composition-root): Dependency injection is passing dependencies in, while the composition root is the one place where they are wired.

Distinct from
[Ports and Adapters Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ports-and-adapters-architecture): Dependency injection is how one object receives its dependencies, while ports and adapters is how a whole core is isolated from its technologies.

Distinct from
[Singleton Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-singleton-pattern): Dependency injection passes a dependency in, while a singleton is reached through a global access point.

Violated by
[Hardcoded Instantiation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-instantiation)

Detected by
direct construction of external dependencies

Measured by
injected dependency ratio

Refactored by
[Factory Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-factory-pattern)

Enforced by
lint rules, dependency review

```typescript
class FooService {
  private readonly clock = new SystemClock();
  private readonly store = new SqlFooStore();
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooService {
  constructor(
    private readonly clock: Clock,
    private readonly store: FooStore,
  ) {}
}
```

### Registry Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Plugin / Extensibility / IoC](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-plugin-extensibility-ioc)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: runtime, module, plugin
- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that replaces a conditional over kinds with a keyed table that each kind registers itself into.

Requires
[Keyed Registration](LEXICON.md#lexicon-keyed-registration)

Reinforces
[Discovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discovery), [Factory Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-factory-pattern)

Enables
[Dynamic Lookup](LEXICON.md#lexicon-dynamic-lookup)

In tension with
[Global State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-global-state)

Conflicts with

Tensions

Distinct from
[Factory Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-factory-pattern): A registry replaces a conditional over kinds with a keyed table, while a factory owns how one object and its defaults are built.

Violated by
[Ungoverned Global Registry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ungoverned-global-registry)

Detected by
mutable global maps without lifecycle

Measured by
registry consistency

Refactored by
[Narrow Type](LEXICON.md#lexicon-narrow-type)

Enforced by
registry validation

Before

```typescript
function makeFoo(kind: string) {
  if (kind === "foo") return new Foo1();
  if (kind === "bar") return new Bar();
  throw new Error("unknown kind");
}
```

After

```typescript
type FooFactory = () => Foo;
const registry = new Map<string, FooFactory>();
export const registerFoo = (kind: string, factory: FooFactory) =>
  registry.set(kind, factory);
export const makeFoo = (kind: string) =>
  registry.get(kind)?.() ?? fail(`unknown ${kind}`);
```

- Scope: application, release, runtime
- Aliases: Feature Flag
- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that switches a code path on or off at runtime from externally held flag state, so a release can happen without a deploy.

Requires
[Externalized Flag State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-externalized-flag-state)

Reinforces
[Continuous Delivery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-continuous-delivery), [Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility)

Enables
[Decoupled Deploy and Release](LEXICON.md#lexicon-decoupled-deploy-and-release), [Gradual Rollout](LEXICON.md#lexicon-gradual-rollout)

In tension with
[Flag Debt](LEXICON.md#lexicon-flag-debt)

Conflicts with
[Hardcoded Branch Constant](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-branch-constant)

Tensions
[Feature Toggle / Flag Debt](SCHEMA.md#tension-feature-toggle-flag-debt)

Violated by
[Hardcoded Branch Constant](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-branch-constant)

Detected by
compile-time flags requiring redeploy to flip

Measured by
redeploys per behavior change

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
release review

Before

```typescript
if (NEW_FOO_FLOW_ENABLED) runNewFooFlow();
else runOldFooFlow();
```

After

```typescript
if (featureFlags.enabled("new-foo-flow", { user, percentage: 10 }))
  runNewFooFlow();
else runOldFooFlow();
```

How it is checked

Checked by
release review

Population
Every extension point, plugin, registration and dependency construction site

Freshness
A verdict stands until a plugin, a registration or the composition root changes

Refusal
The dependency rule, plugin contract test or banned-API rule fails a change that hardcodes an extension or hides a dependency

Observation
Imports from the core to plugins, construction sites and registry contents, read from source and at startup

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The extension contract, which every plugin conforms to while the core names no plugin

Depends on
[Externalized Flag State](LEXICON.md#lexicon-externalized-flag-state), [Continuous Delivery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-continuous-delivery), [Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility), [Decoupled Deploy and Release](LEXICON.md#lexicon-decoupled-deploy-and-release), [Gradual Rollout](LEXICON.md#lexicon-gradual-rollout)

Shape it refuses
[Hardcoded Branch Constant](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hardcoded-branch-constant)

## Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_self_healing_architecture["Self-Healing Architecture"]
    n_health_checks["Health Checks"]
    n_failover["Failover"]
    n_redundancy["Redundancy"]
    n_replication["Replication"]
    n_auto_scaling["Auto-Scaling"]
    n_auto_remediation["Auto-Remediation"]
    n_rollback["Rollback"]
    n_blue_green_deployment["Blue-Green Deployment"]
    n_canary_deployment["Canary Deployment"]
    n_chaos_engineering["Chaos Engineering"]
    n_graceful_shutdown["Graceful Shutdown"]
    n_raid_redundancy["RAID Redundancy"]
    n_self_healing_architecture --> n_health_checks
    n_self_healing_architecture --> n_auto_remediation
    n_health_checks --> n_self_healing_architecture
    n_failover --> n_redundancy
    n_redundancy --> n_failover
    n_replication --> n_failover
    n_auto_remediation --> n_self_healing_architecture
    n_blue_green_deployment --> n_rollback
    n_chaos_engineering --> n_self_healing_architecture
    n_raid_redundancy --> n_redundancy
```

### Self-Healing Architecture

- Kind: [capability](SCHEMA.md#kind-capability)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: system, infrastructure, runtime
- Aliases: Self-Healing
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
The ability of a system to detect a failed component from its health signals and restore it without human action.

Requires
[Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability), [Health Checks](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-health-checks), [Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automation)

Reinforces
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience)

Enables
[Auto-Remediation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auto-remediation)

In tension with
[Unsafe Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unsafe-automation)

Conflicts with
[Manual Runbook Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manual-runbook-dependency)

Referenced by
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Health Checks](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-health-checks), [Auto-Remediation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auto-remediation), [Chaos Engineering](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-chaos-engineering)

Tensions
[Self-Healing Architecture / Unsafe Automation](SCHEMA.md#tension-self-healing-architecture-unsafe-automation)

Distinct from
[Auto-Remediation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auto-remediation): A self-healing architecture is the whole system restoring its components, while auto-remediation is one automated response to one known failure.

Distinct from
[Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automation): Self-healing is restoring failed components without human action, while automation is any task run without manual intervention.

Distinct from
[Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-recovery): Self-healing is recovery that the system starts itself, while recovery is returning to correct operation by any means.

Violated by
[Manual Runbook Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manual-runbook-dependency)

Detected by
recurring manual recovery steps

Measured by
MTTR, auto-recovery success

Refactored by
[Health Checks](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-health-checks), [Recovery Policy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-recovery-policy)

Enforced by
orchestration policy, runbooks

Before

```typescript
process.on("error", (error) => fooLog.record(error));
```

After

```typescript
supervisor.watch("foo-worker", {
  start: startFooWorker,
  health: fooWorkerHealth,
  restart: { maxAttempts: 5, backoffMs: 1000 },
});
```

How it is checked

Checked by
orchestration policy, runbooks

Population
Every service, replica, release and recovery path in production

Freshness
A verdict stands until the topology, the release or the recovery policy changes, and is renewed by each recovery drill

Refusal
The release gate, disaster-recovery test or orchestration policy blocks a release or topology without a working recovery path

Observation
Health signals, recovery outcomes and drill results recorded against each service

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The recovery policy, which each drill and recovery outcome is compared against

Depends on
[Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability), [Health Checks](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-health-checks), [Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automation), [Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Auto-Remediation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auto-remediation)

Shape it refuses
[Manual Runbook Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manual-runbook-dependency)

### Health Checks

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: services
- Scope: service, deployment, runtime
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that reports whether an instance and the dependencies it needs are ready to serve, so routing and restarts can act on it.

Requires
[Observable Health Criteria](LEXICON.md#lexicon-observable-health-criteria)

Reinforces
[Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture), [Load Balancing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-load-balancing)

Enables
[Readiness/Liveness Routing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-readiness-liveness-routing)

In tension with
[False Positives](LEXICON.md#lexicon-false-positives)

Conflicts with
[Blind Routing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-blind-routing)

Referenced by
[Service Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-service-discovery), [Load Balancing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-load-balancing), [Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture)

Tensions
[Health Checks / False Positives](SCHEMA.md#tension-false-positives-health-checks)

Distinct from
[Load Balancing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-load-balancing): Health checks report whether an instance can serve, while load balancing spreads requests across the instances that can.

Violated by
[Blind Routing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-blind-routing)

Detected by
missing or shallow health endpoint

Measured by
health-check accuracy

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
deployment policy

Before

```typescript
app.get("/health", () => "ok");
```

After

```typescript
app.get("/health", async () => {
  const fooStoreOk = await fooStore.ping();
  const eventBusOk = await eventBus.ping();
  return {
    state: fooStoreOk && eventBusOk ? "ready" : "blocked",
    checks: { fooStore: fooStoreOk, eventBus: eventBusOk },
  };
});
```

How it is checked

Checked by
deployment policy

Population
Every service, replica, release and recovery path in production

Freshness
A verdict stands until the topology, the release or the recovery policy changes, and is renewed by each recovery drill

Refusal
The release gate, disaster-recovery test or orchestration policy blocks a release or topology without a working recovery path

Observation
Health signals, recovery outcomes and drill results recorded against each service

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The recovery policy, which each drill and recovery outcome is compared against

Depends on
[Observable Health Criteria](LEXICON.md#lexicon-observable-health-criteria), [Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture), [Load Balancing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-load-balancing), [Readiness/Liveness Routing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-readiness-liveness-routing)

Shape it refuses
[Blind Routing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-blind-routing)

### Failover

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: service, infrastructure, data
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that switches traffic or reads to a standby instance when the active one fails.

Requires
[Redundancy](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-redundancy), [Health Detection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-health-detection)

Reinforces
[Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability)

Enables
[Continuity During Failure](LEXICON.md#lexicon-continuity-during-failure)

In tension with
[Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency)

Conflicts with
[Single Instance Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-instance-dependency)

Referenced by
[Service Discovery](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-service-discovery), [Redundancy](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-redundancy), [Replication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replication)

Tensions
[Failover / Consistency](SCHEMA.md#tension-consistency-failover)

Distinct from
[Redundancy](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-redundancy): Failover is the switch to a standby, while redundancy is keeping the standby there to switch to.

Distinct from
[Replication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replication): Failover switches traffic to another instance, while replication keeps that instance's data current.

Violated by
[Single Instance Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-instance-dependency)

Detected by
single active dependency with no failover

Measured by
failover time, [availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability)

Refactored by
[Read Replica](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-read-replica)

Enforced by
disaster recovery tests

Before

```typescript
const foo = await primaryFooStore.find(id);
```

After

```typescript
const foo = await failover.read([primaryFooStore, secondaryFooStore], (store) =>
  store.find(id),
);
```

How it is checked

Checked by
disaster recovery tests

Population
Every service, replica, release and recovery path in production

Freshness
A verdict stands until the topology, the release or the recovery policy changes, and is renewed by each recovery drill

Refusal
The release gate, disaster-recovery test or orchestration policy blocks a release or topology without a working recovery path

Observation
Health signals, recovery outcomes and drill results recorded against each service

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The recovery policy, which each drill and recovery outcome is compared against

Depends on
[Redundancy](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-redundancy), [Health Detection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-health-detection), [Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability), [Continuity During Failure](LEXICON.md#lexicon-continuity-during-failure)

Shape it refuses
[Single Instance Dependency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-instance-dependency)

### Replication

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)

[Elasticity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-elasticity)

none

none

### Auto-Remediation

- Kind: [capability](SCHEMA.md#kind-capability)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: runtime, service, infrastructure
- Aliases: Autonomous Recovery
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
The ability to run a guarded, automated response, such as a restart, a reset and replay or a compaction, when an alert or a health signal shows a failure whose fix is known.

Requires
[Health Signal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-health-signal), [Remediation Workflow](LEXICON.md#lexicon-remediation-workflow)

Reinforces
[Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture)

Enables
[Incident Reduction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-incident-reduction), [Reduced Mean Time to Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reduced-mean-time-to-recovery)

In tension with
[Unsafe Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unsafe-automation), [Manual Remediation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-manual-remediation)

Conflicts with
[Manual Runbook Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manual-runbook-dependency)

Referenced by
[Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture)

Tensions
[Auto-Remediation / Unsafe Automation](SCHEMA.md#tension-auto-remediation-unsafe-automation), [Auto-Remediation / Manual Remediation](SCHEMA.md#tension-auto-remediation-manual-remediation)

Distinct from
[Incident Reduction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-incident-reduction): Auto-remediation is running the known fix, while incident reduction is the fall in incidents that reach a responder as a result.

Distinct from
[Reduced Mean Time to Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reduced-mean-time-to-recovery): Auto-remediation is running the known fix, while reduced mean time to recovery is the shorter outage that results.

Violated by
[Manual Runbook Dependency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-manual-runbook-dependency)

Detected by
repeated manual runbook actions

Measured by
remediation success, false action rate

Refactored by
[Automate the Runbook](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automate-the-runbook), [Guardrails](LEXICON.md#lexicon-guardrails)

Enforced by
operations policy

Before

```typescript
alert.on("FooDiskFull", pageOnCall);
```

After

```typescript
alert.on("FooDiskFull", async (event) => {
  await fooStorage.compact(event.volumeId);
  await fooStorage.verify(event.volumeId);
});
```

### Rollback

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that restores the previous versioned release when a deployment fails its verification.

Requires
[Versioned Artifact](LEXICON.md#lexicon-versioned-artifact), [Reversible Deployment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reversible-deployment)

Reinforces
[Resilience](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-resilience), [Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-recovery)

Enables
[Fast Failure Recovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fast-failure-recovery)

[Data Migration Compatibility](LEXICON.md#lexicon-data-migration-compatibility)

Referenced by
[Blue-Green Deployment](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-blue-green-deployment)

Tensions
[Rollback / Data Migration Compatibility](SCHEMA.md#tension-data-migration-compatibility-rollback)

Violated by
[Irreversible Deployment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-irreversible-deployment)

Detected by
no rollback path

Measured by
rollback success time

Refactored by
[Rollback Plan](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rollback-plan), [Expand-Contract Migration](LEXICON.md#lexicon-expand-contract-migration)

Enforced by

```typescript
deploy(fooVersion);
```

After

```typescript
const release = await deploy(fooVersion);
if (!(await release.verify())) await release.rollback(previousFooVersion);
```

### Blue-Green Deployment

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that deploys a release to an idle copy of production, verifies it, and switches traffic to it at once.

Requires

Reinforces

Violated by
[In-Place Mutation Only](LEXICON.md#lexicon-in-place-mutation-only)

Detected by
no parallel release environment

Measured by
cutover failure rate

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
deployment pipeline

Before

```typescript
routeAllTraffic(deployFoo("v2"));
```

After

```typescript
const green = await deployFoo("v2");
await verify(green);

```

### Canary Deployment

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that sends a small share of traffic to a new release and widens the share only while its error and latency stay within limits.

Requires
[Traffic Splitting](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traffic-splitting), [Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability)

Reinforces

Violated by
[Big-Bang Release](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-big-bang-release)

Detected by

Measured by
canary error budget, rollback trigger rate

Refactored by
[Guardrails](LEXICON.md#lexicon-guardrails)

Enforced by
deployment pipeline

Before

```typescript
await router.route("foo-v2", 100);
```

After

```typescript
await router.route("foo-v2", 5);
await verifyCanary({ errorRate: 0.01, latencyP95Ms: 200 });
await router.progressiveShift("foo-v2", [25, 50, 100]);
```

### Chaos Engineering

- Kind: [activity](SCHEMA.md#kind-activity)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)

Definition
The practice of injecting controlled faults into a running system to test a stated hypothesis about how it recovers.

Requires
[Observability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability)

Reinforces
[Self-Healing Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-healing-architecture), [Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance)

Measured by

none

After

```typescript
chaos.experiment("foo-zone-loss", {

});
```

### Graceful Shutdown

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Self-Healing / Recovery / Deployment Safety](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-self-healing-recovery-deployment-safety)

- Mandatory for: production systems
- Scope: service, runtime, resilience
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that, on a stop signal, stops accepting work, drains in-flight work and closes connections before the process exits.

Requires
[Lifecycle Signals](LEXICON.md#lexicon-lifecycle-signals)

Reinforces
[Reliability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reliability), [Data Integrity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-data-integrity)

Enables
[In-Flight Work Drain](LEXICON.md#lexicon-in-flight-work-drain), [Connection Cleanup](LEXICON.md#lexicon-connection-cleanup)

In tension with

Conflicts with
[Hard Process Kill](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hard-process-kill)

Tensions
[Graceful Shutdown / Shutdown Latency](SCHEMA.md#tension-graceful-shutdown-shutdown-latency)

Violated by
[Hard Process Kill](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hard-process-kill)

Detected by
dropped in-flight work on deploy/restart

Measured by
requests lost per restart

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
operations review

Before

```typescript
process.on("SIGTERM", () => process.exit(0));
```

After

```typescript
process.on("SIGTERM", async () => {
  server.stopAccepting();
  await fooQueue.drain();
  await server.close();
  process.exit(0);
});
```

```typescript
  }),
});
```

## Schema / Canonical Data / Semantics

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_schema_validation["Schema Validation"]
    n_type_safety["Type Safety"]
    n_canonical_model["Canonical Model"]
    n_canonical_data_model["Canonical Data Model"]
    n_canonical_schema["Canonical Schema"]
    n_canonicalization["Canonicalization"]
    n_single_source_of_truth["Single Source of Truth"]
    n_normalization["Normalization"]
    n_semantic_consistency["Semantic Consistency"]
    n_ubiquitous_language["Ubiquitous Language"]
    n_intent_revealing_interface["Intent-Revealing Interface"]
    n_principle_of_least_surprise["Principle of Least Surprise"]
    n_database_normalization["Database Normalization"]
    n_canonical_model --> n_semantic_consistency
    n_canonical_model --> n_ubiquitous_language
    n_canonical_model --> n_single_source_of_truth
    n_canonical_data_model --> n_canonical_model
    n_canonical_data_model --> n_normalization
    n_canonical_schema --> n_canonical_data_model
    n_canonical_schema --> n_schema_validation
    n_semantic_consistency --> n_ubiquitous_language
    n_ubiquitous_language --> n_intent_revealing_interface
    n_intent_revealing_interface --> n_principle_of_least_surprise
    n_principle_of_least_surprise --> n_intent_revealing_interface
    n_database_normalization --> n_single_source_of_truth
```

### Schema Validation

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Schema / Canonical Data / Semantics](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-schema-canonical-data-semantics)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: data, API, message
- Layer: [Contracts Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-contracts-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that parses incoming data against a schema at the boundary and rejects any payload that does not conform.

Requires
[Schema Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-schema-contract)

Reinforces
[Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [Data Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-data-contract)

Enables
[Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast), [Interoperability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interoperability)

In tension with
[Flexible Input](LEXICON.md#lexicon-flexible-input)

Conflicts with
[Untyped Payloads](LEXICON.md#lexicon-untyped-payloads)

Referenced by
[Schema Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-schema-contract), [Declarative Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declarative-configuration), [Canonical Schema](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-canonical-schema)

Tensions
[Schema Validation / Flexible Input](SCHEMA.md#tension-flexible-input-schema-validation)

Violated by
[Trusting External Input](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trusting-external-input)

Detected by
missing validator at boundary

Measured by
validation coverage

Refactored by
[Introduce Boundary DTO](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-boundary-dto)

Enforced by
[runtime validation](REASONING.md#reasoning-technique-runtime-validation), CI schema checks

Before

```typescript
const foo = JSON.parse(raw) as Foo;
```

After

```typescript
const FooSchema = object({
  id: string(),
  name: string().min(1),
  count: integer().min(0),
});
const foo = FooSchema.parse(JSON.parse(raw));
```

How it is checked

Checked by
runtime validation, CI schema checks

Population
Every schema, type, name and stored fact that represents one concept

Freshness
A verdict stands until a schema, a type or a stored representation changes

Refusal
The type checker, schema registry or validation pipeline fails a representation that diverges from the canonical one

Observation
Schemas and types compared across producers, stores and consumers of the same concept

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The canonical representation, which every producer, store and consumer conforms to

Depends on
[Schema Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-schema-contract), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [Data Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-data-contract), [Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast), [Interoperability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interoperability)

[Untyped Payloads](LEXICON.md#lexicon-untyped-payloads)

### Type Safety

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

Definition

Requires
[Explicit Types](LEXICON.md#lexicon-explicit-types)

Reinforces
[Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [Contracts](LEXICON.md#lexicon-contracts)

Referenced by
[Explicit Contracts](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-contracts), [Data Contract](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-data-contract), [Static Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-static-analysis), [Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-liskov-substitution), [Compile-Time Evaluation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compile-time-evaluation), [Composite Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-composite-pattern)

[Type Safety / Rapid Scripting](SCHEMA.md#tension-rapid-scripting-type-safety)

Distinct from
[Compile-Time Evaluation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compile-time-evaluation): Type safety rejects wrongly typed operations at compile time, while compile-time evaluation runs computations and checks during the build.

Violated by
[Dynamic Untyped Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-dynamic-untyped-boundaries)

Detected by
weak type usage, unsafe casts

Measured by
type coverage, unsafe cast count

Refactored by
[Narrow Type](LEXICON.md#lexicon-narrow-type), [Introduce Boundary DTO](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-boundary-dto)

Enforced by
compiler flags, type checker

Refused by rules
type-safety

Before

```typescript
function loadFoo(id: string): any {
  return fooStore.get(id);
}
const count = loadFoo("x").coutn + 1;
```

After

```typescript
type FooId = string & { readonly __brand: "FooId" };
type Foo = Readonly<{ id: FooId; count: number }>;
function loadFoo(id: FooId): Foo | undefined {
  return fooStore.get(id);
}
```

### Canonical Model

Details

Definition
A design rule that a concept has one authoritative representation, and every other representation is translated to and from it.

Requires
[Semantic Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-semantic-consistency), [Ubiquitous Language](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ubiquitous-language)

[Multiple Competing Models](LEXICON.md#lexicon-multiple-competing-models)

Detected by

Measured by
model duplication count

Enforced by
schema governance, domain review

Before

```typescript
type ApiFoo = { foo_id: string; label: string };
type DbFoo = { id: string; name: string };
type UiFoo = { key: string; title: string };
```

After

```typescript
type Foo = Readonly<{ id: FooId; name: string }>;
const fromApi = (value: ApiFoo): Foo => ({
  id: fooId(value.foo_id),
  name: value.label,
});
const toUi = (foo: Foo): UiFoo => ({ key: foo.id, title: foo.name });
```

How it is checked

Checked by
schema governance, domain review

Population

### Canonicalization

Details

Definition
A technique for converting equivalent values to one normal form before they are compared, stored or checked.

Requires
[Canonical Format](LEXICON.md#lexicon-canonical-format)

Reinforces
[Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-validation), [Deduplication](LEXICON.md#lexicon-deduplication)

Enables

Refactored by
none

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
const keys = ["Foo", " foo ", "FOO"];
const map = new Map(keys.map((key) => [key, loadFoo(key)]));
```

After

```typescript
function canonicalFooKey(value: string) {
  return value.trim().normalize("NFKC").toLowerCase();
}
const map = new Map(
  keys.map((key) => [canonicalFooKey(key), loadFoo(canonicalFooKey(key))]),
);
```

### Single Source of Truth

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Schema / Canonical Data / Semantics](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-schema-canonical-data-semantics)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: configuration, data, rule, schema
- Aliases: SSOT
- Layer: [Contracts Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-contracts-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that each fact, rule or configuration value has one owning definition, and every other value is derived from it.

Requires
[Ownership](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ownership), [Canonical Definition](LEXICON.md#lexicon-canonical-definition)

Reinforces
[Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-duplicate-code), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency)

Enables
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness)

In tension with
[Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability), [Decentralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decentralization)

Conflicts with
[Duplicated Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicated-authority), [Magic Value](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-magic-value)

Referenced by
[Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-duplicate-code), [Canonical Model](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-canonical-model), [Database Normalization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-database-normalization), [Derived Record State](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-derived-record-state), [Projection Channel](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-projection-channel), [Two-Direction Index](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-two-direction-index), [Period-Decided Disposition](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-period-decided-disposition), [Single Aggregate](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-aggregate), [Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Declared Jurisdiction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declared-jurisdiction), [Derived Naming Registry](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-derived-naming-registry), [Collision Consolidation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-collision-consolidation), [Externally Resolved Slot](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-externally-resolved-slot)

Contracts
[Structural Core](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-structural-core), [Centralization Kernel](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-centralization-kernel), [CSS Type-Cascade Kernel](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-css-type-cascade-concern)

Tensions
[Single Source of Truth / Availability](SCHEMA.md#tension-availability-single-source-of-truth), [Single Source of Truth / Decentralization](SCHEMA.md#tension-decentralization-single-source-of-truth)

Distinct from
[Canonical Model](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-canonical-model): A single source of truth gives each fact one owner, while a canonical model gives a concept one representation that others translate to and from.

Distinct from
[Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary): A single source of truth owns each fact once, while a closed vocabulary limits the words a name slot may hold.

Distinct from
[Collision Consolidation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-collision-consolidation): A single source of truth is one owner per fact, while collision consolidation reads a taken filename as evidence of two files doing one job.

Distinct from
[Declared Jurisdiction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declared-jurisdiction): A single source of truth is one owner per fact, while declared jurisdiction is the declaration a naming gate reads its scope from.

Distinct from
[Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-duplicate-code): A single source of truth owns facts, rules and configuration values, while DRY keeps one source for logic and constants in code.

Distinct from
[Decentralization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-decentralization): A single source of truth centralizes ownership of a fact, while decentralization spreads decisions and control to the owning teams.

Distinct from
[Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism): A single source of truth fixes where a fact lives, while determinism fixes that the same inputs give the same result.

Distinct from
[Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-governance): A single source of truth owns facts, while governance holds decisions to policy.

Violated by
[Duplicated Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicated-authority)

Detected by
conflicting definitions

Measured by
duplicate authority count

Refactored by
[Centralize the Rule](LEXICON.md#lexicon-centralize-the-rule)

Enforced by
config governance, [schema registry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-schema-registry)

Before

```typescript
let fooCount = 0;
const foos: Foo[] = [];
function addFoo(foo: Foo) {
  foos.push(foo);
  fooCount += 1;
}
```

After

```typescript
const foos: Foo[] = [];
function addFoo(foo: Foo) {
  foos.push(foo);
}
function fooCount() {
  return foos.length;
}
```
