[Principle of Least Surprise](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-principle-of-least-surprise): An intent-revealing interface states what an operation does in its name and parameters, while least surprise requires the behavior to match what they lead a caller to expect.

Violated by
[Ambiguous API](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ambiguous-api), [Boolean Trap](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-boolean-trap)

Detected by
generic names, unclear parameters

Measured by
API clarity review findings

Refactored by
[Name the Concept](LEXICON.md#lexicon-name-the-concept), [Replace Boolean with Enum](LEXICON.md#lexicon-replace-boolean-with-enum), [Value Object](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-value-object)

Enforced by
naming lint, API review

Before

```typescript
foo.update("s", "A");
foo.apply(3, true);
```

After

```typescript
foo.activate();
foo.reserve({ quantity: 3, notify: true });
```

How it is checked

Checked by
naming lint, API review

Population
Every schema, type, name and stored fact that represents one concept

Freshness
A verdict stands until a schema, a type or a stored representation changes

Refusal

Observation

None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The canonical representation, which every producer, store and consumer conforms to

[Clear Semantics](LEXICON.md#lexicon-clear-semantics), [Naming Consistency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-naming-consistency), [Principle of Least Surprise](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-principle-of-least-surprise), [Readability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-readability), [Correct Usage](LEXICON.md#lexicon-correct-usage)

### Principle of Least Surprise

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Schema / Canonical Data / Semantics](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-schema-canonical-data-semantics)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)

Definition

Reinforces

Detected by

Measured by

Enforced by
API review, [tests](LEXICON.md#lexicon-tests)

Before

```typescript
function getFoo(id: FooId) {
  fooStore.delete(id);
  return undefined;
}
```

After

```typescript
function getFoo(id: FooId) {
  return fooStore.find(id);
}
function deleteFoo(id: FooId) {
  return fooStore.delete(id);
}
```

```typescript
type FooRow = {
  id: string;
  customerName: string;
  customerCity: string;
```

```typescript
type Foo = { id: FooId; customerId: CustomerId };
type Customer = { id: CustomerId; name: string; cityId: CityId };
type City = { id: CityId; name: string; zip: string };
```

## Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. ### Security by Design

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: system, service, codebase
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that threats are modeled and controls built into every component from its first design.

Requires
[Threat Modeling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-threat-modeling), [Secure by Default](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-secure-by-default)

Reinforces
[Defense in Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-defense-in-depth), [Compliance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compliance)

Enables
[Proactive Risk Reduction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-proactive-risk-reduction)

In tension with
[Developer Ergonomics](LEXICON.md#lexicon-developer-ergonomics)

Conflicts with
[Security as Afterthought](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security-as-afterthought)

Referenced by
[Fail Secure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-secure), [Defense in Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-defense-in-depth), [Attack Surface Reduction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-attack-surface-reduction), [Threat Modeling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-threat-modeling), [Risk Management](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-risk-management)

Contracts
[Security Core](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-security-core)

Tensions
[Security by Design / Developer Ergonomics](SCHEMA.md#tension-developer-ergonomics-security-by-design)

Distinct from
[Attack Surface Reduction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-attack-surface-reduction): Security by design builds controls in from the first design, while attack surface reduction removes what nothing uses.

Distinct from
[Fail Secure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-secure): Security by design is the approach to every component, while fail secure is one rule, that a failed check denies access.

Distinct from
[Defense in Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-defense-in-depth): Security by design puts controls in from the start, while defense in depth layers several independent controls on each asset.

Distinct from
[Secure by Default](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-secure-by-default): Security by design shapes the whole design, while secure by default fixes the state its settings ship in.

Violated by
[Security as Afterthought](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security-as-afterthought)

Detected by
missing authz/input validation/threat model

Measured by
security control coverage

Refactored by
[Trust Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trust-boundaries), [Input Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-input-validation), [Access Control](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-access-control)

Enforced by
security gates, [policy-as-code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-policy-as-code)

Before

```typescript
function createFoo(request: Request) {
  return fooStore.save(request.body as Foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
function createFoo(request: Request, identity: Identity) {
  const input = CreateFooSchema.parse(request.body);
  authorize(identity, "foo:create");
  return fooStore.save(Foo.create(input));
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
security gates, policy-as-code

Population
Every endpoint, credential, data store, permission and policy inside the trust boundary

Freshness
A verdict stands until the code, the policy, the configuration or the threat model changes

Refusal
The security gate, policy engine or secret scan fails the change or rejects the request

Observation
Scans of source and configuration, policy decisions, and security test results

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The policy and the threat model, which code, configuration and requests conform to

Depends on
[Threat Modeling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-threat-modeling), [Secure by Default](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-secure-by-default), [Defense in Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-defense-in-depth), [Compliance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compliance), [Proactive Risk Reduction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-proactive-risk-reduction)

Shape it refuses
[Security as Afterthought](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security-as-afterthought)

### Defense in Depth

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: system, infrastructure, application

Details

Definition
A design rule that several independent security controls protect each asset, so one failed control does not expose it.

Requires
[Layered Controls](LEXICON.md#lexicon-layered-controls)

Reinforces
[Security by Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-security-by-design)

Enables

In tension with
[Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-complexity)

Tensions
[Defense in Depth / Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-complexity-defense-in-depth)

Violated by
[Single Control Reliance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-control-reliance)

Detected by

Measured by
control depth

Refactored by
[Controls](LEXICON.md#lexicon-controls)

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
app.post("/foo", createFoo);
```

After

```typescript
app.post(
  "/foo",
  authenticate(),
  authorize("foo:create"),
  validate(CreateFooSchema),
  rateLimit({ limit: 100 }),
  audit("FOO_CREATE"),
  createFoo,
);
```

Every endpoint, credential, data store, permission and policy inside the trust boundary

Observation
Scans of source and configuration, policy decisions, and security test results

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The policy and the threat model, which code, configuration and requests conform to

[Least Privilege Over Broad Privilege](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-no-broad-privilege)

Violated by

Detected by
overbroad roles/scopes

Measured by
privilege excess count

Refactored by
[Least-Privilege Credential](LEXICON.md#lexicon-least-privilege-credential)

Enforced by
IAM policy checks

Before

```typescript
class FooJob {
  constructor(private readonly db: AdminDatabase) {}
  run(foo: Foo) {
    return this.db.execute(`insert into foo values (?)`, foo);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
interface FooWriter {
  insert(foo: Foo): Promise<void>;
}
class FooJob {
  constructor(private readonly foos: FooWriter) {}
  run(foo: Foo) {
    return this.foos.insert(foo);
  }
}
```

### Zero Trust Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: system, network, identity
- Aliases: Zero Trust
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of authenticating and authorizing every request on its own identity and context, whatever network it comes from.

Requires
[Strong Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-strong-identity), [Continuous Authorization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-continuous-authorization)

Reinforces
[Least Privilege](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-least-privilege)

Enables
[Perimeterless Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-perimeterless-security)

In tension with
[Latency/Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-latency-complexity)

Referenced by
[Least Privilege](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-least-privilege)

Term
[Zero Trust](LEXICON.md#lexicon-zero-trust)

Tensions
[Zero Trust Architecture / Latency/Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-latency-complexity-zero-trust-architecture)

Violated by
[Trusted Internal Network Assumption](LEXICON.md#lexicon-trusted-internal-network-assumption)

Detected by
internal endpoints without authz/authn

Measured by
trustless control coverage

Refactored by
[Authentication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-authentication), [Authorization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-authorization), [Network Segmentation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-network-segmentation)

Enforced by
[policy-as-code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-policy-as-code), gateway rules

Before

```typescript
if (request.network === "internal") return createFoo(request.body);
```

After

```typescript
const identity = authenticate(request.credentials);
authorize(identity, "foo:create", { resource: request.body.id });
verifyDevice(request.deviceAttestation);
return createFoo(CreateFooSchema.parse(request.body));
```

### Secure by Default

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: configuration, API, product
- Aliases: Secure Defaults
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that every setting ships in its most restrictive safe state, and weakening one requires an explicit opt-in.

Requires
[Safe Defaults](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-defaults)

Reinforces
[Fail Secure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-secure)

Enables
[Reduced Misconfiguration Risk](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reduced-misconfiguration-risk)

In tension with
[Ease of Initial Use](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ease-of-initial-use)

Conflicts with
[Insecure Defaults](LEXICON.md#lexicon-insecure-defaults)

Referenced by
[Fail Secure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-secure), [Security by Design](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-security-by-design), [Parameterized Queries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-parameterized-queries)

Tensions
[Secure by Default / Ease of Initial Use](SCHEMA.md#tension-ease-of-initial-use-secure-by-default)

Distinct from
[Fail Secure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-secure): Secure by default is the state settings ship in, while fail secure is the state a failed check leaves access in.

Distinct from
[Safe Defaults](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-defaults): Secure by default restricts access in the shipped settings, while safe defaults avoid harm in the shipped behavior.

### Authentication

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: user, service, API
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that verifies a caller's claimed identity from a credential before any protected action runs.

Requires
[Identity Proof](LEXICON.md#lexicon-identity-proof)

Reinforces
[Access Control](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-access-control)

Enables
[Identity-Aware Authorization](LEXICON.md#lexicon-identity-aware-authorization)

In tension with
[User Experience](LEXICON.md#lexicon-user-experience)

Conflicts with
[Anonymous Sensitive Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-anonymous-sensitive-access)

Referenced by
[CSRF Protection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-csrf-protection), [Session Management](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-session-management)

Tensions
[Authentication / User Experience](SCHEMA.md#tension-authentication-user-experience)

Distinct from
[Access Control](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-access-control): Authentication verifies who the caller is, while access control decides what that caller may do.

Distinct from
[CSRF Protection](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-csrf-protection): Authentication verifies an identity, while CSRF protection verifies that a request came from the site's own pages.

Distinct from
[Session Management](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-session-management): Authentication verifies a credential once, while session management keeps the result across requests.

Violated by
[Anonymous Sensitive Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-anonymous-sensitive-access)

Detected by
unauthenticated protected endpoints

Measured by
auth coverage

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
route policies, [tests](LEXICON.md#lexicon-tests)

Before

```typescript
const userId = request.headers.get("X-User-ID");
return loadFooFor(userId!);
```

After

```typescript
const credential = requireHeader(request, "Authorization");
const identity = await authenticator.verify(credential);
if (!identity) throw new UnauthorizedError();
return loadFooFor(identity.subject);
```

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

[Least Privilege](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-least-privilege)

Measured by

Enforced by

access-control


After

```typescript
const decision = accessPolicy.evaluate({
  subject: user,
  action: "foo:list",
  resource: { tenantId: request.tenantId },
});
if (!decision.allowed) throw new ForbiddenError();
return fooStore.findAll(request.tenantId);
```

Definition

Distinct from

residual risk score

[Mitigation Plan](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mitigation-plan), [Restrict Exports](LEXICON.md#lexicon-restrict-exports)

Enforced by
review gates

Before

```typescript
shipFooFeature();
```

After

```typescript
const risk = assessRisk(fooFeature, {
  likelihood: 3,
  impact: 5,
  controls: ["rate-limit", "audit", "rollback"],
});
if (risk.residual > riskTolerance) throw new Error("risk not accepted");
shipFooFeature();
```

### Continuous Compliance

- Kind: [capability](SCHEMA.md#kind-capability)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: CI/CD, infrastructure, codebase
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
The ability to check compliance on every change, with automated policy gates and evidence capture.

Requires
[Policy as Code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-policy-as-code), [Evidence Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-evidence-automation)

Reinforces
[Compliance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compliance), [Auditability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-auditability)

Enables
[Ongoing Assurance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ongoing-assurance)

In tension with
[Pipeline Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-pipeline-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Point-in-Time Audit Only](LEXICON.md#lexicon-point-in-time-audit-only)

Referenced by
[Policy as Code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-policy-as-code)

Tensions
[Continuous Compliance / Pipeline Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-continuous-compliance-pipeline-complexity)

Distinct from
[Evidence Automation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-evidence-automation): Continuous compliance checks every change against policy, while evidence automation collects the proof that the checks ran.

Distinct from
[Ongoing Assurance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ongoing-assurance): Continuous compliance is checking on every change, while ongoing assurance is being able to show at any time that controls still work.

Violated by
[Point-in-Time Audit Only](LEXICON.md#lexicon-point-in-time-audit-only)

Detected by
missing automated compliance checks

Measured by
continuous control pass rate

Refactored by
[Automated Enforcement](LEXICON.md#lexicon-automated-enforcement), [Policy as Code](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-policy-as-code)

Enforced by
CI/CD controls

Before

```typescript
runComplianceAuditOncePerYear();
```

After

```typescript
pipeline.on("change", async (change) => {
  const result = await complianceScanner.evaluate(change);
  if (!result.compliant) throw new ComplianceGateError(result.violations);
});
```

### CSRF Protection

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)

- Scope: service, web, security
- Aliases: Cross-Site Request Forgery Protection
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that rejects state-changing requests which lack proof of coming from the site's own pages, such as an anti-forgery token.

Requires
[Request Origin Verification](LEXICON.md#lexicon-request-origin-verification)

Reinforces
[Authentication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-authentication), [Defense in Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-defense-in-depth)

Violated by
[Ambient-Credential Trust](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ambient-credential-trust)

Detected by
no anti-forgery token on mutating endpoints

Measured by
unprotected state-changing endpoint count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
security review

Before

```typescript
app.post("/foo/delete", deleteFoo);
```

After

```typescript
app.post("/foo/delete", verifyCsrfToken(), requireSameSite(), deleteFoo);
```

### Parameterized Queries

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)

A mechanism that sends query text and values to the database separately, so values are never parsed as query syntax.

[Input Validation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-input-validation): Parameterized queries keep values out of query syntax whatever they contain, while input validation checks what values contain before use.

### Session Management

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Security / Privacy / Compliance / Governance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-security-privacy-compliance-governance)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Mandatory for: sensitive systems
- Scope: service, authentication, security
- Layer: [Security Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-security-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that keeps authenticated sessions on the server, with expiry, rotation and revocation, and gives the client only an opaque identifier.

Requires
[Authentication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-authentication)

Reinforces
[Access Control](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-access-control), [Least Privilege](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-least-privilege)

Enables
[Bounded Session Lifetime](LEXICON.md#lexicon-bounded-session-lifetime), [Revocable Access](LEXICON.md#lexicon-revocable-access)

In tension with
[User Convenience](LEXICON.md#lexicon-user-convenience)

Conflicts with
[Immortal Client-Trusted Session](LEXICON.md#lexicon-immortal-client-trusted-session)

Tensions
[Session Management / User Convenience](SCHEMA.md#tension-session-management-user-convenience)

Violated by
[Immortal Client-Trusted Session](LEXICON.md#lexicon-immortal-client-trusted-session)

Detected by
no expiry/rotation/revocation on sessions

Measured by
unbounded-session count

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
security review

Before

```typescript
res.cookie("userId", user.id);
```

After

```typescript
const session = await sessions.create(user.id, {
  ttlMs: 3_600_000,
  rotateOnAuth: true,
});
res.cookie("sid", session.id, {
  httpOnly: true,
  secure: true,
  sameSite: "strict",
});
```

## Codebase / System Architecture Styles

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_ports_and_adapters_architecture["Ports and Adapters Architecture"]
    n_clean_architecture["Clean Architecture"]
    n_layered_architecture["Layered Architecture"]
    n_component_based_architecture["Component-Based Architecture"]
    n_package_by_feature["Package by Feature"]
    n_microservices["Microservices"]
    n_monolith_architecture["Monolith Architecture"]
    n_pipes_and_filters["Pipes and Filters"]
    n_service_oriented_architecture["Service-Oriented Architecture"]
    n_space_based_architecture["Space-Based Architecture"]
    n_ports_and_adapters_architecture --> n_clean_architecture
```

### Ports and Adapters Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Codebase / System Architecture Styles](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-codebase-system-architecture-styles)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: application, service, component
- Aliases: Hexagonal Architecture, Ports and Adapters
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of keeping a domain core free of framework and data types, with every external dependency behind a port the application owns and implemented by an adapter outside it.

Requires
[Ports](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ports), [Adapters](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adapters), [Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Domain Core](LEXICON.md#lexicon-domain-core)

Reinforces
[Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability), [Clean Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-clean-architecture)

Enables
[Infrastructure Independence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-infrastructure-independence), [External System Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-external-system-isolation)

In tension with
[Boilerplate](LEXICON.md#lexicon-boilerplate), [Initial Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-initial-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Framework Leakage](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-framework-leakage)

Referenced by
[Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion)

Tensions
[Ports and Adapters Architecture / Boilerplate](SCHEMA.md#tension-boilerplate-ports-and-adapters-architecture), [Ports and Adapters Architecture / Initial Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-initial-complexity-ports-and-adapters-architecture)

Distinct from
[Clean Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-clean-architecture): Ports and adapters isolates the core behind ports, while clean architecture arranges concentric layers whose dependencies point inward.

Violated by
[Concrete Coupling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concrete-coupling), [Framework Leakage](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-framework-leakage)

Detected by
inward/outward dependency violations, dependency direction violations

Measured by
adapter coverage, boundary purity, core purity score

Refactored by
[Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port), [Extract Adapter](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-adapter), [Move Framework Outward](LEXICON.md#lexicon-move-framework-outward)

Enforced by
layer dependency rules, architecture tests

Before

```typescript
class FooService {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return sql.query("insert into foo values (?)", foo);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
interface SaveFooPort {
  save(foo: Foo): Promise<void>;
}
class FooService {
  constructor(private readonly port: SaveFooPort) {}
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return this.port.save(foo);
  }
}
class SqlFooAdapter implements SaveFooPort {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return sqlFooStore.save(foo);
  }
}
```

How it is checked

Checked by
layer dependency rules, architecture tests

Population
Every import, package and service boundary the style's dependency rules range over

Freshness
A verdict stands until an import, a package boundary or a deployment unit changes

Refusal
The layer or dependency rule fails the build on an edge the style forbids

Observation
The import graph and the deployment topology, read from source and configuration

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The style's declared dependency rules, which every import and deployment edge conforms to

Depends on
[Ports](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ports), [Adapters](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adapters), [Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Domain Core](LEXICON.md#lexicon-domain-core), [Replaceability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replaceability), [Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability), [Clean Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-clean-architecture), [Infrastructure Independence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-infrastructure-independence), [External System Isolation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-external-system-isolation)

Shape it refuses
[Framework Leakage](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-framework-leakage)

### Clean Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Codebase / System Architecture Styles](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-codebase-system-architecture-styles)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: application, system
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of concentric layers in which source dependencies point only inward, towards the use cases and entities.

Requires
[Dependency Rule](LEXICON.md#lexicon-dependency-rule), [Use Cases](LEXICON.md#lexicon-use-cases), [Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-boundaries)

Reinforces
[Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Testability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-testability)

Enables
[Framework Independence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-framework-independence)

In tension with
[Boilerplate](LEXICON.md#lexicon-boilerplate)

Conflicts with
[Layer Leakage](LEXICON.md#lexicon-layer-leakage)

Referenced by
[Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-inversion), [Ports and Adapters Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ports-and-adapters-architecture)

Tensions
[Clean Architecture / Boilerplate](SCHEMA.md#tension-boilerplate-clean-architecture)

Violated by
[Layer Leakage](LEXICON.md#lexicon-layer-leakage)

Detected by
dependency rule violations

Measured by
inward dependency compliance

Refactored by
[Move Logic to the Domain](LEXICON.md#lexicon-move-logic-to-the-domain), [Extract Interface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-interface), [Extract Adapter](LEXICON.md#lexicon-extract-adapter)

Enforced by
dependency graph rules

Before

```typescript
class FooController {
  async create(request: Request) {
    return orm.foo.create(await request.json());
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
interface CreateFooGateway {
  save(foo: Foo): Promise<void>;
}
class CreateFooInteractor {
  constructor(private readonly gateway: CreateFooGateway) {}
  execute(input: CreateFooInput) {
    return this.gateway.save(Foo.create(input));
  }
}
class FooController {
  constructor(private readonly useCase: CreateFooInteractor) {}
}
```

dependency graph rules

### Layered Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Codebase / System Architecture Styles](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-codebase-system-architecture-styles)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: application, system
- Aliases: N-Tier Architecture

Details

Definition

Requires

Tensions

Violated by
[Layer Skipping](LEXICON.md#lexicon-layer-skipping)

Detected by
forbidden layer imports

Measured by
layer violation count

Refactored by
[Move Behavior to Its Owner](LEXICON.md#lexicon-move-behavior-to-its-owner), [Introduce Port](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-port)

Enforced by
layer rules

Before

```typescript
function createFoo(request: Request) {
  return sql.query("insert into foo values (?)", JSON.parse(request.body));
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooController {
  constructor(private readonly service: FooService) {}
}
class FooService {
  constructor(private readonly repository: FooRepository) {}
}
class SqlFooRepository implements FooRepository {
  save(foo: Foo) {
    return fooTable.insert(foo);
  }
}
```

### Component-Based Architecture

- Kind: [style](SCHEMA.md#kind-style)
- Category: [Codebase / System Architecture Styles](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-codebase-system-architecture-styles)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)

- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A convention of building a system from components that declare what they export and what they require.

Requires
[Component Boundaries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-component-boundaries), [Contracts](LEXICON.md#lexicon-contracts)

Measured by

Refactored by

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
const app = {
  createFoo,
  createBar,
  renderFoo,
  saveBar,
  publishBaz,
};
```

After

```typescript
const fooComponent = defineComponent({
  name: "foo",
  exports: { createFoo, FooView },
  requires: { FooStore, EventBus },
});
```

Measured by

Refactored by

Enforced by

Before

```typescript
class SharedApplication {
  createFoo(foo: Foo) {
    return sharedDb.insert("foo", foo);
  }
  createBar(bar: Bar) {
    return sharedDb.insert("bar", bar);
  }
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooService {
  constructor(
    private readonly fooStore: FooStore,
    private readonly outbox: Outbox,
  ) {}
  create(foo: Foo) {
    return transact(() => [
      this.fooStore.save(foo),
      this.outbox.append(fooCreated(foo)),
    ]);
  }
}
class BarService {
  constructor(private readonly barStore: BarStore) {}
}
```

```typescript
const filters: FooFilter[] = [parseFoo, cleanFoo, enrichFoo];
```

## Coordination Surfaces

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_stated_invariant["Stated Invariant"]
    n_derived_record_state["Derived Record State"]
    n_declared_subject["Declared Subject"]
    n_write_barrier["Write Barrier"]
    n_operand_free_outcome_surface["Operand-Free Outcome Surface"]
    n_projection_channel["Projection Channel"]
    n_two_direction_index["Two-Direction Index"]
    n_independent_lifetime_axes["Independent Lifetime Axes"]
    n_section_lifetime_divergence["Section Lifetime Divergence"]
    n_write_scope_and_read_population["Write Scope and Read Population"]
    n_read_time_join["Read-Time Join"]
    n_one_sided_liveness["One-Sided Liveness"]
    n_reversible_channel_encoding["Reversible Channel Encoding"]
    n_declare_before_read_order["Declare-Before-Read Order"]
    n_period_decided_disposition["Period-Decided Disposition"]
    n_derived_party_count["Derived Party Count"]
    n_fan_in_ceiling["Fan-In Ceiling"]
    n_state_arity_limit["State-Arity Limit"]
    n_carrier_and_payload_split["Carrier and Payload Split"]
    n_joinable_mandated_field["Joinable Mandated Field"]
    n_single_aggregate["Single Aggregate"]
    n_contradicted_invariant["Contradicted Invariant"]

    n_narrowed_aggregate["Narrowed Aggregate"]
    n_cyclic_tiebreak["Cyclic Tiebreak"]
    n_destructive_closure["Destructive Closure"]
    n_hand_kept_index["Hand-Kept Index"]
    n_stated_invariant --x n_contradicted_invariant
    n_derived_record_state --x n_written_status_marker
    n_operand_free_outcome_surface --> n_stated_invariant
    n_operand_free_outcome_surface --x n_contradicted_invariant
    n_two_direction_index --x n_hand_kept_index
```

### Stated Invariant

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: topology, coordination
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that an invariant a topology relies on is written with its property in a form that could be false, the set it ranges over, the parties it binds and the thing that would object if it stopped holding.

Requires
[Coordination Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-surface)

Reinforces
[Fitness Functions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fitness-functions)

Enables
[Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Contradicted Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-contradicted-invariant)

Referenced by
[Operand-Free Outcome Surface](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-operand-free-outcome-surface)

Expressed in the grammar by
[INVARIANT](GRAMMAR.md#pag-keyword-invariant), [invariant_record](GRAMMAR.md#pag-production-invariant-record), [invariant_block](GRAMMAR.md#pag-production-invariant-block)

Violated by
[Unobjected Invariant](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unobjected-invariant), [Unreceived Invariant](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unreceived-invariant)

Detected by
an invariant with no objector, or one that names no set or no bound party

Measured by
invariants stated without an objector and not marked unheld

Refactored by
[Name the Objector](LEXICON.md#lexicon-name-the-objector), [Mark the Invariant Unheld](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mark-the-invariant-unheld)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
every surface has one writer → nothing counts writers → a second writer lands and every guarantee resting on the first still reads as sound
```

After

```text
property: one writer per record → set: every record on a coordination surface → parties: every writer → objector: a check failing a record whose fence names two writers
```

How it is checked

Checked by
coordination review

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Coordination Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-surface), [Fitness Functions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fitness-functions), [Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

Shape it refuses
[Contradicted Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-contradicted-invariant)

### Derived Record State

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: record, coordination
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a record's state is a query over the edges it carries, open while its satisfying artifact is unresolved, blocked while a blocker is open and absorbed once the artifact exists, so no party writes a state.

Requires
[Coordination Record](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-record), [Acknowledger](LEXICON.md#lexicon-acknowledger)

Reinforces
[Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth)

Enables
[Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Written Status Marker](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-written-status-marker)

Distinct from
[Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth): Derived record state applies one owning source to a record's status, while a single source of truth covers any fact, rule or configuration value.

Violated by
[Written Status Marker](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-written-status-marker)

Detected by
a record carrying a state that its edges no longer support

Measured by
records whose written state differs from the derived one

Refactored by
[Derive State from Edges](LEXICON.md#lexicon-derive-state-from-edges)

Enforced by
the coordination closure check, which refuses a judgment closure that cites an artifact and an artifact closure that cites none

Before

```text
a record reads status: done → its artifact was later deleted → the marker still asserts done
```

After

```text
the record cites satisfied-by: <artifact> → the artifact resolves: absorbed → the artifact is gone: open, with no field anyone has to remember to change
```

How it is checked

Checked by
the coordination closure check, which refuses a judgment closure that cites an artifact and an artifact closure that cites none

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Coordination Record](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-record), [Acknowledger](LEXICON.md#lexicon-acknowledger), [Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth), [Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

### Declared Subject

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: record, identity
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that a record carries an allocated id and a declared subject key as two fields, so a moved surface keeps the id, a renamed subject keeps the key, and two records sharing a key are a finding.

Requires
[Coordination Record](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-record)

Reinforces
[Stable Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stable-identity)

Enables
[Rederivation Detection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rederivation-detection)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
none

Distinct from
[Stable Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stable-identity): A declared subject keeps a record's id and its subject as two fields that survive different renames, while stable identity requires only that one identifier last the entity's lifetime.

Violated by
[Location-Derived Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-location-derived-identity)

Detected by
a record whose id changes when its surface moves, or two records about one subject

Measured by
records sharing a subject key

Refactored by
[Allocate Identity Once](LEXICON.md#lexicon-allocate-identity-once), [Declare the Subject Beside the Id](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-the-subject-beside-the-id)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
record id = <surface-path>-<ordinal> → the surface moves → every id changes and every edge citing one dangles
```

After

```text
id = <surface-key>-<ordinal>, allocated once → subject = <declared> → a second record declaring the same subject is reported
```

How it is checked

Checked by
coordination review

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Coordination Record](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-record), [Stable Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stable-identity), [Rederivation Detection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rederivation-detection)

Shape it refuses
Not answered

### Write Barrier

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: surface, concurrency
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets a planned exclusive write to a shared surface proceed only once every peer is observed parked, beside a compare-and-swap that covers every other write.

Requires
[Coordination Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-surface)

Reinforces
[Optimistic Locking](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-optimistic-locking)

Enables
[Single-Writer Coordination](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-writer-coordination)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Lost Update](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-lost-update)

Expressed in the grammar by
[refusal_line](GRAMMAR.md#pag-production-refusal-line)

Violated by
[Whole-Surface Rewrite](LEXICON.md#lexicon-whole-surface-rewrite)

Detected by
content a peer wrote missing after an exclusive write that reported success

Measured by
exclusive writes taken without every peer observed parked

Refactored by
[Hold the Barrier for Planned Writes](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hold-the-barrier-for-planned-writes), [Optimistic Locking](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-optimistic-locking)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
a tool rewrites the board whole → a peer's record written a moment earlier is gone → every check passes
```

After

```text
planned rewrite → wait until every peer is parked → write → any other write: re-read, compare its own span, refuse with the diff on an overlap
```

coordination review

Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Coordination Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-surface), [Optimistic Locking](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-optimistic-locking), [Single-Writer Coordination](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-writer-coordination)

Shape it refuses
[Lost Update](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-lost-update)

### Operand-Free Outcome Surface

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: surface, authorship
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that a surface carrying one jointly authored product declares that one writer per record has no operand there, and settles a collision by announcement and by each author cutting its own duplicate.

Requires
[Outcome Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-outcome-surface)

Reinforces
[Stated Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stated-invariant)

Enables
[Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Contradicted Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-contradicted-invariant)

Distinct from
[Stated Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stated-invariant): An operand-free outcome surface declares where one invariant cannot apply, while a stated invariant is the form every invariant is written in.

Violated by
[Assumed Single Writer](LEXICON.md#lexicon-assumed-single-writer), [Fenced Joint Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-fenced-joint-surface)

Detected by
an outcome surface with no declaration that the invariant has no operand there

Measured by
outcome surfaces missing the declaration

Refactored by
[Declare the Missing Operand](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-the-missing-operand), [Settle Collisions by Announcement](LEXICON.md#lexicon-settle-collisions-by-announcement)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
a class statement written by several parties → the one-writer invariant is assumed to hold → nothing objects when two parties write the same clause
```

After

```text
the surface declares: one writer per record has no operand here → a collision is announced → each author cuts its own duplicate
```

coordination review

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Outcome Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-outcome-surface), [Stated Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-stated-invariant), [Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

Shape it refuses
[Contradicted Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-contradicted-invariant)

### Projection Channel

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)

- Scope: context, reader
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that the projection a host injects into every bounded reader is refreshed in the same change as the fact it carries, in a shape a check reads.

[Host Projection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-host-projection), [Bounded Reader](LEXICON.md#lexicon-bounded-reader)

none

none

Violated by

Detected by
a projection line that disagrees with the surface it summarizes

Measured by
changes that moved a projected fact without the projection

Refactored by
[Refresh the Projection in the Same Change](LEXICON.md#lexicon-refresh-the-projection-in-the-same-change), [Check the Projection's Shape](LEXICON.md#lexicon-check-the-projection-s-shape)

Enforced by
coordination review

```text
a seat goes inactive on the board → the injected line still lists it → every spawned reader plans around a party that is gone
```

### Two-Direction Index

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: index, directory
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that generates an index from the directory on every run and checks it both ways, reporting an entry with no file and a file with no entry, with every scan independent of depth.

Requires
[Coordination Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordination-surface)

Reinforces
[Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth)

Enables
[Traceable Guarantee](LEXICON.md#lexicon-traceable-guarantee)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Hand-Kept Index](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-hand-kept-index)

Violated by
[Hand-Kept Index](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-hand-kept-index), [One-Way Index Check](LEXICON.md#lexicon-one-way-index-check)

Detected by
an index entry that resolves to no file, or a file no entry names

Measured by
index entries and files missing their counterpart

Refactored by
[Generate the Index from the Directory](LEXICON.md#lexicon-generate-the-index-from-the-directory), [Check Both Directions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-check-both-directions)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
the agent index is edited by hand → a seat is added without an entry → the scan covers fewer seats than it claims
```

After

```text
the index is generated from the directory → an entry with no file fails → a file with no entry fails
```

### Independent Lifetime Axes

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: surface, lifetime
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a surface's lifetime is declared on three independent axes, retention, mutability and removal authority, each taking a value from a closed set, so no single word stands for all three.

Requires
[Retention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retention), [Mutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mutability), [Removal Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-removal-authority)

Reinforces
[Immutability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-immutability)

Enables
[Governed Removal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-removal)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Destructive Closure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-destructive-closure)

Referenced by
[Section Lifetime Divergence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-section-lifetime-divergence)

Contracts
[Convergence Walk](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-convergence-walk), [Lifetime Resolution](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-lifetime-resolution)

Distinct from
[Immutability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-immutability): Independent lifetime axes declare mutability as one of three questions about a surface, while immutability is the single rule that a value never changes after it is created.

Violated by
[Single-Word Lifetime](LEXICON.md#lexicon-single-word-lifetime)

Detected by
a surface whose lifetime names retention alone

Measured by
surfaces missing a value on any axis

Refactored by
[Declare All Three Lifetime Axes](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-all-three-lifetime-axes)

Enforced by
the coordination declaration check, which reports a mechanism named for a lifetime axis that never reads that axis

Before

```text
lifetime: deleted on close → a sweep implements it faithfully → the argument behind a ruling is destroyed
```

After

```text
retention: kept → mutability: frozen → removal authority: nobody → closing moves the surface to the archive
```

How it is checked

Checked by
the coordination declaration check, which reports a mechanism named for a lifetime axis that never reads that axis

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Retention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retention), [Mutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mutability), [Removal Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-removal-authority), [Immutability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-immutability), [Governed Removal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-removal)

[Destructive Closure](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-destructive-closure)

### Section Lifetime Divergence

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: surface, section
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that a file states a default lifetime and each section declares only the axes on which it differs, since the narrower unit is the more constrained one.

Requires
[Retention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retention), [Mutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mutability)

Reinforces
[Independent Lifetime Axes](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-independent-lifetime-axes)

Enables
[Governed Removal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-removal)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
none

Violated by
[File-Wide Lifetime](LEXICON.md#lexicon-file-wide-lifetime)

Detected by
an operation permitted by the file's lifetime acting on a section whose own lifetime forbids it

Measured by
divergent sections carrying no declaration

Refactored by
[Declare the File Default](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-the-file-default), [Declare Each Divergent Section](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-each-divergent-section)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
a document declares owner-rewritable → its contract block is rewritten by a sweep that the file's word allowed
```

After

```text
file default: owner-rewritable → contract block: mutability frozen → the sweep skips the block
```

coordination review

Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

[Retention](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retention), [Mutability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-mutability), [Independent Lifetime Axes](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-independent-lifetime-axes), [Governed Removal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-removal)

### Write Scope and Read Population

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: run, invocation
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a run declares the paths it writes and publishes the set it read as two declarations, because collision is decided by the first and a published result's validity by the second.

Requires
[Write Scope](LEXICON.md#lexicon-write-scope), [Read Population](LEXICON.md#lexicon-read-population)

Reinforces
[Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism)

Enables
[Shared Invocation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-invocation)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
none

Referenced by
[Read-Time Join](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-read-time-join)

Expressed in the grammar by
[population_clause](GRAMMAR.md#pag-production-population-clause)

Distinct from
[Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism): Write scope and read population separate what a run touches from what it read, while determinism requires that the same inputs produce the same result.

Violated by
[Conflated Scope](LEXICON.md#lexicon-conflated-scope)

Detected by
a run that reads more than it writes and publishes only its write scope

Measured by
runs publishing no read population

Refactored by
[Declare the Write Scope](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-the-write-scope), [Publish the Read Population](LEXICON.md#lexicon-publish-the-read-population)

Enforced by
the coordination writer check, which fails a writer a run reaches outside the sanctioned set

Before

```text
a run declares scope: <subtree> → it also reads a sibling tree → a later caller reuses its result for the sibling and gets a verdict nobody measured
```

After

```text
write scope: <subtree> → read population: <subtree> + <sibling> → the collision test reads the first, the coverage test reads the second
```

How it is checked

Checked by
the coordination writer check, which fails a writer a run reaches outside the sanctioned set

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Write Scope](LEXICON.md#lexicon-write-scope), [Read Population](LEXICON.md#lexicon-read-population), [Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism), [Shared Invocation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-invocation)

Shape it refuses
Not answered

### Read-Time Join

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: run, invocation
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets a caller whose question a live declared scope already covers read that run's published result and its standing, writing nothing, so it cannot deadlock, be orphaned or need cleanup.

Requires
[Joiner](LEXICON.md#lexicon-joiner), [Read Population](LEXICON.md#lexicon-read-population)

Reinforces
[Write Scope and Read Population](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-write-scope-and-read-population)

Enables
[Shared Invocation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-invocation)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
none

Contracts
[Invocation Join](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-invocation-join)

Distinct from
[Joiner](LEXICON.md#lexicon-joiner): A read-time join is the mechanism that serves a covered question from a published result, while a joiner is the caller that uses it.

Violated by
[Attached Second Caller](LEXICON.md#lexicon-attached-second-caller), [Duplicate Covered Run](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicate-covered-run)

Detected by
two runs over one covered question, or a caller waiting on another run's handle

Measured by
duplicate runs a live scope covered

Refactored by
[Test Coverage First](LEXICON.md#lexicon-test-coverage-first), [Join by Reading the Published Result](LEXICON.md#lexicon-join-by-reading-the-published-result)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
a second caller starts the same measurement → both write the same report → the second waits on the first's lock
```

After

```text
caller → does a live scope cover the question? yes: read the published result and its standing, write nothing → no: start, and only then enter the collision comparison
```

Checked by
coordination review

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

Freshness
A verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes

Refusal
The coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes

Observation
Each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

Depends on
[Joiner](LEXICON.md#lexicon-joiner), [Read Population](LEXICON.md#lexicon-read-population), [Write Scope and Read Population](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-write-scope-and-read-population), [Shared Invocation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-invocation)

### One-Sided Liveness

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: process, liveness
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a process's absence proves it is dead while its presence proves nothing, so liveness is derived once, from the witness first and from a generous window only where the witness cannot decide.

Requires
[Liveness Witness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-liveness-witness)

Reinforces
[Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism)

Enables
[Shared Invocation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shared-invocation)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
none

Distinct from
[Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism): One-sided liveness decides what a process's presence can prove, while determinism requires that the same inputs produce the same result.

Violated by
[Presence as Liveness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-presence-as-liveness), [Per-Consumer Liveness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-per-consumer-liveness)

Detected by
two consumers of one liveness question reaching different answers

Measured by
liveness derivations outside the single one

Refactored by
[Derive Liveness Once](LEXICON.md#lexicon-derive-liveness-once), [Witness First](LEXICON.md#lexicon-witness-first), [Window Second](LEXICON.md#lexicon-window-second)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
a process id is present → the claim is kept → the id was reused by an unrelated process and the claim never expires
```

After

```text
id absent: dead → id present: undecided → fall to the window, set long, because too short loses a write and too long costs one re-run
```

How it is checked

Checked by
coordination review

Population
Every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries

### Reversible Channel Encoding

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with

Violated by
[Digest-Named Channel](LEXICON.md#lexicon-digest-named-channel)

Detected by
a channel whose name decodes to no scope

Measured by
channels no remover can attribute to a scope

Refactored by

Enforced by


### Period-Decided Disposition

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Coordination Surfaces](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-coordination-surfaces)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: duplicate, derivation
- Layer: [Execution Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-execution-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a duplicate is first counted by its distinguished copies and then read by the period of each derivation edge, so a periodic copy owes a comparator and a one-shot copy is a record whose source is repaired instead.

Requires
[Distinguished Copy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-distinguished-copy), [Derivation Period](LEXICON.md#lexicon-derivation-period)

Contracts
[Duplicate Disposition Walk](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-duplicate-disposition-walk)

Distinct from
[Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth): Period-decided disposition decides what to do with the copies a fact already has, while a single source of truth is the state it restores.

Violated by
[Blanket Collapse](LEXICON.md#lexicon-blanket-collapse)

Detected by
a collapse that removed a copy written once against an earlier state of its source

Measured by
copies collapsed across one-shot edges

Refactored by
[Count Distinguished Copies](LEXICON.md#lexicon-count-distinguished-copies), [Read Each Period](LEXICON.md#lexicon-read-each-period), [Repair the Source](LEXICON.md#lexicon-repair-the-source)

Enforced by
coordination review

Before

```text
a rule stated in code and in several documents → every document copy is rewritten to match → the record of what each surface said when it was written is gone
```

After

```text
one distinguished copy: a direction → every other edge one-shot: diagnose the copies, repair the source → a copy no party reaches: add it
```

## Taxonomy / Classification / Naming

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

### Closed Vocabulary

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: repository, folder, filename
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that every word in a name slot comes from a declared list, and a new word enters the list only by an approved edit.

Requires
[Vocabulary Admission](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-admission), [Rejection Table](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rejection-table)

Reinforces
[Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth), [Ubiquitous Language](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ubiquitous-language)

Enables
[Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability), [Concern-Folder Correspondence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concern-folder-correspondence)

In tension with
[Naming Expressiveness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-naming-expressiveness)

Conflicts with
[Vocabulary Inflation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-inflation), [Nominalized Process Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-nominalized-process-word), [Adjective Slot Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adjective-slot-word), [Plural Subject](LEXICON.md#lexicon-plural-subject), [Measurement Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-measurement-word), [Instance Identifier Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-instance-identifier-word)

Referenced by
[Carrier and Payload Split](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-carrier-and-payload-split), [Positional Slot Resolution](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-positional-slot-resolution), [Agnostic-First Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-agnostic-first-vocabulary), [Guided Vocabulary Refusal](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-guided-vocabulary-refusal), [Sanctioned Generic Subject](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-sanctioned-generic-subject), [Externally Resolved Slot](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-externally-resolved-slot), [Case Dialect](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-case-dialect)

Contracts
[Vocabulary Admission Gate](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-vocabulary-admission-gate), [Taxonomy Kernel](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-taxonomy-kernel)

Tensions
[Closed Vocabulary / Naming Expressiveness](SCHEMA.md#tension-closed-vocabulary-naming-expressiveness)

Distinct from
[Agnostic-First Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-agnostic-first-vocabulary): A closed vocabulary admits a word only by approved edit, while agnostic-first decides which words to admit, domain-neutral roles before domain ones.

Violated by
[Vocabulary Inflation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-inflation)

Detected by
a name slot holding a word absent from its declared array

Measured by
undeclared-word count per governed root

Refactored by
[Rename to a Declared Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rename-to-a-declared-word), [Vocabulary Admission](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-admission)

Enforced by
registry-backed naming gate, developer approval

Before

```text
<container>/managers/foo.manager.ts → neither "managers" nor "manager" is a declared word
```

After

```text
<container>/coordinators/foo.coordinator.ts → the declared concern that already covers the role
```

How it is checked

Checked by
registry-backed naming gate, developer approval

Population
Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file is added, moved or renamed, or a vocabulary or root declaration changes

Refusal
The naming or placement gate fails the lint run on the file, naming the declared word that covers a refused one

Observation
Each path parsed by position against the declared containers, depth cap and closed vocabularies

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: one suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, another refuses a repeated role and a path past the depth cap, and both pass conforming paths

Authoritative side
The declared vocabularies and roots, which every path conforms to, so an undeclared word is an approved edit to the declaration

Depends on
[Vocabulary Admission](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-admission), [Rejection Table](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rejection-table), [Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth), [Ubiquitous Language](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-ubiquitous-language), [Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability), [Concern-Folder Correspondence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concern-folder-correspondence)

Shape it refuses
[Vocabulary Inflation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-inflation), [Nominalized Process Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-nominalized-process-word), [Adjective Slot Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adjective-slot-word), [Plural Subject](LEXICON.md#lexicon-plural-subject), [Measurement Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-measurement-word), [Instance Identifier Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-instance-identifier-word)

### Positional Slot Resolution

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: folder, filename
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that reads each word of a path by the slot it lands in, so the last dot-segment before a file's extension is always its concern and a folder named after a concern tag resolves as the latest role its depth can legally take.

Requires
[Concern Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-tag), [Subject Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subject-slot), [Ordered Role Sequence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ordered-role-sequence)

Reinforces
[Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability)

Enables
[Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-variant-slot), [Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability), [Concern-Folder Correspondence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concern-folder-correspondence)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Concern-Swallowing Compound](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-swallowing-compound), [Free-Form Folder Level](LEXICON.md#lexicon-free-form-folder-level)

Referenced by
[Registry-Held Order](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-registry-held-order), [Case Dialect](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-case-dialect)

Contracts
[Name Projection](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-name-projection)

Distinct from
[Case Dialect](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-case-dialect): Positional slot resolution reads slots from dot-separated segments, while a case dialect reads the same slots from word boundaries in another case.

Distinct from
[Subject Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subject-slot): Positional slot resolution is the reading rule, while the subject slot is one position it reads.

Distinct from
[Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-variant-slot): Positional slot resolution is the reading rule, while the variant slot is one position it reads.

Violated by
[Vocabulary-Bound Reading](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-bound-reading)

Detected by
a filename whose last segment before the extension is not a declared concern tag, or a folder carrying a concern tag's label that the resolver places in the subject role

Measured by
unparseable filename count, and folders whose resolved role differs from the latest legal role for their word

Refactored by
[Split the Compound](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-the-compound), [Move the Tag to the Concern Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-move-the-tag-to-the-concern-slot), [Correct the Resolver](LEXICON.md#lexicon-correct-the-resolver)

Enforced by
filename parser, naming gate, placement gate

Before

```text
foo-registry.ts → one fused word, so neither slot resolves
```

After

```text
foo.registry.ts → subject "foo", concern "registry"; position decides, so a concern word is legal in the subject slot too
```

How it is checked

Checked by
filename parser, naming gate, placement gate

Population
Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file is added, moved or renamed, or a vocabulary or root declaration changes

Refusal
The naming or placement gate fails the lint run on the file, naming the declared word that covers a refused one

Observation
Each path parsed by position against the declared containers, depth cap and closed vocabularies

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: one suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, another refuses a repeated role and a path past the depth cap, and both pass conforming paths

Authoritative side
The declared vocabularies and roots, which every path conforms to, so an undeclared word is an approved edit to the declaration

Depends on
[Concern Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-tag), [Subject Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subject-slot), [Ordered Role Sequence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ordered-role-sequence), [Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability), [Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-variant-slot), [Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability), [Concern-Folder Correspondence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concern-folder-correspondence)

Shape it refuses
[Concern-Swallowing Compound](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-swallowing-compound), [Free-Form Folder Level](LEXICON.md#lexicon-free-form-folder-level)


After

How it is checked

Checked by
placement gate, naming gate

Population
Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file is added, moved or renamed, or a vocabulary or root declaration changes

The naming or placement gate fails the lint run on the file, naming the declared word that covers a refused one

Observation
Each path parsed by position against the declared containers, depth cap and closed vocabularies
