### Glob-Resolvable Tree

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: repository
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that lets one unanchored pattern per concern collect every matching file or folder, at whatever depth it sits.

Requires
[Concern-Folder Correspondence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concern-folder-correspondence)

Reinforces
[Discoverability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discoverability), [Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

Enables
[Shape-Discovered Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shape-discovered-surface)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Concern-Swallowing Compound](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-swallowing-compound)

Referenced by
[Concern-Folder Correspondence](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concern-folder-correspondence), [Declared Jurisdiction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declared-jurisdiction), [Conformance at Creation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-conformance-at-creation)

Contracts
[Discovery Verification](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-discovery-verification)

Distinct from
[Shape-Discovered Surface](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shape-discovered-surface): A glob-resolvable tree is the property that one pattern collects a concern at any depth, while a shape-discovered surface is a consumer that collects by such a pattern.

Violated by
[Depth-Anchored Discovery](LEXICON.md#lexicon-depth-anchored-discovery)

Detected by
a pattern that must enumerate depths to collect one concern

Measured by
depth-anchored pattern count

Refactored by
[Unanchor the Pattern](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unanchor-the-pattern), [Restore the Terminating Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-restore-the-terminating-tag)

Enforced by
aggregator review, placement gate

Before

```text
<root>/*/validators/*.ts and <root>/*/*/validators/*.ts → one pattern per depth, and a new grouping adds another
```

After

```text
**/*.validator.ts for the files, **/validators/ for the folders → two unanchored patterns resolve the concern tree-wide
```

aggregator review, placement gate

### Declared Jurisdiction

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: repository, root, file
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that a naming gate reads from one declaration the roots it governs, the containers and buckets under each, the classes of file exempt from the grammar, and the trees another system authors or resolves by name, which are exempted once and never governed.

Requires
[Governed Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-root), [Container Level](LEXICON.md#lexicon-container-level), [Flat Bucket](LEXICON.md#lexicon-flat-bucket), [Ignore Declaration](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ignore-declaration), [Ecosystem-Fixed Name](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ecosystem-fixed-name), [Structurally Exempt File](LEXICON.md#lexicon-structurally-exempt-file), [Compound Marker](LEXICON.md#lexicon-compound-marker)

Reinforces
[Explicit Boundaries](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-explicit-boundaries), [Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth)

Enables
[Bounded Nesting Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bounded-nesting-depth), [Glob-Resolvable Tree](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-glob-resolvable-tree), [Backward Compatibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backward-compatibility)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Ignore-List Silencing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ignore-list-silencing), [Depth-Relief Container](LEXICON.md#lexicon-depth-relief-container), [Claimed Foreign Tree](LEXICON.md#lexicon-claimed-foreign-tree), [Duplicated Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicated-authority)

Referenced by
[Derived Naming Registry](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-derived-naming-registry)

Contracts
[Taxonomy Jurisdiction](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-taxonomy-jurisdiction), [Container Ladder](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-container-ladder)

Violated by
[Shape-Inferred Jurisdiction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-shape-inferred-jurisdiction), [Ignore-List Silencing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ignore-list-silencing), [Per-Check Exemption List](LEXICON.md#lexicon-per-check-exemption-list)

Detected by
a folder at a governed root that is in neither the container nor the bucket declaration, an ignore entry naming authored source that belongs to no exempt class, or a declared root that holds another system's ownership marker

Measured by
undeclared root-level folder count, ignore entries outside the exempt classes, and exemptions held outside the one upstream declaration

Refactored by
[Declare the Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-the-root), [Place the Folder in an Existing Container](LEXICON.md#lexicon-place-the-folder-in-an-existing-container), [Remove the Ignore Entry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-remove-the-ignore-entry), [Collapse the Exemption Lists](LEXICON.md#lexicon-collapse-the-exemption-lists)

Enforced by
jurisdiction gate, the taxonomy validator, which refuses an ignore entry of wildcards or of a whole extension, and the coordination member's declaration check, which resolves every declared upstream root against the disk and refuses a root carrying a foreign ownership marker

Before

```text
"a folder holding no folders is a bucket" → inferred, so a container that loses its last folder silently reclassifies and its next loose file passes
```

After

```text
containers{<root>: [...]} + specialContainers{<root>: [...]} → both kinds declared; a folder in neither is flagged
```

jurisdiction gate, the taxonomy validator, which refuses an ignore entry of wildcards or of a whole extension, and the coordination member's declaration check, which resolves every declared upstream root against the disk and refuses a root carrying a foreign ownership marker

### Bounded Nesting Depth

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: folder, root
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that a file sits within a fixed number of folders below its governed root, with each folder taking a later role than the one above it.

Requires
[Depth Cap](LEXICON.md#lexicon-depth-cap), [Ordered Role Sequence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ordered-role-sequence)

Reinforces
[Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability)

Enables
[Sideways Overflow](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-sideways-overflow)

In tension with
[Tree Compactness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-tree-compactness)

Conflicts with
[Downward Nesting](LEXICON.md#lexicon-downward-nesting)

Referenced by
[Declared Jurisdiction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declared-jurisdiction), [Sideways Overflow](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-sideways-overflow)

Contracts
[Path Role Walk](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-path-role-walk)

Tensions
[Bounded Nesting Depth / Tree Compactness](SCHEMA.md#tension-bounded-nesting-depth-tree-compactness)

Distinct from
[Backward Compatibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-backward-compatibility): Bounded nesting depth limits a path, while backward compatibility keeps a new version working for old consumers.

Distinct from
[Depth Cap](LEXICON.md#lexicon-depth-cap): Bounded nesting depth joins two conditions on a path, while the depth cap is the first, the number of folders.

Distinct from
[Ordered Role Sequence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ordered-role-sequence): Bounded nesting depth joins two conditions on a path, while the ordered role sequence is the second, the order of roles.

Violated by
[Downward Nesting](LEXICON.md#lexicon-downward-nesting)

Detected by
a path over the cap, or a role repeated or revisited along it

Measured by
over-cap path count

Refactored by
[Take the Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-take-the-variant-slot), [Add a Sibling Subject Folder](LEXICON.md#lexicon-add-a-sibling-subject-folder)

Enforced by
placement gate

Before

```text
<container>/foo/pools/lru/bar.pool.ts → one folder past the cap, and the extra level resolves to no role at all
```

After

```text
<container>/foo/pools/bar.lru.pool.ts → container, subject, concern, in order and at the cap; the discriminator moved into the variant slot
```

placement gate

Depends on
[Depth Cap](LEXICON.md#lexicon-depth-cap), [Ordered Role Sequence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ordered-role-sequence), [Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability), [Sideways Overflow](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-sideways-overflow)

- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: folder, filename
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that resolves a naming collision with the filename's variant slot and resolves breadth with a sibling subject folder.

[Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-variant-slot), [Subject Folder](LEXICON.md#lexicon-subject-folder)

Reinforces
[Bounded Nesting Depth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-bounded-nesting-depth)

Enables
[Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

Violated by
[Downward Nesting](LEXICON.md#lexicon-downward-nesting)

Measured by
nesting-relief count

Refactored by
[Take the Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-take-the-variant-slot), [Add a Sibling Subject Folder](LEXICON.md#lexicon-add-a-sibling-subject-folder)

Enforced by
placement gate, reshape review

```text
<container>/caches/lru/foo.cache.ts beside <container>/caches/fifo/foo.cache.ts → the collision was relieved by a new level
```

After

```text
<container>/caches/foo.lru.cache.ts beside <container>/caches/foo.fifo.cache.ts → relieved by the variant slot, at the same depth
```

### One Concern Per File

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: file
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that each file plays exactly one declared role, and a file that plays two is split.

Requires
[Classification Judgment](LEXICON.md#lexicon-classification-judgment)

Reinforces
[Separation of Concerns](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-separation-of-concerns)

Enables
[Narrowest Concern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-narrowest-concern)

In tension with
none

Referenced by
[Collision Consolidation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-collision-consolidation)

Distinct from
[Collision Consolidation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-collision-consolidation): One concern per file splits a file that plays two roles, while collision consolidation merges two files that play one.

Distinct from
[Narrowest Concern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-narrowest-concern): One concern per file requires a single role, while narrowest concern chooses which declared role names it.

Violated by
[Multi-Role File](LEXICON.md#lexicon-multi-role-file)

Detected by
a file that classifies equally well under two declared concerns

Measured by
split-candidate count

Refactored by
[Split by Responsibility](LEXICON.md#lexicon-split-by-responsibility)

Enforced by
classification review

Before

```text
foo.store.ts → holds the state AND validates every write, so its concern is two words
```

After

```text
foo.store.ts + foo.validator.ts → the ambiguity was the finding; the split is the fix
```

Details

Definition

Requires
[Is-A Test](LEXICON.md#lexicon-is-a-test), [Rejection Table](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rejection-table)

### Guided Vocabulary Refusal

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: repository, vocabulary, tooling
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that answers a refused word with the declared word that covers its role, looked up in an indexed rejection table.

Requires
[Rejection Table](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rejection-table), [Covering Concern](LEXICON.md#lexicon-covering-concern), [Reverse Coverage Resolution](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reverse-coverage-resolution)

Enables

In tension with
none

Conflicts with

Violated by
[Unguided Refusal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-unguided-refusal)

Detected by

Measured by

Refactored by
[Index the Rejection Table by Refused Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-index-the-rejection-table-by-refused-word), [Name the Covering Concern in the Refusal](LEXICON.md#lexicon-name-the-covering-concern-in-the-refusal)

Enforced by
registry-backed naming gate, rejection-table index drift-check

Before

```text
'foo.manager.ts' → "'manager' is not a declared concern tag" → the developer guesses again, and the table that already answered this sits in prose no gate reads
```

After

```text
refused word → rejection-table index → "'manager' is covered by 'coordinator'" → foo.coordinator.ts; coverage is decided by the role a file plays, never by a general-language synonym set
```

registry-backed naming gate, rejection-table index drift-check

### Registry-Held Order

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: filename
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A design rule that load or execution order is held by an import list or a registry, so a filename carries no numeric prefix the grammar would have to parse.

Requires
[Positional Slot Resolution](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-positional-slot-resolution)

Reinforces
[Declarative Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declarative-configuration)

Enables
[Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Numeric Order Prefix](LEXICON.md#lexicon-numeric-order-prefix)

Distinct from
[Declarative Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declarative-configuration): Registry-held order keeps sequence out of filenames, while declarative configuration keeps settings in validated data.

Violated by
[Numeric Order Prefix](LEXICON.md#lexicon-numeric-order-prefix)

Detected by
a filename whose first segment is a number

Measured by
numerically prefixed filenames

Refactored by
[Move the Order into the Registry](LEXICON.md#lexicon-move-the-order-into-the-registry), [Drop the Prefix](LEXICON.md#lexicon-drop-the-prefix)

Enforced by
naming gate

Before

```text
01-setup.step.ts, 02-build.step.ts → inserting a step renumbers every name after it
```

After

```text
setup.step.ts, build.step.ts, and the order held once in the registry that runs them
```

How it is checked

Checked by
naming gate

Population
Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file is added, moved or renamed, or a vocabulary or root declaration changes

Refusal
The naming or placement gate fails the lint run on the file, naming the declared word that covers a refused one

Observation
Each path parsed by position against the declared containers, depth cap and closed vocabularies

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: one suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, another refuses a repeated role and a path past the depth cap, and both pass conforming paths

Authoritative side
The declared vocabularies and roots, which every path conforms to, so an undeclared word is an approved edit to the declaration

Depends on
[Positional Slot Resolution](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-positional-slot-resolution), [Declarative Configuration](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-declarative-configuration), [Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

Shape it refuses
[Numeric Order Prefix](LEXICON.md#lexicon-numeric-order-prefix)

### Externally Resolved Slot

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: root, filename, vocabulary
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that resolves a name slot whose words another source owns against that source, whether an index that allocates identities, an upstream key set or a field the file itself carries, so the closed vocabulary never holds a copy of them.

Requires
[Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-variant-slot), [Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary)

Reinforces
[Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth), [Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism)

Enables
[Stable Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stable-identity), [Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Vocabulary Inflation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-inflation), [Duplicated Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicated-authority)

Violated by
[Copied Slot Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-copied-slot-word)

Detected by
a vocabulary entry that mirrors a row of an allocating index, or a corpus file whose facet segment differs from the facet its own field declares

Measured by
slot words held both in the vocabulary and in the source that owns them

Refactored by
[Resolve the Slot Against Its Source](LEXICON.md#lexicon-resolve-the-slot-against-its-source), [Remove the Copies](LEXICON.md#lexicon-remove-the-copies)

Enforced by
the coordination member's slot check, which resolves a seat letter against the index that allocates it

Before

```text
each new seat letter is added to the variants array → the array and the index disagree as soon as one moves
```

After

```text
the variant slot resolves against the index that allocates letters → a new seat needs no vocabulary edit
```

How it is checked

Checked by
the coordination member's slot check, which resolves a seat letter against the index that allocates it

Population
Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file is added, moved or renamed, or a vocabulary or root declaration changes

Refusal
The naming or placement gate fails the lint run on the file, naming the declared word that covers a refused one

Observation
Each path parsed by position against the declared containers, depth cap and closed vocabularies

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: one suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, another refuses a repeated role and a path past the depth cap, and both pass conforming paths

Authoritative side
The declared vocabularies and roots, which every path conforms to, so an undeclared word is an approved edit to the declaration

Depends on
[Variant Slot](LEXICON.md#lexicon-variant-slot), [Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Single Source of Truth](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-single-source-of-truth), [Determinism](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-determinism), [Stable Identity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-stable-identity), [Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

Shape it refuses
[Vocabulary Inflation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-vocabulary-inflation), [Duplicated Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicated-authority)

### Case Dialect

- Kind: [mechanism](SCHEMA.md#kind-mechanism)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: filename
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A mechanism that binds file extensions to the case their language names files in and reads the same subject, variant and concern slots from the stem's word boundaries.

Requires
[Word-Boundary Case](LEXICON.md#lexicon-word-boundary-case), [Positional Slot Resolution](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-positional-slot-resolution)

Reinforces
[Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Portability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-portability)

Enables
[Glob Resolvability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-glob-resolvability)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Concern-Swallowing Compound](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-swallowing-compound)

Contracts
[Dialect Resolution](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-dialect-resolution)

Violated by
[Per-Language Vocabulary](LEXICON.md#lexicon-per-language-vocabulary)

Detected by
a dialect file whose trailing words are not a declared concern tag, or a dialect naming a case no splitter reads

Measured by
dialect files that do not resolve to three declared slots

Refactored by
[Declare the Dialect](LEXICON.md#lexicon-declare-the-dialect), [Rename to the Case's Word Run](LEXICON.md#lexicon-rename-to-the-case-s-word-run)

Enforced by
naming gate, which parses a dialect's word run, and the taxonomy validator, which refuses a case no splitter reads

Before

```text
a language that names files in pascal case falls outside the grammar, so its files are ignored or forced into dotted kebab names its tools do not find
```

After

```text
SessionRefreshValidator.<ext> under a pascal dialect → words session, refresh, validator → subject session, variant refresh, concern validator, and its folder stays kebab
```

How it is checked

Checked by
naming gate, which parses a dialect's word run, and the taxonomy validator, which refuses a case no splitter reads

Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

Freshness

### Root Spine Files

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: root
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that a governed root carries only its entry document and its accumulators at the root, and every other file sits in a concern folder.

Requires
[Governed Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-root), [Concern Folder](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concern-folder)

Reinforces
[Placement Predictability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-placement-predictability)

Enables
[Discoverability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-discoverability)

In tension with
none

Conflicts with
[Free-Form Folder Level](LEXICON.md#lexicon-free-form-folder-level)

Distinct from
[Governed Root](LEXICON.md#lexicon-governed-root): Root spine files limit which files may sit at a governed root, while the governed root is the declaration that brings a tree under the taxonomy.

Violated by
[Loose Root File](LEXICON.md#lexicon-loose-root-file)

Detected by
a loose file at a governed root

Measured by
loose root files

Refactored by
[Move the File into Its Concern Folder](LEXICON.md#lexicon-move-the-file-into-its-concern-folder)

Enforced by
placement gate

Before

```text
<root>/notes.ts beside <root>/README.md → the loose file resolves to no role
```

After

```text
<root>/README.md and the underscore-marked accumulators stay; every other file moves to <root>/<container>/<concern>/
```

How it is checked

placement gate

Every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies

## Transactions / State / Concurrency

Every principle in this category is listed as a record. Each record carries its kind, its severity, the scopes it applies at and the layer it lives in, then the edge relations that join it to other records, the records that point back at it, the contracts that answer to it and the tensions it takes part in. The descriptors say how it is violated, detected, measured, repaired and enforced. Where the record carries one, an exemplar shows the shape before and after the principle is applied.

Relations diagram

The relations inside this category.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    n_idempotency["Idempotency"]
    n_atomicity["Atomicity"]
    n_acid["ACID"]
    n_transaction_boundary["Transaction Boundary"]
    n_unit_of_work_pattern["Unit of Work Pattern"]
    n_consistency["Consistency"]
    n_isolation["Isolation"]
    n_concurrency_control["Concurrency Control"]
    n_optimistic_locking["Optimistic Locking"]
    n_pessimistic_locking["Pessimistic Locking"]
    n_state_isolation["State Isolation"]
    n_controlled_side_effects["Controlled Side Effects"]
    n_petri_nets["Petri Nets"]
    n_atomicity --> n_transaction_boundary
    n_atomicity --> n_consistency
    n_acid --> n_atomicity
    n_acid --> n_consistency
    n_acid --> n_isolation
    n_transaction_boundary --> n_atomicity
    n_transaction_boundary --> n_unit_of_work_pattern
    n_unit_of_work_pattern --> n_transaction_boundary
    n_unit_of_work_pattern --> n_atomicity
    n_unit_of_work_pattern --> n_consistency
    n_isolation --> n_concurrency_control
    n_concurrency_control --> n_isolation
    n_optimistic_locking --> n_concurrency_control
    n_pessimistic_locking --> n_isolation
```

### Idempotency

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Transactions / State / Concurrency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-transactions-state-concurrency)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: API, command, message handler
- Aliases: Idempotence
- Layer: [Atomic Boundary](SCHEMA.md#layer-atomic-boundary)

Details

Definition
A design rule that repeating an operation with the same input has the same effect as running it once.

Requires
[Idempotency Key or Deterministic Operation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-idempotency-key-or-deterministic-operation)

Reinforces
[Retry Safety](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retry-safety), [Event-Driven Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-driven-architecture)

Enables
[Safe Retries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-retries)

In tension with
[State Tracking](LEXICON.md#lexicon-state-tracking)

Conflicts with
[Non-Repeatable Side Effects](LEXICON.md#lexicon-non-repeatable-side-effects)

Referenced by
[Event-Driven Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-driven-architecture), [Eventual Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-eventual-consistency), [Saga Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-saga-pattern), [Retry Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-retry-pattern), [Canonicalization](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-canonicalization)

Tensions
[Idempotency / State Tracking](SCHEMA.md#tension-idempotency-state-tracking)

Violated by
[Non-Idempotent Operation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-non-idempotent-operation), [Duplicate Side Effects](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicate-side-effects)

Detected by
side-effectful handlers without deduplication

Measured by
duplicate-effect defect rate

Refactored by
[Idempotency Key](LEXICON.md#lexicon-idempotency-key), [Idempotent Consumer](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-idempotent-consumer)

Enforced by
retry tests, API policy

Before

```typescript
app.post("/foo", async (request) => fooStore.create(await request.json()));
```

After

```typescript
app.post("/foo", async (request) => {
  const key = requireHeader(request, "Idempotency-Key");
  const body = await request.json();
  return idempotency.execute(key, () => fooStore.create(body));
});
```

How it is checked

Checked by
retry tests, API policy

Population
Every multi-step write, shared mutable state and retried side effect

Freshness
A verdict stands until the write path, the isolation level or the concurrency model changes

Refusal
The transaction or concurrency test fails a write path that loses an update, commits partially or repeats an effect

Observation
Outcomes of concurrent and retried runs, plus the transaction boundaries read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The transaction boundary and the isolation level, which every write path conforms to

Depends on
[Idempotency Key or Deterministic Operation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-idempotency-key-or-deterministic-operation), [Retry Safety](LEXICON.md#lexicon-retry-safety), [Event-Driven Architecture](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-event-driven-architecture), [Safe Retries](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-retries)

Shape it refuses
[Non-Repeatable Side Effects](LEXICON.md#lexicon-non-repeatable-side-effects)

### Atomicity

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)
- Category: [Transactions / State / Concurrency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-transactions-state-concurrency)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: transaction, operation, workflow
- Layer: [Atomic Boundary](SCHEMA.md#layer-atomic-boundary)

Details

Definition
A design rule that the steps of a state change either all take effect or none do.

Requires
[Transaction Boundary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-transaction-boundary)

Reinforces
[Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness)

Enables
[All-or-Nothing State Change](LEXICON.md#lexicon-all-or-nothing-state-change)

In tension with
[Distributed Scalability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-distributed-scalability)

Conflicts with
[Partial Commit](LEXICON.md#lexicon-partial-commit)

Referenced by
[ACID](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-acid), [Transaction Boundary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-transaction-boundary), [Unit of Work Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-unit-of-work-pattern)

Contracts
[Atomic Boundary](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-atomic-boundary)

Tensions
[Atomicity / Distributed Scalability](SCHEMA.md#tension-atomicity-distributed-scalability)

Violated by
[Partial Commit](LEXICON.md#lexicon-partial-commit)

Detected by
multi-step writes without transaction/compensation

Measured by
partial failure rate

Refactored by
[Introduce Transaction Boundary](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-transaction-boundary), [Saga Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-saga-pattern), [Compensating Transaction](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-compensating-transaction)

Enforced by
transaction tests

Before

```typescript
await fooStore.remove(from, foo.id);
await fooStore.add(to, foo.id);
```

After

```typescript
await database.transaction(async (tx) => {
  await tx.foos.remove(from, foo.id);
  await tx.foos.add(to, foo.id);
});
```

Checked by
transaction tests

Every multi-step write, shared mutable state and retried side effect

Freshness
A verdict stands until the write path, the isolation level or the concurrency model changes

Refusal
The transaction or concurrency test fails a write path that loses an update, commits partially or repeats an effect

Observation
Outcomes of concurrent and retried runs, plus the transaction boundaries read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The transaction boundary and the isolation level, which every write path conforms to

[Transaction Boundary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-transaction-boundary), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [All-or-Nothing State Change](LEXICON.md#lexicon-all-or-nothing-state-change)

### ACID

- Kind: [model](SCHEMA.md#kind-model)
- Category: [Transactions / State / Concurrency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-transactions-state-concurrency)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: database, transaction
- Aliases: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
- Layer: [Atomic Boundary](SCHEMA.md#layer-atomic-boundary)

Details

Definition
A conceptual representation of the four guarantees of a database transaction: atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.

Requires
[Atomicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-atomicity), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Isolation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-isolation), [Durability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-durability)

Reinforces
[Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness)

Enables
[Strong Transactional Guarantees](LEXICON.md#lexicon-strong-transactional-guarantees)

In tension with
[Distributed Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-distributed-availability), [BASE/Eventual Consistency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-base-eventual-consistency)

Conflicts with
none

Tensions
[ACID / Distributed Availability](SCHEMA.md#tension-acid-distributed-availability), [ACID / BASE/Eventual Consistency](SCHEMA.md#tension-acid-base-eventual-consistency)

Distinct from
[BASE/Eventual Consistency](LEXICON.md#lexicon-base-eventual-consistency): ACID keeps each transaction atomic, consistent, isolated and durable, while BASE favors availability and lets replicas converge later.

Violated by
[Partial Commit](LEXICON.md#lexicon-partial-commit)

Detected by
non-transactional multi-write invariants

Measured by
transactional invariant defects

Refactored by
[Introduce Transaction Boundary](LEXICON.md#lexicon-introduce-transaction-boundary), [Invariant Check](LEXICON.md#lexicon-invariant-check)

Enforced by
DB transactions, isolation tests

Before

```typescript
await fooDb.write(foo);
await barDb.write(bar);
```

After

```typescript
await database.transaction({ isolation: "serializable" }, async (tx) => {
  await tx.foos.save(foo);
  await tx.bars.save(bar);
  assertInvariant(foo, bar);
});
```

DB transactions, isolation tests

Every multi-step write, shared mutable state and retried side effect

A verdict stands until the write path, the isolation level or the concurrency model changes

Refusal

Observation
Outcomes of concurrent and retried runs, plus the transaction boundaries read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The transaction boundary and the isolation level, which every write path conforms to

[Atomicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-atomicity), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Isolation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-isolation), [Durability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-durability), [Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness), [Strong Transactional Guarantees](LEXICON.md#lexicon-strong-transactional-guarantees)

### Transaction Boundary

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [Transactions / State / Concurrency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-transactions-state-concurrency)
- Severity: [mandatory](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-mandatory)
- Scope: unit of work, aggregate, service
- Layer: [Atomic Boundary](SCHEMA.md#layer-atomic-boundary)

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that a transaction covers exactly the writes of one unit of work inside one service.

Requires
[Consistency Rules](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consistency-rules)

Reinforces
[Atomicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-atomicity), [Unit of Work Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-unit-of-work-pattern)

Enables
[Safe State Mutation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-safe-state-mutation)

In tension with
[Large Transaction Scope](LEXICON.md#lexicon-large-transaction-scope)

Conflicts with
[Hidden Distributed Transaction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-distributed-transaction)

Referenced by
[Atomicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-atomicity), [Unit of Work Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-unit-of-work-pattern)

Contracts
[Transaction Boundary](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-transaction-boundary)

Tensions
[Transaction Boundary / Large Transaction Scope](SCHEMA.md#tension-large-transaction-scope-transaction-boundary)

Distinct from
[Consistency Rules](LEXICON.md#lexicon-consistency-rules): A transaction boundary fixes which writes one transaction covers, while consistency rules are the invariants it must keep inside that scope.

Violated by
[Hidden Distributed Transaction](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hidden-distributed-transaction)

Detected by
transaction scope leakage

Measured by
transaction size/duration

Refactored by
[Restrict Exports](LEXICON.md#lexicon-restrict-exports), [Saga Pattern](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-saga-pattern)

Enforced by
transaction policy

Before

```typescript
await beginTransaction();
await controller.parse(request);
await service.validate(foo);
await repository.save(foo);
await commitTransaction();
```

After

```typescript
async function createFoo(input: CreateFoo) {
  const foo = validateFoo(input);
  return database.transaction((tx) => new FooRepository(tx).save(foo));
}
```

### Unit of Work Pattern

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Transactions / State / Concurrency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-transactions-state-concurrency)
- Severity: [recommended](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-recommended)
- Scope: application service, persistence
- Aliases: Unit of Work
- Layer: [Atomic Boundary](SCHEMA.md#layer-atomic-boundary)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that collects the changes of one use case and commits them together in a single transaction.

Requires
[Transaction Boundary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-transaction-boundary)

Reinforces
[Atomicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-atomicity), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency)

Enables
[Coordinated Persistence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordinated-persistence)

In tension with
[Repository Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-repository-complexity)

Conflicts with
[Scattered Save Calls](LEXICON.md#lexicon-scattered-save-calls)

Referenced by
[Transaction Boundary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-transaction-boundary)

Tensions
[Unit of Work Pattern / Repository Complexity](SCHEMA.md#tension-repository-complexity-unit-of-work-pattern)

Violated by
[Scattered Save Calls](LEXICON.md#lexicon-scattered-save-calls)

Detected by
multiple independent saves in one use case

Measured by
save coordination defects

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
persistence conventions

Before

```typescript
await fooRepository.save(foo);
await barRepository.save(bar);
await eventRepository.save(event);
```

After

```typescript
const uow = unitOfWork.begin();
uow.foos.save(foo);
uow.bars.save(bar);
uow.events.append(event);
await uow.commit();
```

How it is checked

Checked by
persistence conventions

Population
Every multi-step write, shared mutable state and retried side effect

Freshness
A verdict stands until the write path, the isolation level or the concurrency model changes

Refusal
The transaction or concurrency test fails a write path that loses an update, commits partially or repeats an effect

Observation
Outcomes of concurrent and retried runs, plus the transaction boundaries read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The transaction boundary and the isolation level, which every write path conforms to

Depends on
[Transaction Boundary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-transaction-boundary), [Atomicity](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-atomicity), [Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-consistency), [Coordinated Persistence](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordinated-persistence)

Definition

Distinct from
[Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness): Consistency is stored data satisfying its invariants, while correctness is code behavior matching its specification.

Distinct from
[Fault Tolerance](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fault-tolerance): Consistency is data keeping its invariants, while fault tolerance is operation continuing through component failure.

Distinct from
[Interoperability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-interoperability): Consistency is data inside one system keeping its invariants, while interoperability is separate systems exchanging data.

Distinct from
[Always-Fresh Reads](LEXICON.md#lexicon-always-fresh-reads): Consistency is invariants holding after every change, while always-fresh reads is every read seeing the latest write.

Distinct from
[Availability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-availability): Consistency is data keeping its invariants, while availability is the system answering at all.

Distinct from
[Durability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-durability): Consistency is invariants holding after a change, while durability is a committed change surviving a crash.

Distinct from
[Maintainability](LEXICON.md#lexicon-maintainability): Consistency is a property of stored data, while maintainability is a property of the code that changes it.

Distinct from
[Scalability](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-scalability): Consistency is invariants holding, while scalability is performance holding as load grows.

Distinct from
[Operational Complexity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-operational-complexity): Consistency is invariants holding, while operational complexity is the effort of running the system in production.

Distinct from
[Quality](LEXICON.md#lexicon-quality): Consistency is one property of stored data, while quality is how far a system meets all its expectations.

Distinct from
[Security](LEXICON.md#lexicon-security): Consistency is data keeping its invariants, while security is protection from misuse and attack.

Distinct from
[Simplicity](LEXICON.md#lexicon-simplicity): Consistency is invariants holding, while simplicity is the absence of unneeded structure.

```typescript
foo.total = foo.items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.value, 0);
foo.itemCount = externalCount;
```

Details

Definition
A rule or precondition that concurrent transactions do not see each other's uncommitted changes, to the degree the isolation level declares.

Requires

Reinforces
[Correctness](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-correctness)

Before

```typescript
const foo = await fooStore.find(id);
foo.count += 1;
await fooStore.save(foo);
```

After

```typescript
await database.transaction({ isolation: "serializable" }, async (tx) => {
  const foo = await tx.foos.lock(id);
  await tx.foos.save({ ...foo, count: foo.count + 1 });
});
```

```typescript
const foo = await fooStore.find(id);
```

### Optimistic Locking

- Kind: [pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-pattern)
- Category: [Transactions / State / Concurrency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-category-transactions-state-concurrency)
- Severity: [contextual](SCHEMA.md#vocabulary-severity-contextual)
- Scope: persistence, transaction
- Aliases: Own-Span Compare-and-Swap
- Layer: [Atomic Boundary](SCHEMA.md#layer-atomic-boundary)

Details

Definition
A design pattern that checks a record's version when it is written and rejects the write if another writer changed it first, comparing only the writer's own span where a surface is fenced per writer.

Requires
[Version Field](LEXICON.md#lexicon-version-field)

Reinforces
[Concurrency Control](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-concurrency-control)

Enables
[Conflict Detection](LEXICON.md#lexicon-conflict-detection)

Violated by
[Lost Update](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-lost-update)

Detected by
updates without version check

Measured by
conflict/retry rate

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
repository rules, integration tests

Before

```typescript
await fooTable.update({ id: foo.id, name: foo.name });
```

After

```typescript
const updated = await fooTable.update({
  id: foo.id,
  expectedVersion: foo.version,
  next: { ...foo, version: foo.version + 1 },
});
if (!updated) throw new ConflictError(foo.id);
```

repository rules, integration tests

### State Isolation

- Kind: [principle](SCHEMA.md#kind-principle)

Definition

Refactored by

Before

```typescript
const globalFooState: Foo[] = [];
function addFoo(foo: Foo) {
  globalFooState.push(foo);
}
```

After

```typescript
class FooSession {
  #state: Foo[] = [];
  add(foo: Foo) {
    this.#state = [...this.#state, foo];
  }
  snapshot() {
    return [...this.#state];
  }
}
```

Before

```typescript
function calculateFoo(foo: Foo) {
  foo.count += 1;
  fooLog.record(foo);
  fooDb.save(foo);
  return foo.count;
}
```

After

```typescript
function nextFoo(foo: Foo): Foo {
  return { ...foo, count: foo.count + 1 };
}
async function applyFoo(foo: Foo, store: FooStore, log: Log) {
  const next = nextFoo(foo);
  log.write(next);
  await store.save(next);
  return next;
}
```

Details

Definition
A conceptual representation of concurrent flow as places holding tokens and transitions that consume and produce them, which can be analyzed for deadlock.

Requires
[Places and Transitions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-places-and-transitions)

Reinforces
[Concurrency Correctness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concurrency-correctness), [Deadlock Freedom](LEXICON.md#lexicon-deadlock-freedom)

Enables
[Concurrent-Flow Modeling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concurrent-flow-modeling), [Reachability and Deadlock Analysis](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reachability-and-deadlock-analysis)

In tension with
[Modeling Overhead](LEXICON.md#lexicon-modeling-overhead)

Conflicts with
[Ad-Hoc Lock Ordering](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ad-hoc-lock-ordering)

Contracts
[Petri Nets](ALGORITHMS.md#algorithms-petri-nets)

Tensions
[Petri Nets / Modeling Overhead](SCHEMA.md#tension-modeling-overhead-petri-nets)

Violated by
[Ad-Hoc Lock Ordering](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ad-hoc-lock-ordering)

Detected by
deadlocks or lost tokens found only at runtime

Measured by
unreachable or deadlock-prone markings

Refactored by
none

Enforced by
concurrency model review

Before

```typescript
acquire(a);
acquire(b);
work();
release(b);
release(a);
```

After

```typescript
const net = petriNet({
  places: { idle: 1, aHeld: 0, bHeld: 0 },
  transitions: [
    { name: "takeA", consume: { idle: 1 }, produce: { aHeld: 1 } },
    { name: "takeB", consume: { aHeld: 1 }, produce: { bHeld: 1 } },
  ],
});
assertNoDeadlock(reachableMarkings(net));
```

How it is checked

Checked by
concurrency model review

Population
Every multi-step write, shared mutable state and retried side effect

Freshness
A verdict stands until the write path, the isolation level or the concurrency model changes

Refusal
The transaction or concurrency test fails a write path that loses an update, commits partially or repeats an effect

Observation
Outcomes of concurrent and retried runs, plus the transaction boundaries read from source

Evidence
None, because the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it

Authoritative side
The transaction boundary and the isolation level, which every write path conforms to

Depends on
[Places and Transitions](LEXICON.md#lexicon-places-and-transitions), [Concurrency Correctness](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concurrency-correctness), [Deadlock Freedom](LEXICON.md#lexicon-deadlock-freedom), [Concurrent-Flow Modeling](LEXICON.md#lexicon-concurrent-flow-modeling), [Reachability and Deadlock Analysis](LEXICON.md#lexicon-reachability-and-deadlock-analysis)

Shape it refuses
[Ad-Hoc Lock Ordering](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ad-hoc-lock-ordering)
